title: CommandRunner Component
body:
Many users of Tapir are familiar and comfortable with the Python language. The `Handshake_Component` already provides an interface to access the python package directly from Grasshopper. For the ones who are not comfortable with getting their hands dirty, we can create the `CommandRunner` component - which provides grasshopper style access to the python package.

* The component can have a drop down list with the commands available.
* The user can select the command that needs to be accessed.
* This creates / removes the inputs of the component. (Some commands need parameters, some don't)
* As soon as the `Execute` button is pressed, the command is executed.

title: python scripts by KAA DESIGN
body:
https://github.com/KAA-MB/archicad-python-scripts-KAA

I'd love to help incorporate some of the script logic / features into Tapir in the future!  Here are descriptions of the scripts included:

ZONE NUMBERING BY DISTANCE FROM FIRST
•	Numbers Zones sequentially starting from "First Zone" (a custom property), and proceeding by closest distance from this first zone. If there's a selection, the script uses only selected zones; otherwise it uses all zones in project. Numbering series is unique per story level (e.g. 101, 102 for 1st floor; 201, 202 for 2nd floor).

ZONE NUMBERING BY DISTANCE FROM PREVIOUS
•	Numbers Zones sequentially starting from "First Zone" (a custom property), and proceeding by closest distance from the previous zone numbered. If there's a selection, the script uses only selected zones; otherwise it uses all zones in project. 

ZONE DIMENSIONS
•	Measures each Zone's length and width dimensions (feet-inches) based on Bounding Box, and writes it to a custom property. We use a Zone Label to display these dimensions in plan. The script takes a custom property called "Zone Angle" (user input) in order to calculate the dimensions correctly for rotated zones. We did not find a way to pull the rotation angle automatically, so it defaults to 0 degrees and is filled in by the user if different. The math formula breaks at 45 degrees (a compromise, since to fix this would require another user input). If there's a selection, the script uses only selected zones; otherwise it uses all zones in project. 

ATTRIBUTES - create folders and sort attributes into folders (layers example)
•	Creates attribute folders, and sorts attributes into the folders according to our firm’s naming convention. If folders have already been created, it moves all attributes into a temporary “dummy” folder, removes other folders and proceeds with creating/sorting (then erases dummy folder). Attributes not matching the naming convention are placed in a folder called “Audit Non-compliant”.  *script is broken in AC27 due to changes in JSON commands (need help fixing)

ATTRIBUTES - audit names (layers example)
•	Audits attribute names according to our firm’s naming convention, and prints a list of “non-compliant” attributes. 

INTERIOR DOORS - number sequentially
•	Numbers interior Doors sequentially starting from "First Door” (a custom property), and proceeding by closest distance from this first door. The script relies on correct Classification as Door, and uses the built-in property for Position: Interior. If there's a selection, the script uses only selected doors; otherwise it uses all doors in project. Numbering series is unique per story level (e.g. 101, 102 for 1st floor; 201, 202 for 2nd floor).

INTERIOR DOORS - number by zone
•	Numbers interior Doors based on associated Zone’s number + letter of alphabet (e.g. 101a, 101b). The script uses the built-in property for Position: Interior. If there's a selection, the script uses only selected doors; otherwise it uses all doors in project. Ideally this script would also have logic to move clockwise around each zone so the a, b, c sequence is more logical.

EXTERIOR DOORS/WINDOWS
•	Numbers interior Doors and Windows sequentially starting from "First Door” or “First Window” (a custom property), and proceeding clockwise around the building. The script relies on correct Classification as Door or Window, built-in property Position: Exterior, and also takes several custom properties. The clockwise direction is controlled by custom property “Exterior Side” to identify Top, Right, Bottom, Left position in plan (cardinal directions were more error prone since people get confused. Numbering series is unique per “Story Level” (e.g. 101, 102 for 1st floor; 201, 202 for 2nd floor) - we decided to make this a custom property also in order to have more control over numbering of clerestories, since “z bands” didn’t produce reliable results. The “Building Number” custom property defaults to 1, and if the site has multiple buildings the user can identify unique numbers for each (though the numbering starts at 101 for any building, the building’s number doesn’t become part of door/window’s number). This part of the script breaks right now if Building Numbers are not sequential - needs fixing.

title: Proposal: CLAUDE.md + AI contributor guidelines for the Add-On
body:
Hi @tlorantfy,

I saw you mentioned on Discord that you're planning to add a `CLAUDE.md` to the repo and define a template prompt for generating GH nodes for new commands. I'd love to help with that — having submitted a few PRs now, I've collected some patterns from your reviews that would be useful to codify.

**What I have so far** (from your review feedback on my PRs):

- Error handling: always use `CreateErrorResponse(code, "msg")`, never manual `ObjectState` construction
- Schema references: shared types go in `CommonSchemaDefinitions.json` via `$ref`, not inline
- Enums: string fields with known values → `"enum": [...]` in the schema
- Types: use native types directly (`short` for `floorIndex`), avoid unnecessary `static_cast`
- Error messages: no error codes in the string — they come automatically via `ErrorItem`
- PR scope: one feature per PR, no cross-branch registrations
- Schema patterns: `FooOrError` following the `ViewSettingsOrError` pattern
- String formatting: `GS::UniString::Printf` (not `ValueToUniString`) for AC25+ compatibility

**Three options I see:**

1. **`CLAUDE.md` only** — Claude Code reads it automatically as project context. Other AI tools can also pick it up. Focused on coding patterns, architecture overview, and do/don'ts.

2. **`CONTRIBUTING.md` with AI section** — Tool-agnostic. A "For AI Contributors" section with the same coding patterns, plus the command template prompt you mentioned.

3. **Both** — `CONTRIBUTING.md` for human + AI general guidelines, `CLAUDE.md` for Claude-specific context (file structure, schema system, command registration pattern, GH node generation template).

I could draft a PR for whichever approach you prefer. I already have a good overview of the codebase architecture (`AddOnMain.cpp` registration, command class hierarchy, `CommonSchemaDefinitions.json` inheritance, the `R"(...)"` schema pattern, etc.).

What would be most useful to you?

title: Feature request: read classification of Building Material / attribute-level classification commands
body:
Currently there's no way to read the classification assigned to a Building Material (or other attributes) via the Tapir/Archicad JSON API. dev_get_classifications_of_elements only works for elements, not attributes, and attributes_get_building_materials / attributes_get_attributes_by_type don't expose classification data either.

Use case: in composite walls/complex profiles measured via "measição por componentes", each skin's Building Material is classified into a BOQ chapter (e.g. via the "Mapa de Quantidades" classification system), so quantities can be automatically routed to the correct chapter per material layer. Right now the only workaround is duplicating the classification into a custom property on the material, which is fragile (easy to get out of sync with the real classification).

Would it be possible to add something like GetClassificationsOfAttributes / SetClassificationsOfAttributes, analogous to the existing element-level commands?
author: dmacielarq-creator

title: A read-only view/layout standards audit built on Tapir, looking for projects to break it
body:
I built a tool on top of Tapir that answers a question Archicad can't:
**which views in this project carry custom settings instead of a named
combination?**

`GetViewSettings` returns an empty string for `layerCombination`,
`penSetName`, `modelViewOptions`, `dimensionStyle` or
`graphicOverrideCombination` when a view has custom settings rather than a
named one. That empty string is the mechanism behind office standards
quietly failing to propagate. Those views don't follow when the standard
changes, and there's no way to list them from inside Archicad.

So it lists them. It also reports duplicate sheet numbers, sheets with no
number, layouts sitting outside any subset, and layouts with no drawings on
them (that last one comes free from the Layout Book tree, since a
LayoutItem's children *are* its drawings, so no element query is needed).

On the stock Hillside House sample: 172 views, 38 layouts, 4 views on custom
layer combinations, 97.7% consistency.

**What I'm asking for.** It has only ever run against Hillside House and the
generic template. That's a terrible sample. I'd like a handful of people to
run it on real projects and tell me where it's wrong: miscounts, crashes,
things it claims that aren't true, structures it doesn't understand.

It's a single .exe, needs no Python, and:

- reads only, never writes to the project
- makes no network calls at all (127.0.0.1 only)
- writes two files: a full HTML report, and a counts-only summary with no
  project, view or sheet names in it, so you can share results without
  disclosing anything about the job

If you'd like to try it, reply here and I'll send it over. Happy to send the
source instead if you'd rather read it before running it.

A few things I learned building on Tapir that might be useful to others here:

- `GetDocumentRevisions` returned **zero** on a project with 38 layouts. A
  layout only has a revision once it's been issued, so the Layout Book tree
  has to be the source of truth for layouts, not revisions.
- `prefix` is empty on layouts; **`uiId`** carries the layout number.
- Neither layout names nor numbers are unique. Hillside House has 38 layouts,
  26 distinct names, 34 distinct numbers.
- `GetNavigatorItemTree` has no declared output schema. The real shape is
  `{"navigatorItemTree": {...}}` with each child wrapped in
  `{"navigatorItem": ...}`, and there's no `rootItem`.

Thanks for Tapir. None of this would exist without it.

title: FilterElements: add layer, story and element type filters
body:
`FilterElements` only accepts Archicad's flag filters (`IsEditable`, `OnActualFloor`, …), so scripts that need "all walls on story 2 on layer X" must fetch everything and filter client-side.

- Add optional inputs to `FilterElementsCommand` (`archicad-addon/Sources/ElementCommands.cpp`, ~line 3990): `layerIndices` (array of int), `floorIndices` (array of int), `elementTypes` (array of the existing element type enum from `SchemaDefinitions.cpp`).
- An element passes when it matches all given criteria (each array is OR within itself). Read `elem.header.layer`, `elem.header.floorInd`, and the type via the existing helpers in `CommandBase`.
- Fully backward compatible: omitted inputs mean no filtering.
- Extend `archicad-addon/Examples/filter_elements.py` (or the existing filter example) and the Grasshopper `FilterElementsComponent.cs` with the new optional inputs.

Related: #108 was closed as covered by `FilterElements`, but its flag filters (`IsEditable`, `OnActualFloor`, …) cannot select by a given layer, story or element type, which is what this asks for.

title: Add command to activate a layer combination
body:
You can create layer combinations (`CreateLayerCombinations`) and list them (`GetLayerCombinations`) but cannot apply one to the current view.

- Add `ActivateLayerCombinationCommand` in `archicad-addon/Sources/AttributeCommands.cpp/.hpp`.
- Input: `attributeId` (the layer combination's attribute guid, same shape as other attribute commands).
- Implementation: `ACAPI_Attribute_Get` the `API_LayerCombID`, then apply it (`ACAPI_Environment` / `ACAPI_Navigator` layer-combination change call available in the DevKit — check `archicad-addon/Build/DevKits/AC29/Support` headers). Guard API differences per `AC_VERSION` as done elsewhere.
- Register in the Attribute group in `AddOnMain.cpp`, add an example and a Grasshopper component next to `SetLayerCombinationsComponent.cs`.
