title: Add ModifyCurtainWalls command
body:
Curtain walls can be created (`CreateCurtainWalls`) and read (`GetDetailsOfElements`), but not modified: there is no `ModifyCurtainWalls`, and `SetDetailsOfElements` has no curtain wall branch. Changing an existing curtain wall's height or grid means deleting and recreating it, which loses its GUID, properties and classifications.

- Add `ModifyCurtainWallsCommand` following `ModifySlabsCommand` (`archicad-addon/Sources/ExtendedElementCommands.cpp/.hpp`, `Execute` ~line 6062).
- Modifiable fields: the ones `CreateCurtainWalls` accepts (`archicad-addon/Sources/ElementCreationCommands.cpp`, schema ~line 2814): `height`, `zCoordinate`/`floorIndex`, `primaryPattern`, `secondaryPattern`, and `coordinates` (reference line) if `ACAPI_Element_Change` supports it for curtain walls. Use the same field names and value shapes as the curtain wall branch of `GetDetailsOfElements` (`archicad-addon/Sources/ElementCommands.cpp`, ~line 1373) so read → modify round-trips. Fields the API cannot change should fail the item with a clear message rather than be silently ignored.
- Register in `AddOnMain.cpp` with the other Modify commands (after `ModifyLabelsCommand`), version from `tools/package_info.json`.
- Add `archicad-addon/Examples/modify_curtain_walls.py` (following `create_curtain_walls.py`) and a Grasshopper `ModifyCurtainWallsComponent.cs` next to `ModifySlabsComponent.cs`.
author: parikshit99

title: Add UngroupElements command
body:
Groups can be created (`CreateGroups`) and read (`GetGroupsOfElements`, `GetElementsOfGroups`), but there is no way to ungroup, so a script that groups elements cannot undo or rebuild its grouping.

- Add `UngroupElementsCommand` in `archicad-addon/Sources/ElementGroupingCommands.cpp/.hpp`, next to `CreateGroupsCommand` (~line 72).
- Input: `groups` — array of group ids, as returned by `GetGroupsOfElements`. Ungroup one level, like Archicad's Edit > Grouping > Ungroup.
- Implementation: get the group's elements with `ACAPI_Grouping_GetGroupedElems` and call `ACAPI_Grouping_Tool (guids, APITool_Ungroup, nullptr)` inside `ACAPI_CallUndoableCommand`, like `LockElementsCommand::Execute` (`archicad-addon/Sources/ElementCommands.cpp`, ~line 4846). Check the `APITool_Ungroup` behaviour in the DevKit headers and guard version differences per `AC_VERSION` as `SetSuspendGroupsModeCommand` does.
- Response: execution results per group.
- Register in `AddOnMain.cpp` next to `CreateGroupsCommand`, version from `tools/package_info.json`. Extend `archicad-addon/Examples/create_groups.py` to ungroup at the end, and add a Grasshopper `UngroupElementsComponent.cs` next to `CreateGroupsComponent.cs`.
author: parikshit99

title: Add CreateLibraryParts command: create GDL objects from scripts and parameters
body:
Tapir can read and set GDL parameters of placed objects, add files to the embedded library and list library parts, but it cannot create a library part. Scripts that generate parametric objects (MEP symbols, switchboards, sanitary fittings, office-standard objects) have to go through the GDL editor by hand.

The DevKit has the full API for this (AC29 `ACAPI_LibraryPart.h`): `ACAPI_LibraryPart_Create`, `ACAPI_LibraryPart_NewSection` / `AddSection` / `EndSection`, `ACAPI_LibraryPart_SetDetails_ParamDef` and `ACAPI_LibraryPart_Save`. The DevKit's `LibPart_Test` example shows the whole sequence.

- Add `CreateLibraryPartsCommand` in `archicad-addon/Sources/LibraryCommands.cpp/.hpp`.
- Input: `libraryParts` — array of `{ name, parentId (subtype, e.g. Object / Lamp / Label, as the library part unique ID or GUID), masterScript, script2D, script3D, parameterScript, uiScript, propertiesScript (all optional strings), parameters [{ name, type (Length, Angle, RealNum, Integer, Boolean, String, Material, FillPattern, LineType, PenColor), value, description, isHidden? }], overwriteExisting (bool, optional) }`. Only `name` and `parentId` are required.
- Save into the embedded library: see how `AddFilesToEmbeddedLibraryCommand::Execute` (`LibraryCommands.cpp`, ~line 54) finds it. Respond per item with the new part's `name`, `unId` and `guid`, or an execution error, and reload so the part is placeable right away.
- Guard API differences per `AC_VERSION` (AC25–AC30) as done elsewhere.
- Register in the Library group in `AddOnMain.cpp` next to `AddFilesToEmbeddedLibraryCommand`, with the version from `tools/package_info.json`. Add `archicad-addon/Examples/create_library_parts.py` that creates a simple box object with a length parameter and places it with `CreateObjects`, plus a Grasshopper `CreateLibraryPartsComponent.cs` in `grasshopper-plugin/TapirGrasshopperPlugin/Components/LibraryComponents/`.
- If this is too large for one PR, splitting it is fine: first the command with scripts and parameters, then the Grasshopper component.
author: parikshit99

title: Add rendering commands: list scenes, set the current scene, photo render to a file
body:
Tapir has no rendering commands. Scripts can save the current window as an image (`SaveCurrentWindowAsImage`) but cannot produce a photorealistic rendering, which blocks batch render workflows (render every saved 3D view, render design options for comparison).

The DevKit (AC29 `ACAPI_Rendering.h`) provides `ACAPI_Rendering_GetRenderingSceneNames`, `ACAPI_Rendering_SetCurrentRenderingScene` and `ACAPI_Rendering_PhotoRender (const API_PhotoRenderPars*, const API_PrintPars*)`.

- `GetRenderingScenes`: returns the scene names and the current one.
- `SetCurrentRenderingScene`: input `sceneName`.
- `PhotoRender`: input `outputPath`, optional `sceneName`, and optional image format and size where `API_PhotoRenderPars` allows them. It renders the current 3D view and saves the file, with an execution result. Follow `SaveCurrentWindowAsImage` (`archicad-addon/Sources/ProjectCommands.cpp`, ~line 1615) for output path handling and format names.
- Put them in a new `RenderingCommands.cpp/.hpp` (or `ProjectCommands`), register them in `AddOnMain.cpp` next to `SaveCurrentWindowAsImageCommand` with the version from `tools/package_info.json`, and guard per `AC_VERSION` where the API differs.
- Add `archicad-addon/Examples/photo_render.py` and Grasshopper components next to `SaveCurrentWindowAsImageComponent.cs`.
author: parikshit99

title: Add 3D style commands and show selection / all in 3D
body:
Tapir covers 3D cutting planes and 3D projection settings, but not 3D styles. A script also cannot open the 3D window on a set of elements, as Archicad's "Show Selection/Marquee in 3D" does.

The DevKit (AC29 `ACAPI_View.h`) provides `ACAPI_View_Get3DStyleList (GS::Array<GS::UniString>* styles, GS::UniString* current)`, `ACAPI_View_SetCurrent3DStyle`, `ACAPI_View_ShowSelectionIn3D ()` and `ACAPI_View_ShowAllIn3D ()`.

- `Get3DStyles`: returns the 3D style names and the current one.
- `SetCurrent3DStyle`: input `name`.
- `ShowElementsIn3D`: input optional `elements`. Select them (as `ChangeSelectionOfElements` does), then call `ShowSelectionIn3D`. With no elements, call `ShowAllIn3D`.
- Add them to `archicad-addon/Sources/3DProjectionCommands.cpp/.hpp` next to `Set3DProjectionSettingsCommand` (~line 108), register them next to it in `AddOnMain.cpp` with the version from `tools/package_info.json`, and guard per `AC_VERSION` where a function is missing in older DevKits.
- Extend `archicad-addon/Examples/get_and_set_3d_projection_settings.py` (or add `3d_styles.py`) and add Grasshopper components next to `Set3DProjectionSettingsComponent.cs`.
author: parikshit99

title: Add HideElements / ShowAllHiddenElements commands
body:
Scripts can highlight elements (`HighlightElements`) and zoom to them (`FitInWindow`), but cannot hide elements in the current view, as Archicad's View > Hide / Show All Hidden Elements does. Isolating the elements a script works on, or clearing clutter before `SaveCurrentWindowAsImage`, is not possible.

The DevKit (AC29 `ACAPI_View.h`) provides `ACAPI_View_ChangeShowHideState (bool* toShow)` and `ACAPI_View_GetShowHideState (bool* isShown)`. They act on the current selection, so the command selects the given elements first (as `ChangeSelectionOfElements` does) and restores the previous selection afterwards.

- `HideElements`: input `elements`. Hides them in the current window.
- `ShowAllHiddenElements`: no input. Shows every hidden element.
- Check the exact semantics of `toShow` in the DevKit docs, and guard per `AC_VERSION` if the functions are missing in older DevKits.
- Add both in `archicad-addon/Sources/NavigatorCommands.cpp/.hpp` next to `FitInWindowCommand` (~line 879) and register them next to it in `AddOnMain.cpp` with the version from `tools/package_info.json`. Add `archicad-addon/Examples/hide_and_show_elements.py` and Grasshopper components in `NavigatorComponents/`.

Related: open PR #833 adds `ZoomToBox`. This issue is only about hiding and showing.
author: parikshit99

title: Add renovation filter commands: list filters, get and set the active one
body:
`SetViewSettings` can set a saved view's renovation filter, but a script cannot list the project's renovation filters or switch the filter of the current window (Document > Renovation > Renovation Filter). This blocks scripted existing/demolition/new-construction output.

The DevKit (AC29 `ACAPI_Renovation.h`) provides `ACAPI_Renovation_GetRenovationFilters (GS::Array<API_Guid>*)`, `ACAPI_Renovation_GetRenovationFilterName`, `ACAPI_Renovation_GetActualRenovationFilter` and `ACAPI_Renovation_SetActualRenovationFilter`.

- `GetRenovationFilters`: returns `{ renovationFilterId (guid), name }` for each filter, plus the active one.
- `SetActiveRenovationFilter`: input `renovationFilterId` (or `name`). Sets the filter of the current window.
- Use the same guid format as the `renovationFilterGuid` field `GetViewSettings` reports (`archicad-addon/Sources/NavigatorCommands.cpp`, ~line 427) so the outputs can be fed into `SetViewSettings`.
- Add them in `NavigatorCommands.cpp/.hpp`, register them next to `GetViewSettingsCommand` in `AddOnMain.cpp` with the version from `tools/package_info.json`, and guard per `AC_VERSION` if needed. Add `archicad-addon/Examples/renovation_filters.py` and Grasshopper components next to `GetViewSettingsComponent.cs`.

Related: open PR #837 reads the renovation filter name of views.
author: parikshit99

title: Hotlinks: break and delete hotlink nodes, report missing sources
body:
Tapir can create, place, change and update hotlinks (`CreateHotlinkNodes`, `CreateHotlinkInstances`, `ChangeHotlinkNodes`, `UpdateHotlinks`), but cannot remove them or tell whether a source file is missing. Cleaning up a project's Hotlink Manager still has to be done by hand.

The DevKit (AC29 `ACAPI_Hotlink.h`) provides `ACAPI_Hotlink_BreakHotlinkNode (const API_Guid*)`, `ACAPI_Hotlink_DeleteHotlinkNode (const API_Guid*)` and `ACAPI_Hotlink_GetHotlinkSourceStatus (const IO::Location*, API_HotlinkSourceStatus*)`.

- `BreakHotlinkNodes`: input `hotlinkNodes` — array of node ids, as `GetHotlinks` returns them. Breaks each node, so its instances become regular elements. Returns execution results.
- `DeleteHotlinkNodes`: same input. Deletes each node together with its instances.
- Add a `sourceStatus` field (e.g. `Available`, `Missing`, as `API_HotlinkSourceStatus` defines) to each node in `GetHotlinks` (`archicad-addon/Sources/ProjectCommands.cpp`, `GetHotlinksCommand::Execute` ~line 671).
- Implement the two commands next to `ChangeHotlinkNodesCommand` (`ProjectCommands.cpp`, ~line 3159), inside `ACAPI_CallUndoableCommand`, and register them next to it in `AddOnMain.cpp` with the version from `tools/package_info.json`. Guard per `AC_VERSION` if needed.
- Extend `archicad-addon/Examples/update_hotlinks.py` (or add `break_and_delete_hotlinks.py`) and add Grasshopper components next to `ChangeHotlinkNodesComponent.cs`.
author: parikshit99

title: Add attribute folder commands: create, rename, delete, move attributes into folders
body:
Tapir creates, reads and deletes attributes, but always in the root folder. Templates maintained by script cannot organise layers, surfaces, building materials, composites etc. into attribute folders, so every scripted template ends up flat.

The DevKit (AC29 `ACAPI_Attribute.h`) provides `ACAPI_Attribute_CreateFolder (API_AttributeFolder&)`, `ACAPI_Attribute_RenameFolder`, `ACAPI_Attribute_DeleteFolder` and `ACAPI_Attribute_Move (folders, attributes, targetFolder)`. The folder API exists from Archicad 26 and is missing in the AC25 DevKit, so guard per `AC_VERSION` and fail with a clear message on AC25.

- `CreateAttributeFolders`: input `attributeFolders` — array of `{ attributeType, path (array of folder names) }`.
- `RenameAttributeFolders` / `DeleteAttributeFolders`: identify a folder by `attributeType` + `path`.
- `MoveAttributesAndFolders`: input `attributeIds`, optional `folders`, and a `targetFolder` (type + path).
- Return execution results per item. Optionally add each attribute's folder path to `GetAttributesByType` (`archicad-addon/Sources/AttributeCommands.cpp`, ~line 128).
- Implement in `AttributeCommands.cpp/.hpp` next to `DeleteAttributesCommand` (~line 2638) and register in the Attribute group of `AddOnMain.cpp` with the version from `tools/package_info.json`. Add `archicad-addon/Examples/attribute_folders.py` and Grasshopper components next to `DeleteAttributesComponent.cs`.
author: parikshit99

title: Teamwork: get element reservation owners, grant elements, project and connection info
body:
For elements, Tapir only learns who holds a reservation as the `conflicts` of a failed `ReserveElements`. A script cannot ask who has an element reserved without trying to take it, cannot hand elements to a colleague, and cannot check whether it runs in an online Teamwork project.

The DevKit (AC29 `ACAPI_Teamwork.h`) provides `ACAPI_Teamwork_GetLockableStatus` (already used for object sets in `GetLockableObjectSetStatusCommand`), `ACAPI_Teamwork_GrantElements (const GS::Array<API_Guid>&, short toUserId)`, `ACAPI_Teamwork_IsOnline ()` and `ACAPI_Teamwork_GetTeamworkProjectDetails`.

- `GetReservationStatusOfElements`: input `elements`. Returns per element `{ status (Free, Editable, Locked, NotAvailable…), user { userId, userName } }`, with names from `ACAPI_Teamwork_GetUsernameFromId` as `ReserveElementsCommand` does. Check that `GetLockableStatus` accepts element guids; if not, use the API the DevKit documents for element ownership.
- `GrantElements`: input `elements` and `userId` (or `userName`). Returns execution results.
- `GetTeamworkProjectInfo`: returns `isTeamwork`, `isOnline`, `serverUrl`, `projectName`, `userName`.
- Implement in `archicad-addon/Sources/TeamworkCommands.cpp/.hpp`, following `ReserveElementsCommand::Execute` (~line 132) and `GetLockableObjectSetStatusCommand::Execute` (~line 450). Register in the Teamwork group of `AddOnMain.cpp` with the version from `tools/package_info.json`, and guard per `AC_VERSION` (the API names differ before AC28, see the existing `#ifdef ServerMainVers_2800` blocks).
- Extend `archicad-addon/Examples/test_teamwork_commands.py` and add Grasshopper components in `TeamworkComponents/`.
author: parikshit99

title: Add NewProject command
body:
Tapir can open, save and close projects (`OpenProject`, `SaveProject`, `CloseProject`), but cannot start a new one. Scripts that set up projects from scratch (batch-create test projects, start a project and populate it from data) still need a manual File > New.

The DevKit (AC29 `ACAPI_Automate.h`) provides `ACAPI_ProjectOperation_NewProject (const API_NewProjectPars*)`. `API_NewProjectPars` only has `newAndReset`. The API takes no template path: the new project uses the template set in Archicad's New Project settings.

- `NewProject`: input optional `newAndReset` (bool, default false), mirroring File > New and New & Reset All. Like `OpenProject`, it discards unsaved changes in the current project, so document that and return a failed execution result if the API refuses (e.g. `APIERR_REFUSEDCMD`).
- Implement it in `archicad-addon/Sources/ProjectCommands.cpp/.hpp` next to `OpenProjectCommand::Execute` (~line 1289) and register it next to `OpenProjectCommand` in `AddOnMain.cpp` with the version from `tools/package_info.json`. It must run outside an undoable command, as `OpenProject` does.
- Add `archicad-addon/Examples/new_project.py` (new project, then `SaveProject` to a path) and a Grasshopper component next to the `OpenProject` one in `ProjectComponents/`.
author: parikshit99

title: Add GetProjectPreferences / SetProjectPreferences (working units, dimensions, zones, reference levels…)
body:
Tapir reads only one page of the project preferences (`GetCalculationUnits`, `APIPrefs_CalcUnitsID`) and writes none. Template setup scripts cannot set working units, dimension precision, zone settings or reference levels, which every office template needs.

The DevKit (AC29 `ACAPI_Environment.h`) provides `ACAPI_ProjectSetting_GetPreferences` and `ACAPI_ProjectSetting_SetPreferences (void* prefs, API_PrefsTypeID)` for `APIPrefs_WorkingUnitsID`, `APIPrefs_DimensionsID`, `APIPrefs_CalcUnitsID`, `APIPrefs_CalcRulesID`, `APIPrefs_ZonesID`, `APIPrefs_ReferenceLevelsID`, `APIPrefs_LayoutsID`, `APIPrefs_LegacyID`, `APIPrefs_ImagingAndCalcID` and `APIPrefs_DataSafetyID`.

- `GetProjectPreferences`: input optional `preferenceTypes` (array of `WorkingUnits`, `Dimensions`, `CalculationUnits`, `CalculationRules`, `Zones`, `ReferenceLevels`, `Layouts`, `Legacy`). Returns each page's fields with readable enum names.
- `SetProjectPreferences`: the same structure, partial. Read the page, change only the given fields, write it back. Return execution results per page.
- Start with `WorkingUnits`, `Dimensions`, `Zones` and `ReferenceLevels`. The others can follow in a later PR if this gets large.
- Reuse the unit name mapping of `GetCalculationUnitsCommand::Execute` (`archicad-addon/Sources/ProjectCommands.cpp`, ~line 2149), and guard per `AC_VERSION` where the structs differ (`MigrationHelper.hpp` maps the old names).
- Register both next to `GetCalculationUnitsCommand` in `AddOnMain.cpp` with the version from `tools/package_info.json`. The preferences dialog is a lockable object set in Teamwork (`PreferencesDialog`, see `ReserveLockableObjectSet`), so say in the description that it must be reserved first. Add `archicad-addon/Examples/project_preferences.py` and Grasshopper components in `ProjectComponents/`.

Project notes (client, project name…) need nothing new: `GetProjectInfo` / `SetProjectInfoField` already cover them.
author: parikshit99

title: Add element link commands: link, unlink and get links between elements
body:
Scripts cannot record their own persistent relations between elements, such as "this label documents that column", "this zone was generated from these walls" or "this object replaces that one". Today they resort to storing GUIDs in properties, which breaks when elements are copied.

The DevKit (AC29 `ACAPI_Element.h`) provides element links, stored in the project: `ACAPI_ElementLink_Link (guidFrom, guidTo, GSFlags linkFlags)`, `ACAPI_ElementLink_Unlink (guidFrom, guidTo)`, `ACAPI_ElementLink_GetLinks (guidFrom, GS::Array<API_Guid>*)` and `ACAPI_ElementLink_GetLinkFlags`.

- `LinkElements`: input `links` — array of `{ fromElementId, toElementId, flags (int, optional) }`.
- `UnlinkElements`: same input, without flags.
- `GetLinksOfElements`: input `elements`. Returns per element `{ links: [{ elementId, flags }] }`.
- Return execution results per item, and run the writes inside `ACAPI_CallUndoableCommand`.
- Implement in `archicad-addon/Sources/ElementCommands.cpp/.hpp` next to `GetRelationsOfElementsCommand`, and register next to it in `AddOnMain.cpp` with the version from `tools/package_info.json`. Check in the DevKit docs how links behave on copy/delete and in Teamwork, and note it in the descriptions.
- Add `archicad-addon/Examples/element_links.py` and Grasshopper components in `ElementsComponents/`.
author: parikshit99

title: Store custom script data in the project and on elements (module data and element user data)
body:
Scripts have nowhere to keep their own state in the project, such as external database ids, sync timestamps or "generated by script X" markers. The usual workaround is creating hidden properties, which shows up in schedules and the UI and pollutes templates.

The DevKit (AC29) has two storage mechanisms that are invisible to users and saved with the project:
- **Project level:** `ACAPI_ModulData_Store`, `ACAPI_ModulData_Get`, `ACAPI_ModulData_GetList` and `ACAPI_ModulData_Delete`, holding named blobs owned by the add-on.
- **Element level:** `ACAPI_Element_SetUserData` / `ACAPI_Element_GetUserData`, one blob per element per add-on.

Suggested commands:
- `SetProjectData` / `GetProjectData` / `DeleteProjectData`: key → string value, with keys mapped to module data names. `GetProjectData` with no keys lists them.
- `SetElementUserData` / `GetElementUserData`: per element a JSON object of key → string. Since there is one blob per element for the whole add-on, store a JSON object and merge on set, so different scripts using different keys don't overwrite each other.
- Return execution results per item. Element writes go inside `ACAPI_CallUndoableCommand`.
- Implement in a new `CustomDataCommands.cpp/.hpp` (or `ProjectCommands` / `ElementCommands`). Register in `AddOnMain.cpp` with the version from `tools/package_info.json`, and add `archicad-addon/Examples/custom_data.py` and Grasshopper components.
- Check and document how the data behaves in Teamwork (send/receive, reservation) and when elements are copied.

Related: draft PR #360 ("Get and set custom user data") implemented element user data with a root key per caller. Its author closed it in February to improve it, and no follow-up came. Reuse its approach where it fits.
author: parikshit99

title: Add element change tracking: capture a state, get new / modified / deleted elements since
body:
Scripts that keep an external copy of the model (Grasshopper, a database, a BIM sync) must re-read every element to find what changed. That is slow on real projects and is the main cost of incremental sync.

The DevKit (AC29 `ACAPI_Element.h`, `APIdefs_ElementDifferenceGenerator.h`) provides `ACAPI_DifferenceGenerator_GetState (type, API_ElemDifferenceGeneratorState*)` and `ACAPI_DifferenceGenerator_GenerateDifference (type, state1, state2, API_ElemDifference&)`. The result is the sets `newElements`, `modifiedElements` and `deletedElements`. Types are `APIDiff_ModificationStampBased`, `APIDiff_3DModelBased` and `APIDiff_ContextBased`.

- `CaptureElementState`: input optional `type` (`ModificationStamp` default, `3DModel`, `Context`). Stores the state in the add-on and returns a `stateId`.
- `GetElementChangesSince`: input `stateId`, optional `toStateId` (default: capture now). Returns `newElements`, `modifiedElements` and `deletedElements` as element id lists.
- `ReleaseElementState`: input `stateId`. Frees a stored state.
- States live in add-on memory and are lost when Archicad restarts or the project is closed. Say so in the descriptions, and make `GetElementChangesSince` fail clearly for an unknown `stateId`.
- Implement in `archicad-addon/Sources/ElementCommands.cpp/.hpp` (or a new file). Register in the Element group of `AddOnMain.cpp` next to `GetAllElementsCommand`, with the version from `tools/package_info.json`. Guard per `AC_VERSION` if the API is missing in older DevKits.
- Add `archicad-addon/Examples/element_changes.py` (capture, create a wall, list changes) and Grasshopper components in `ElementsComponents/`.
author: parikshit99

title: Geometry queries: element at a coordinate, element hotspots, zone area reductions, floor plan cut polygons
body:
Four geometry queries the DevKit offers that Tapir does not expose:

1. **Element at a coordinate:** `ACAPI_Element_SearchElementByCoord (const API_ElemSearchPars*, API_Guid*)`, where `API_ElemSearchPars` is `{ type, filterBits, loc, z }`. Add `GetElementAtCoordinate`: input `{ elementType, coordinate {x,y}, z (optional), filters (optional, same values as FilterElements) }`. Returns the found element id or none. Useful together with `GetPointFromUser`.
2. **Hotspots:** `ACAPI_Element_GetHotspots (guid, GS::Array<API_ElementHotspot>*)`. Add `GetHotspotsOfElements`: input `elements`. Returns each element's hotspot coordinates (x, y, z), so scripts can snap or dimension to real element points.
3. **Zone area reductions:** `ACAPI_Element_RoomReductions (const API_Guid*, RoomReductionPolyProc*)`. Add `GetZoneReductions`: input zone `elements`. Returns per zone the reduction polygons with their percentage and area. Area calculations by local standards need this; `GetQuantitiesOfElements` only gives totals.
4. **Floor plan cut polygons:** `ACAPI_CuttingPlane_GetCutPolygonInfo (bodyIndex, API_Plane3D cutPlane, GS::Array<Geometry::MultiPolygon2D>*, double* area)`. Add `GetCutPolygonsOfElements`: input `elements` and an optional cut height (default: the story's floor plan cut plane). Returns the cut outline polygons and area per element. It needs the element's 3D body indices; see how `Get3DGeometryOfElements` reaches the 3D model.

- Implement in `archicad-addon/Sources/ElementCommands.cpp/.hpp`, next to `GetZoneBoundariesCommand` and `Get3DBoundingBoxesCommand`, and register next to them in `AddOnMain.cpp` with the version from `tools/package_info.json`. Guard per `AC_VERSION` where needed.
- Add an example per command in `archicad-addon/Examples/` and Grasshopper components in `ElementsComponents/`.
- One PR per query is fine; 1–3 are small, 4 is the largest.
author: parikshit99

title: Selection: deselect all, get and set the marquee
body:
`ChangeSelectionOfElements` adds or removes given elements, but clearing the selection means first reading every selected element and passing them all back. Scripts also cannot read or draw a marquee, which `PrintView` already supports as a print area (`"marquee"`).

The DevKit (AC29 `ACAPI_Selection.h`) provides `ACAPI_Selection_DeselectAll ()`, `ACAPI_Selection_Get` (already used for the selection) and `ACAPI_Selection_SetMarquee (API_SelectionInfo*)`, with `marquee` an `API_Region`.

- `DeselectAll`: no input. Clears the selection in the current window.
- `GetMarquee`: returns the current marquee as a polygon (`Coordinate2D` list), its type (rectangle, rotated rectangle, polygon) and `multiStory`, or none.
- `SetMarquee`: input `polygon` (or `box {xMin, yMin, xMax, yMax}`) and optional `multiStory`. An empty input removes the marquee.
- Implement next to `ChangeSelectionOfElementsCommand::Execute` (`archicad-addon/Sources/ElementCommands.cpp`, ~line 2652), register next to it in `AddOnMain.cpp` with the version from `tools/package_info.json`, and guard per `AC_VERSION` where the API differs.
- Extend `archicad-addon/Examples/get_selected_elements.py` (or add `selection_and_marquee.py`) and add Grasshopper components next to `ChangeSelectionComponent.cs`.
author: parikshit99

title: Get and set snap grid and auto-intersect settings
body:
Scripts that set up a project or a working view cannot read or change two common drafting aids: the snap/construction grid (View > Grid & Editing Plane Options) and Auto-Intersection. Auto-Intersection in particular changes the result of scripted wall/beam creation, so scripts need to know its state and be able to switch it.

The DevKit (AC29) provides `ACAPI_Window_GetGridSettings (API_GridType*)` / `ACAPI_Window_ChangeGridSettings (API_GridType*)` and `ACAPI_View_IsAutoIntersectOn (bool*)` / `ACAPI_View_ChangeAutoIntersect (bool*)`. `API_GridType` holds the main and auxiliary spacing and line counts, `gridSwitch`, the grid angle/origin and the snap settings.

- `GetGridSettings` / `SetGridSettings`: the `API_GridType` fields with readable names. Set is partial: read, change the given fields, write back.
- `GetAutoIntersect` / `SetAutoIntersect`: input `isOn`.
- Implement in `archicad-addon/Sources/NavigatorCommands.cpp/.hpp` next to `FitInWindowCommand` (~line 879) or in `ProjectCommands`. Register in `AddOnMain.cpp` with the version from `tools/package_info.json`, and guard per `AC_VERSION` where the API differs.
- Add `archicad-addon/Examples/grid_and_auto_intersect.py` and Grasshopper components.
author: parikshit99

title: Get and set ghost story settings
body:
Scripts that prepare floor plan views or image exports cannot read or set the Trace & Reference / ghost story display: whether it is on, which story is ghosted (above, below or a given one), and its color.

The DevKit (AC29 `ACAPI_View.h`) provides `ACAPI_View_GetGhostStorySettings (API_GhostStoryType*)`, where `API_GhostStoryType` is `{ on, showOne, showAbove, showBelow, storyInd, ghostColor, filter }`, and `ACAPI_View_GetGhostRecord` / `ACAPI_View_ChangeGhostRecord` / `CreateGhostRecord` / `DeleteGhostRecord` for the per-window ghost record.

- `GetGhostStorySettings`: returns those fields, with the story as a floor index (as `GetStories` reports it).
- `SetGhostStorySettings`: partial input of the same fields. Change the current window's ghost record via `ChangeGhostRecord`, or `CreateGhostRecord` if it has none. Check in the DevKit docs which call sets which part, and fail clearly where the API offers no setter.
- Implement in `archicad-addon/Sources/NavigatorCommands.cpp/.hpp`. Register in `AddOnMain.cpp` with the version from `tools/package_info.json`, and guard per `AC_VERSION`.
- Add `archicad-addon/Examples/ghost_story.py` and Grasshopper components in `NavigatorComponents/`.
author: parikshit99

title: Add ModifyRevisionIssues: change a revision issue's ID, description and custom data
body:
Tapir reads revision issues, changes and document revisions (`GetRevisionIssues`, `GetRevisionChanges`, `GetDocumentRevisions`…) but cannot write any of them. Fixing an issue's ID or description, or filling its custom scheme fields from a project database, is manual.

The DevKit (AC29 `ACAPI_Revision.h`) provides `ACAPI_Revision_ChangeRVMIssue (API_RVMIssue*)`, which "modifies the short description, the ID, or the custom data of the given issue", plus `ACAPI_Revision_GetRVMIssueCustomScheme` for the custom field definitions.

- `ModifyRevisionIssues`: input `revisionIssues` — array of `{ revisionIssueId (guid, as GetRevisionIssues returns), id, description, customData { fieldName: value } }`, all except the guid optional. Read the issue, change the given fields, write back. Return execution results per item.
- Optionally add the custom scheme (field ids and names) and each issue's custom data to `GetRevisionIssues` (`archicad-addon/Sources/RevisionCommands.cpp`, ~line 33) so values can round-trip.
- Implement in `RevisionCommands.cpp/.hpp` and register next to `GetRevisionIssuesCommand` in `AddOnMain.cpp` with the version from `tools/package_info.json`. Guard per `AC_VERSION` if the API differs. Note in the description that issued revisions may refuse changes.
- Extend `archicad-addon/Examples/revision_management.py` and add a Grasshopper component next to `GetRevisionIssuesComponent.cs`.
author: parikshit99

title: Get/SetGeoLocation: survey point visibility and lock
body:
`GetGeoLocation` / `SetGeoLocation` read and write the survey point's position, but not whether it is shown or locked. Template and georeferencing scripts set the position, then still have to show or lock the survey point by hand.

The DevKit (AC29 `ACAPI_SurveyPoint.h`) provides `ACAPI_SurveyPoint_IsSurveyPointVisible` / `SetSurveyPointVisibility (bool*)` and `ACAPI_SurveyPoint_IsSurveyPointLocked` / `SetSurveyPointLocked (bool*)`.

- Add optional `isVisible` and `isLocked` booleans to the `surveyPoint` object of `GetGeoLocation` (`archicad-addon/Sources/ProjectCommands.cpp`, `GetGeoLocationCommand::Execute` ~line 1847) and `SetGeoLocation` (`SetGeoLocationCommand::Execute`, ~line 1911). Omitted means unchanged.
- Guard per `AC_VERSION`: visibility is available from AC25 (`APIEnv_IsSurveyPointVisibleID` / `APIEnv_SetSurveyPointVisibilityID` through `ACAPI_Environment`, see `MigrationHelper.hpp`), the lock only from AC26 (`APIEnv_IsSurveyPointLockedID` / `APIEnv_SetSurveyPointLockedID`). On AC25 leave `isLocked` out of the response and fail clearly if it is given.
- Update the descriptions in `AddOnMain.cpp`, extend `archicad-addon/Examples/set_geo_location.py`, and add the inputs and outputs to the Grasshopper geo location components.
author: parikshit99

title: Sun studies: get and set the project date/time, calculate the sun position, read sun settings
body:
Tapir reads and writes the project's geographic location (`GetGeoLocation` / `SetGeoLocation`) and copies the 3D view's sun angles inside `Set3DProjectionSettings`, but scripts cannot set the date and time of the sun or ask where the sun is. Shadow and sun studies (step through a day, set the 3D sun and save an image per hour) are not possible.

The DevKit (AC29 `ACAPI_GeoLocation.h`) provides:
- `ACAPI_GeoLocation_GetPlaceSets` / `ACAPI_GeoLocation_ChangePlaceSets (API_PlaceInfo*)`, where `API_PlaceInfo` is `{ sumTime, year, month, day, hour, minute, second, longitude, latitude, altitude, north, sunAngXY, sunAngZ, timeZoneInMinutes, timeZoneOffset, … }`;
- `ACAPI_GeoLocation_CalcSunOnPlace (API_PlaceInfo*)`, which fills `sunAngXY` / `sunAngZ` from the date, time and location;
- `ACAPI_GeoLocation_CanChangePlaceSets` and `ACAPI_GeoLocation_GetSunSets (API_SunInfo*)` (sun and ambient color and intensity).

All of these also exist in the AC25 and AC26 DevKits as `APIEnv_GetPlaceSetsID` / `APIEnv_ChangePlaceSetsID` / `APIEnv_CanChangePlaceSetsID` / `APIEnv_GetSunSetsID` and `APIAny_CalcSunOnPlaceID`; map them in `MigrationHelper.hpp` as done for other renamed calls.

- `GetSunSettings`: returns the date and time (`year` … `second`, `daylightSaving`, time zone), the current sun angles (`azimuth`, `altitude` in degrees), and the sun/ambient color and intensity.
- `SetSunSettings`: partial input of the date/time fields (and `daylightSaving`). Read the place sets, change the given fields, `CalcSunOnPlace`, `ChangePlaceSets`. Fail clearly when `CanChangePlaceSets` says no (e.g. not reserved in Teamwork). Returns the resulting sun angles.
- `CalculateSunPosition`: input date/time (and optional location, defaulting to the project's). Returns `azimuth` / `altitude` without changing the project.
- Keep the location fields in `GetGeoLocation` / `SetGeoLocation` (`archicad-addon/Sources/ProjectCommands.cpp`, ~lines 1847 and 1911) as they are, and put the new commands next to them; register them next to `SetGeoLocationCommand` in `AddOnMain.cpp` with the version from `tools/package_info.json`.
- Check whether changing the place sets also moves the 3D window's sun (`sunAngSets`, see `archicad-addon/Sources/3DProjectionCommands.cpp`, ~line 170), and note the result in the descriptions.
- Add `archicad-addon/Examples/sun_study.py` (step through a day, set the sun, `SaveCurrentWindowAsImage` per hour) and Grasshopper components next to the geo location ones.
author: parikshit99

title: Project Info groups and fields on Archicad 30: create, rename, move and delete groups; rename and move fields
body:
Tapir's Project Info commands (`GetProjectInfoFields`, `SetProjectInfoField`, `CreateProjectInfoFields`, `DeleteProjectInfoFields`) go through autotexts. They cannot see or manage Project Info groups, and cannot rename a field or move it to another group. Office templates organise Project Info into groups (Client, Site, Contract…), so a scripted template cannot reproduce them.

Archicad 30 adds a dedicated API (AC30 DevKit): `ACAPI_ProjectInfo_GetGroups`, `GetGroupName`, `CreateGroup`, `RenameGroup`, `DeleteGroup`, `MoveGroup (groupGuid, beforeGroupGuid)`, `GetFields (groupGuid)`, `GetField`, `CreateField (groupGuid, name)`, `RenameField`, `SetFieldValue`, `DeleteField` and `MoveField (fieldGuid, toGroupGuid, beforeFieldGuid)`. Some older autotext-based calls are marked deprecated in favour of these.

- `GetProjectInfoGroups`: returns the groups in order, each with its fields `{ fieldId, name, value }`.
- `CreateProjectInfoGroups` / `RenameProjectInfoGroups` / `DeleteProjectInfoGroups` / `MoveProjectInfoGroups`.
- `RenameProjectInfoFields` / `MoveProjectInfoFields`.
- Add an optional `groupId` to `CreateProjectInfoFields` (`archicad-addon/Sources/ProjectCommands.cpp`, ~line 462).
- On AC30, consider moving `CreateProjectInfoFields`, `DeleteProjectInfoFields` and `SetProjectInfoField` to the new API too; it may fix open bug #667 (see PR #674).
- The new commands need `#ifdef ServerMainVers_3000` and should fail with a clear "Available from Archicad 30" message on older versions, as the AC29-only Design Options commands do.
- Register them next to `GetProjectInfoFieldsCommand` in `AddOnMain.cpp` with the version from `tools/package_info.json`. Add `archicad-addon/Examples/project_info_groups.py` and Grasshopper components in `ProjectComponents/`.
author: parikshit99

title: Graphic overrides: get and set the current window's override combination, read an element's effective override style
body:
Scripts can assign an override combination to a saved view through `SetViewSettings`, but cannot read or switch the combination of the current window. They also cannot ask which override style actually applies to an element, e.g. to check that a fire-rating rule hits the right walls.

The DevKit provides:
- **AC30:** `ACAPI_GraphicalOverride_GetActualOverrideCombination (API_Guid&)` and `ACAPI_GraphicalOverride_SetActualOverrideCombination (const API_Guid&)`, which apply a combination to the active window. These are new in Archicad 30.
- **All supported versions (already in the AC25 DevKit):** `ACAPI_Element_GetActualOverrideStyle (const API_Guid& element, API_OverrideStyle&)`, the merged override style of an element in the current window.

Suggested commands:
- `GetActiveGraphicalOverrideCombination`: returns `{ combinationId, name }` or none.
- `SetActiveGraphicalOverrideCombination`: input `combinationId` or `name`. Guard with `#ifdef ServerMainVers_3000` and fail with "Available from Archicad 30" on older versions.
- `GetGraphicalOverrideStyleOfElements`: input `elements`. Returns per element the effective style: surface color, cut/uncut surface flags, line/marker/text pen, contour override, fill overrides, or none when no rule applies. Guard per `AC_VERSION` where `API_OverrideStyle` differs.
- Register the commands with the other graphic override commands. If none are merged yet, put them in the Navigator group next to `GetViewSettingsCommand` (`archicad-addon/Sources/NavigatorCommands.cpp`, ~line 360). Use the version from `tools/package_info.json`.
- Add `archicad-addon/Examples/active_override_combination.py` and Grasshopper components.

Related: #561 and open PRs #663, #873 and #880 add commands to create and read override rules and combinations. This issue only covers applying a combination to the window and reading an element's effective style. Reuse their file (`GraphicalOverrideCommands.cpp`) and name lookups if one of them is merged first.
author: parikshit99

title: Get and set property values and classifications of tool defaults
body:
Properties and classifications can be read and set on placed elements (`Get/SetPropertyValuesOfElements`, `Get/SetClassificationsOfElements`), but not on a tool's defaults (the settings new elements get). The only way to change them is to save a favorite and apply it with `ApplyFavoritesToElementDefaults`. Template scripts cannot say "every new Wall gets classification X and property Fire Rating = REI 60" directly. Scripts that create elements and then classify them also do twice the work.

The DevKit (AC29 `ACAPI_Element.h`; `API_ElemType` from AC26) provides `ACAPI_Element_GetPropertyValuesOfDefaultElem (type, definitions, properties)`, `ACAPI_Element_SetPropertyOfDefaultElem (type, property)`, `ACAPI_Element_GetPropertyDefinitionsOfDefaultElem`, `ACAPI_Element_GetClassificationItemsDefault (type, systemItemPairs)`, `ACAPI_Element_AddClassificationItemDefault` (already used by `ApplyFavoritesToElementDefaults`) and `ACAPI_Element_RemoveClassificationItemDefault`.

- `GetPropertyValuesOfElementDefaults` / `SetPropertyValuesOfElementDefaults`: same shape as `Get/SetPropertyValuesOfElements` (`archicad-addon/Sources/PropertyCommands.cpp`, ~lines 391 and 518), with `elementType` (the `ElementType` enum of the common schema, plus variation where needed) in place of `elementId`.
- `GetClassificationsOfElementDefaults` / `SetClassificationsOfElementDefaults`: same shape as `Get/SetClassificationsOfElements` (`archicad-addon/Sources/ClassificationCommands.cpp`, ~lines 55 and 148).
- Reuse the property value conversion helpers those commands use, and return execution results per item.
- Register the commands next to their element counterparts in `AddOnMain.cpp`, with the version from `tools/package_info.json`. Guard the pre-AC26 type/variation signatures per `AC_VERSION` (see `TAPIR_Element_AddClassificationItemDefault` in `FavoritesCommands.cpp`, ~line 265).
- Add `archicad-addon/Examples/element_default_properties.py` (set a default, create a wall, read its property) and Grasshopper components next to the element property and classification ones.
author: parikshit99

title: Add GetSurfaceQuantitiesOfElements: covered and exposed surface areas between elements
body:
`GetQuantitiesOfElements` returns per-element totals (volumes, surfaces, lengths, per building material). Scripts cannot ask how much of an element's surface is covered by other elements, e.g. the wall area behind a slab or the slab area under walls. Finish and cladding take-offs, thermal envelope checks and formwork estimates need exactly this.

The DevKit (AC29 `ACAPI_Element.h`) provides `ACAPI_Element_GetSurfaceQuantities (const GS::Array<API_Guid>* elemGuids, const GS::Array<API_Guid>* coverElemGuids, GS::Array<API_ElemPartSurfaceQuantity>* quantities)`. It returns the surface information of the given elements relative to the covering elements.

- `GetSurfaceQuantitiesOfElements`: input `elements` and optional `coverElements` (default: all construction elements). Returns per element the fields of `API_ElemPartSurfaceQuantity` (exposed and covered surface areas, per building material where the struct provides them), with readable names.
- Implement in `archicad-addon/Sources/ElementCommands.cpp/.hpp` next to `GetQuantitiesOfElementsCommand` (~line 5470), reusing its element-type checks and building material lookups. Register next to it in `AddOnMain.cpp` with the version from `tools/package_info.json`, and guard per `AC_VERSION` where the API differs.
- Add `archicad-addon/Examples/get_surface_quantities.py` (a wall with a slab on it) and a Grasshopper component next to the quantities one.
author: parikshit99

title: Add ImportMarkupsFromPDF command
body:
Tapir manages issues (markups) and imports them from BCF (`ImportIssuesFromBCF`), but cannot import markups from PDF. Archicad supports this (Issue Manager > Import PDF markups). It is the usual way consultants and clients return comments on published PDF sets, and automating it closes the PDF review loop.

The DevKit (`ACAPI_Markup.h`) provides `ACAPI_Markup_ImportFromPDF (const IO::Location& fileLoc, const bool silentMode = false, const bool openMarkUpPalette = false)`. It is in the AC29 and AC30 DevKits and missing from AC25–AC28.

- `ImportMarkupsFromPDF`: input `pdfFilePath`. Imports in `silentMode = true` so no dialog blocks the API, without opening the palette. Returns an execution result.
- Also return the issues created by the import if that can be determined (e.g. diff `GetIssues` before and after), so scripts can process them.
- Guard with `#ifdef ServerMainVers_2900` and fail with "Available from Archicad 29" on older versions.
- Implement in `archicad-addon/Sources/IssueCommands.cpp/.hpp` next to `ImportIssuesFromBCFCommand` (~line 832) and register next to it in `AddOnMain.cpp` with the version from `tools/package_info.json`.
- Add `archicad-addon/Examples/import_pdf_markups.py` and a Grasshopper component next to the BCF import one in `IssuesComponents/`.
author: parikshit99

title: GetAttributesByType: add attribute creation info on Archicad 30 (method, source, creator, time)
body:
`GetAttributesByType` reports an attribute's `modificationTime` (#637), but not how, when and by whom it was created. Template audits ("which surfaces came in with that imported IFC or that hotlink?", "who added these layers?") need that.

Archicad 30 adds `ACAPI_Attribute_GetCreationInfo (API_AttrTypeID, API_AttributeIndex, std::optional<API_AttributeCreationInfo>&)` (AC30 DevKit, `ACAPI_Attribute.h`). `API_AttributeCreationInfo` is `{ methodID (API_AttrCreationMethod), methodDescription, source, creatorUserName, creationTime }`. The optional is empty when Archicad has no creation info for the attribute.

- In `GetAttributesByTypeCommand::Execute` (`archicad-addon/Sources/AttributeCommands.cpp`, ~line 156; `modificationTime` is added ~line 180), add an optional `creationInfo` object per attribute: `{ method (readable name of API_AttrCreationMethod), methodDescription, source, creatorUserName, creationTime }`, in the same time format as `modificationTime`. Leave it out when the optional is empty.
- Guard with `#ifdef ServerMainVers_3000`. On older versions the field is never present. Update the response schema and the registered description in `AddOnMain.cpp` accordingly.
- Extend `archicad-addon/Examples/get_attributes_by_type.py` to print it, and add the output to the Grasshopper attribute component.
author: parikshit99

title: Add GetCurrentViewImage: return the 3D or rendering window image without a file (Archicad 30)
body:
`SaveCurrentWindowAsImage` writes the current window to an image file. Scripts that only want to show or forward the image (Grasshopper previews, posting to a chat, comparing design options) must then read the file back and clean it up. Archicad 30 can also grab the rendering window directly, which pairs with the rendering commands requested in #920.

Archicad 30 adds `ACAPI_View_GetCurrentImage (NewDisplay::NativeImage& nativeImage, const API_ImageSource& imageSource)` (AC30 DevKit, `ACAPI_View.h`). It "gets an image of the current view (3D, or rendering)", with `imageSource` selecting the 3D window or the rendering window.

- `GetCurrentViewImage`: input `source` (`3DWindow` default, or `RenderingWindow`) and optional `format` (`png` default, `jpg`). Returns the image as base64 with its width and height. Encode it the way `GetElementPreviewImage` / `GetRoomImage` return their images, so clients handle all three alike.
- Guard with `#ifdef ServerMainVers_3000` and fail with "Available from Archicad 30" on older versions. Fail clearly when the requested window is not open.
- Implement in `archicad-addon/Sources/ProjectCommands.cpp/.hpp` next to `SaveCurrentWindowAsImageCommand` (~line 1615) and register next to it in `AddOnMain.cpp` with the version from `tools/package_info.json`.
- Add `archicad-addon/Examples/get_current_view_image.py` and a Grasshopper component next to `SaveCurrentWindowAsImageComponent.cs`.
author: parikshit99

title: Add ModifyPens: change single pens of the active pen table
body:
Pen tables can be read (`GetPenTables`) and created or overwritten as a whole (`CreatePenTables` with `overwriteExisting`). Changing one pen's color or width in the active pen table, e.g. setting pen 5 to 0.35 mm, means rewriting the whole table.

The DevKit (`ACAPI_Attribute.h`) provides `ACAPI_Attribute_ModifyPen (const API_Pen&)`, which modifies a pen by index in the active pen table. `API_Pen` is `{ index, modiTime, rgb, width, description }`. The call is in the AC27–AC30 DevKits and missing from AC25 and AC26.

- `ModifyPens`: input `pens` — array of `{ index, color {red, green, blue} (0..1), width (mm), description }`, all except `index` optional. Read the current pen with `ACAPI_Attribute_GetPen`, change the given fields, write it back. Returns execution results per pen.
- Optionally an input `target` (`model` default, `layout`) if the API distinguishes the active model and layout pen tables; check the DevKit docs.
- Guard with `#ifdef ServerMainVers_2700`. On AC25/26 fall back to rewriting the active pen table the way `CreatePenTables` overwrites (`archicad-addon/Sources/AttributeCommands.cpp`, schema ~line 4370), or fail with "Available from Archicad 27".
- Implement in `AttributeCommands.cpp/.hpp` next to `GetPenTablesCommand` (~line 1056), and register it in the Attribute group of `AddOnMain.cpp` with the version from `tools/package_info.json`. The pen tables are a Teamwork lockable set (`PenTables`, see `ReserveLockableObjectSet`), so mention it in the description.
- Add `archicad-addon/Examples/modify_pens.py` and a Grasshopper component next to the pen table ones in `AttributesComponents/`.
author: parikshit99

title: ModifyOpenings: support Archicad 29 and 30 through ACAPI::Element::Opening::Modify
body:
PR #918 (for #911) adds `ModifyOpenings` for Archicad 25–28, but on Archicad 29 and 30 it reports "not supported yet" for every item. `API_OpeningType` does not compile there, and the modifier side of the new opening interface was not available when the PR was written. Openings are mostly used on current versions, so the command needs to cover 29 and 30 too.

The AC29 DevKit (identical headers in AC30) has the modifier, in `Support/Modules/ArchicadAPI/ACAPI/Element/Opening/`:

- `Opening.hpp`: `ACAPI::Element::Opening::Get (UniqueID)` and `Opening::Modify (modifierFunc, undoString)`. The `Opening::Modifier` gives `GetExtrusionParameters ()`, `GetOpeningGeometry ()`, `GetFloorPlanParameters ()` and `ChangeParentElement (UniqueID)`.
- `OpeningExtrusionParameters.hpp` (modifiable side): `SetWidth`, `SetHeight`, `SetAnchor`, `SetAnchorAltitude`, `SetConstraint`, `SetLinkedStatus`, `SetLimitType`, `SetExtrusionStartOffset`, `SetFiniteBodyLength`.
- `OpeningGeometry.hpp` (modifiable side): `SetPolygon (Geometry::Polygon2D)` and `Transform (API_Tranmat)`. The read side gives `GetAnchorPoint`, `GetVectorX`, `GetVectorY` and `GetExtrusionDirection`.
- The DevKit example `Examples/Opening_Test/Src/Opening_Functions.cpp` shows the `Get` → `Modify ([&] (Opening::Modifier& modifier) { … }, "undo name")` pattern (change parent, add/remove cut element).

What to do:
- Fill the `#else` (AC29+) branch of `ModifyOpenings` with the same inputs as on AC25–28 (`width`, `height`, `basePoint`):
  - `width` / `height` through `SetWidth` / `SetHeight`, keeping the bottom edge in place as on AC25–28.
  - `basePoint` through `Transform` with a translation from the current anchor point (`GetAnchorPoint`), and/or `SetAnchorAltitude` for the Z, mirroring how `CreateOpenings` places openings on AC29+ through `ACAPI::Element::OpeningDefault`.
- Read the opening back after `Modify` and fail the item clearly if a value was not applied, as the AC25–28 branch does.
- If #918 is not merged yet, build on its branch or follow it up right after it merges; do not duplicate the command.
- Update the registered description in `AddOnMain.cpp` (no more "not supported" on 29/30) and make `archicad-addon/Examples/modify_openings.py` produce the same output on all versions.
author: parikshit99

title: Rendering: set the image size and resolution, report the current scene
body:
PR #943 (part 1 of #920) adds `GetRenderingScenes`, `SetCurrentRenderingScene` and `PhotoRender`. It leaves out two things it believed the API did not offer. Both are in the DevKit:

1. **Image size and resolution.** `API_PhotoRenderPars` indeed only holds the file, type, color depth and dithering. The size is a rendering setting: `ACAPI_Rendering_GetRenderingSets (void* rendInfo, API_RendSetTypeID, const GS::UniString* sceneName = nullptr)` and `ACAPI_Rendering_ChangeRenderingSets (void*, API_RendSetTypeID)` with `APIRendSet_ImageID` read and write `API_RendImage { hSize, vSize, outResolution, proportional, bkgPict, bkgSkyRGB, … }`. `APIRendSet_EffectsID` gives `API_RendEffects` (renderer id, background alpha…). On AC25/26 the same calls are `APIEnv_GetRenderingSetsID` / `APIEnv_ChangeRenderingSetsID`.
   - Add optional `width`, `height` (pixels) and `resolution` (dpi) to `PhotoRender`. Read the image settings, change the given fields, write them back before rendering, and restore the previous values afterwards so the scene is not changed permanently. Alternatively, add separate `GetRenderingImageSettings` / `SetRenderingImageSettings` commands.
2. **The current scene.** The DevKit documents that `ACAPI_Rendering_GetRenderingSceneNames` returns the names "in the order of recent usage, putting the most recent rendering scene first". Report the first name as `currentSceneName` in `GetRenderingScenes`, after confirming in Archicad that the first entry is the scene selected in the PhotoRendering palette. If it is not, leave the field out and say so in the description.

- Build on #943's `RenderingCommands.cpp/.hpp` (wait for it or follow it up right after it merges). Update the registered descriptions in `AddOnMain.cpp` and `archicad-addon/Examples/photo_render.py`.
- Part 2 of #920 (the Grasshopper components) should then expose the new inputs/outputs too; mention it on #920 if part 2 is already open.
author: parikshit99

title: Give the Claude bots the Archicad DevKit headers (issue bot, steward fix, PR review)
body:
**For a maintainer.** This needs changes under `.github/workflows/`, which the issue bot cannot make: it is denied Edit/Write under `.github/` and its `GITHUB_TOKEN` has no `workflows` permission.

## Problem

None of the Claude jobs has the Archicad API DevKit:

- `claude_issue_triage.yml`: the `fix` and `reply` jobs
- `claude_bot_pr_steward.yml`: the fix job
- `claude_pr_review.yml`: the review job

The DevKits are only downloaded into the gitignored `archicad-addon/Build/DevKits/`, by the build checks. These jobs just check out the repository and run Claude, whose tool allowlist (correctly) has no `python`, `curl` or web fetch. Each prompt therefore says "THE DEVKIT IS NOT ON THIS RUNNER", so the bot infers struct members, function names and version availability from existing call sites and from the issue text.

When a new API has no existing call site, the guesses fail the build. Examples from bot PRs opened for issues filed on 2026-10-17:

- **#943 (rendering):** sets `API_PhotoRenderPars::fileLoc`. The member is `IO::Location* file` in every DevKit from AC25 to AC30, so all 12 add-on builds failed.
- **#947 (renovation filters):** the AC25/26 shims call `APIEnv_*RenovationFilter*ID`. Those IDs don't exist; before AC27 these calls go through `ACAPI_Database (APIDb_...)` and `ACAPI_Goodies (APIAny_GetRenovationFilterNameID)`.
- **Bot PR bodies:** they now end with "the DevKit is not available where this was written ... a maintainer should confirm against the DevKit". In practice the build checks catch some of these errors, but each one costs a steward fix round (3 at most). The review can't catch the errors that still compile, such as a wrong elevation field or a wrong version guard.

`claude_pr_review.yml` notes that skipping the download was decided, "Revisit if reviews start getting the API wrong in ways that matter". The cases above suggest it is time.

## Proposal

1. **Add a download step before each Claude step.**
   - It runs from trusted code before Claude starts, so the tool allowlist and the security bounds in the workflow headers stay unchanged.
   - Example for the `fix`/`reply` jobs, after "Checkout repository":
     ```yaml
     - name: Download Development Kits
       run: |
         python archicad-addon/Tools/download_and_unzip.py https://github.com/GRAPHISOFT/archicad-api-devkit/releases/download/30.3000/API.Development.Kit.WIN.30.3000.zip archicad-addon/Build/DevKits/AC30
         # ...AC25-AC29 likewise, with the URLs from archicad_addon_build_check.yml
     ```
   - Cost: the AC27–AC30 zips are about 15 MB each and the AC25/AC26 zips about 63 MB each, so all six are roughly 190 MB, under a minute on a GitHub runner. AC30 alone covers most API lookups. The older versions are what lets the bot write correct `ServerMainVers_*` guards and pre-27 shims.
2. **Never run the download script from a pull request's branch.**
   - The steward's fix job checks out the bot PR's head, and the review must never execute PR code (`pull_request_target`).
   - In those jobs, run `download_and_unzip.py` from a checkout of `main` (or the base commit the review already pins), or download before checking out the PR branch.
3. **Keep the DevKit URLs in one place**, to answer the "third copy of the DevKit URLs" concern in `claude_pr_review.yml`.
   - For example, a small composite action (`.github/actions/download-devkits`) or one list read by both the build checks and the bot jobs.
4. **Update the prompts.**
   - Replace the "THE DEVKIT IS NOT ON THIS RUNNER" rules (`claude_issue_triage.yml` ~L304 and ~L576, `claude_bot_pr_steward.yml` ~L456, `claude_pr_review.yml` ~L258) with something like: "The DevKit headers are under `archicad-addon/Build/DevKits/AC<NN>/Support` (AC25–AC30). Grep them to confirm every struct member, function and API ID you use, and check that it exists in each version your guards build for."
   - Update the header comment in `claude_pr_review.yml` to match.
5. **Optional: add the DevKit Examples folder** to the AC30 download (or the latest version). The examples show call patterns, such as `Element_Test/Src/Element_Edit.cpp` for `API_EditPars`.

## Acceptance

- In the `fix` job, `ls archicad-addon/Build/DevKits/AC30/Support/Inc/APIdefs_Elements.h` succeeds before the Claude step runs.
- No Claude step's `--allowedTools`/`--disallowedTools` changes.
- The steward fix job and the review job never execute code from the PR branch.
author: parikshit99

title: Claude bots: a burst of issues used up the subscription, every bot run since fails silently, and nothing retries
body:
**For a maintainer.** This is about `.github/workflows/`, which the issue bot can't change.

## What happened (2026-10-17)

- **03:29–03:43 UTC:** about 40 feature issues were filed in quick succession. Each started a `fix` run of `claude_issue_triage.yml` at the same time, because the only `concurrency` group is per issue (`claude-issue-<n>`). Single runs cost up to $7 (one used 126 turns).
- **About 03:57 UTC:** every run still in progress failed at the same moment.
- **Since then:** every Claude run fails within about 0.3 s, with `num_turns: 1`, `total_cost_usd: 0`, `modelUsage: {}`, and then `Claude result reported subtype success with is_error:true`. This covers the issue bot, the review bot and the steward's fix job.
- **Count so far:** about 21 failed `claude_issue_triage.yml` runs, 17 failed `claude_pr_review.yml` runs and 6 failed steward `fix` runs. Examples:
  - [39001688902](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/actions/runs/39001688902) (fix of #947)
  - [39001268870](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/actions/runs/39001268870) (#976)
  - [39000044553](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/actions/runs/39000044553), which was cut off at 03:57 after 244 s of work
- **Cause:** almost certainly the usage limit of the subscription behind `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`. The logs don't say, because claude-code-action hides the output ("Running Claude Code via SDK (full output hidden for security)").

## Why it matters

The failures cascade:

- Issues whose run died never get a PR. #959 got nothing at all. #960 has a pushed branch `claude/issue-960-rendering-image-size` but no PR.
- No multi-part issue got its part 2 (see the split-chain issue filed alongside this one).
- The steward spends fix rounds and review attempts on runs that never started, and hands PRs to a maintainer (see the companion issue on counting).
- Nothing retries once the quota is back. Each affected issue or PR needs a person to act.

## Proposal

1. **Throttle runs across the repository.**
   - Add a repository-wide `concurrency` group, or a small semaphore job, that limits how many model runs (triage + review + fix) are in flight. For example 3–5, configurable through a repository variable.
   - A `concurrency` group without `cancel-in-progress` keeps only one pending run per group, so a queue needs either several fixed groups (`claude-slot-${{ n % 4 }}`) or a pre-step that waits until fewer than N runs are in progress.
2. **Recognise a quota or API failure.** When the result has `is_error: true` with zero turns and zero cost:
   - mark the run as an infrastructure failure (for example a distinct job output or a step summary line);
   - don't post anything on the issue or PR;
   - make sure the steward doesn't count it.
3. **Retry later.** Have the hourly steward sweep, or a small scheduled job, re-dispatch `claude_issue_triage.yml` (`workflow_dispatch` with `issue_number`) for open issues with no bot PR or comment whose last run failed this way. The same applies to reviews.
4. **Make the error visible.** Surface the error text in the job summary, for example from `claude-execution-output.json` with secrets redacted, so the next occurrence is diagnosable without guessing.

## Immediate mitigation

Until the quota resets, setting the repository variable `BOT_PR_STEWARD=false` stops the steward from re-dispatching reviews and fixes that can only fail. Each failed one counts toward the per-PR limits: #918 and #927 already have 6 of their 10 review attempts, and #943 and #947 were already labelled `needs-maintainer`. Set it back once runs succeed again.
author: parikshit99

title: Auto-merge only looks at the 30 newest open pull requests (gh pr list default limit)
body:
**For a maintainer.** This needs a change to `.github/workflows/claude_auto_merge.yml`.

## Problem

`claude_auto_merge.yml:123` builds its candidate list with

```bash
candidates=$(gh pr list --repo "$REPO" --state open --base main \
  --json number --jq '.[].number')
```

`gh pr list` returns at most **30** pull requests unless `--limit` is given. With 76 open pull requests there now, only the 30 newest are ever considered.

The scheduled run at 2026-10-17 03:50 UTC ([run 39000281658](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/actions/runs/39000281658)) logged exactly 30 groups, from #973 down to #912, and stopped. #906 and everything older was not looked at.

## Effect

- **Bot PRs that will never merge:** green, reviewed bot PRs such as #886, #872, #842, #841, #834, #828, #826, #763, #751, #750, #743, #676, #675 and #649. They have all build checks green, `claude-review` = success since 2026-10-16 ~18:20 UTC, mergeable state `clean`, and no `needs-maintainer` label. They become due on 2026-10-19 but will never be merged automatically, because they are outside the 30 newest.
- **Gets worse with more PRs:** every new bot PR pushes one more old one out of the window, so the oldest work is the least likely to merge.
- **Split issues don't close:** at line 334 the split-issue closing logic already passes `--limit 500` for merged PRs. Only the candidate list is affected.

## Fix

```bash
candidates=$(gh pr list --repo "$REPO" --state open --base main --limit 500 \
  --json number --jq '.[].number')
```

Optionally, also process the oldest first (`| sort -n`), so the longest-waiting PRs are handled first.

The steward already uses `--limit 200` (`claude_bot_pr_steward.yml:91`), so its view and the auto-merge's view of the open PRs currently differ.
author: parikshit99

title: Bot PR steward counts fix runs and reviews that never ran against a PR's limits
body:
**For a maintainer.** This needs a change to `.github/workflows/claude_bot_pr_steward.yml`.

## Problem

The steward caps each bot PR at `BOT_PR_MAX_FIX_ROUNDS` (default 3) fix runs and at 10 reviews without a recorded verdict. Both caps count **dispatched runs**:

- fix rounds through `countRuns claude_bot_pr_steward.yml "$fixTitle" "$created"` (~L211, ~L291);
- reviews through the `total -ge 10` check (~L279).

A run in which Claude errored before its first turn counts exactly like a real attempt. This happens, for example, when the subscription's usage limit is reached (see #977).

## What happened (2026-10-17)

- **#943:** the build failed on a single wrong member name (`API_PhotoRenderPars::fileLoc`; the member is `IO::Location* file`). The exact fix was posted in a comment. The steward dispatched fix runs at 04:01, 04:04 and 04:07 UTC; each failed in about 0.3 s with zero turns and zero cost. At 04:12 it labelled the PR `needs-maintainer` with "3 fix rounds did not make the builds and the review pass". No fix was ever attempted.
- **#947:** the same thing happened (fix runs at 04:04, 04:07 and 04:12; labelled at 04:15).
- **#918, #927 and #940:** their reviews are re-dispatched on every sweep and fail the same way. They are at 6, 6 and 4 of the 10 allowed, and will be handed over in the same way unless runs start succeeding again first.

A sweep runs every few minutes while the issue bot and the review keep starting it, so all the rounds are used up within minutes, long before a usage limit resets.

## Proposal

- **Count only real attempts.** A fix round counts when the fix job actually ran the model, for example when a job output from the fix job reports `num_turns > 0` or a non-zero cost, or when a step after the Claude step ran. Reviews work the same way.
- **Pause on infrastructure errors.** When the latest fix or review run of a PR failed as an infrastructure error, the sweep skips that PR until a later sweep, instead of re-dispatching immediately. A simple rule would be: no re-dispatch within 30 minutes of an `is_error` run with zero turns.
- **Record the reason.** Put the reason into the hand-over comment, so a maintainer can tell "the fixes failed" from "the model never ran".

## Recovering the affected PRs

Once fixed, and once runs succeed again, remove `needs-maintainer` from #943 and #947 to hand them back. Do this only for those two: #775, #837 and #843 were handed over for a different reason ("its fix run pushed nothing").
author: parikshit99

title: Split issues: one failed part run ends the chain for good (15 issues are stuck at part 1)
body:
**For a maintainer.** This needs a change to `.github/workflows/claude_issue_triage.yml` (and possibly to the steward).

## Problem

The `next-part` job dispatches the run for part k+1 only when the run for part k succeeded and opened a part (`needs.fix.result == 'success'`, and `count > PARTS_BEFORE`). As its header says, "a run that gives up or fails ends the chain". Nothing restarts a chain afterwards. Only a person can, by applying `claude-fix`, dispatching the workflow with `issue_number`, or commenting on the issue.

That's fine when the model decides to stop. It's wrong when the run died for an infrastructure reason, such as the subscription usage limit (#977), a runner loss, or the turn limit (see the max-turns issue filed alongside this one).

## What happened (2026-10-17)

- **03:39–03:55 UTC:** 15 split issues got their part 1 PR, and `next-part` dispatched the part 2 runs.
- **About 03:57 UTC:** those runs (`workflow_dispatch` runs of `claude_issue_triage.yml`) failed when the usage limit was hit, so each chain ended. No `claude/issue-<n>-part2-*` branch exists for any of them.

| Issue | Part 1 PR | Parts planned |
|---|---|---|
| #919 | #957 | 2 |
| #920 | #943 | 2 |
| #923 | #947 | 2 |
| #925 | #953 | 4 |
| #926 | #955 | 3 |
| #929 | #964 | 4 |
| #930 | #958 | 2 |
| #931 | #961 | 3 |
| #932 | #965 | 2 |
| #933 | #966 | 4 |
| #934 | #963 | 2 |
| #935 | #962 | 3 |
| #939 | #967 | 3 |
| #942 | #971 | 3 |
| #944 | #968 | 3 |

That is 28 planned parts that will never be started without a person. The auto-merge closes a split issue only "once all N parts are merged", so these issues also stay open forever.

## Proposal

- **Resume stalled chains from the scheduled sweep.** In the hourly steward sweep or another scheduled job, find open issues with a `claude-split-plan: parts=N` comment from the bot, fewer than N part PRs, and no run of `claude_issue_triage.yml` in progress for them. For each, dispatch `claude_issue_triage.yml` with `issue_number`, at most once per issue per sweep and within the throttle proposed in #977.
- **Keep deliberate stops final.** If the model itself stopped (a run that succeeded but opened no part), leave it. To tell the cases apart, the fix job can write an output such as `outcome=stopped|opened|infra-error`.
- **Optional:** `count` uses `gh pr list --state all --limit 500`. With the current rate of bot PRs, that limit will be reached. Filtering on `--search "head:claude/issue-${ISSUE_NUMBER}-part"` keeps it exact.

## Recovering the 15 issues

Once runs succeed again, a short comment on each of the issues above restarts the bot through the `reply` job, which also feeds `next-part`. Ideally post the comments a few at a time, not all 15 at once.
author: parikshit99

title: Issue bot: a run that goes past --max-turns is marked failed even after it opened its PR
body:
**For a maintainer.** This needs a change to `.github/workflows/claude_issue_triage.yml` (the same pattern exists in `claude_pr_review.yml` and the steward's fix job).

## Problem

All Claude steps run with `--max-turns 120`. When a run finishes its work in slightly more turns, claude-code-action still fails the step:

```
"subtype": "success", "is_error": false, "num_turns": 126, "total_cost_usd": 7.15
##[error]Claude reported a successful result after 126 turns, exceeding the configured maximum of 120
```

([run 38998962841](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/actions/runs/38998962841), issue #937)

That run did its job: it pushed `claude/issue-937-modify-revision-issues` and opened **#973** at 03:49:25 UTC. But the `fix` job is marked failed, so both follow-up jobs (`next-part` and `start-steward`, which require `needs.fix.result == 'success'`) were skipped:

- `start-steward` didn't start the build checks and the review for #973. The PR waits for a later scheduled sweep.
- For a split issue, `next-part` would end the chain after a part that was in fact opened (see #980).
- The run shows red in the Actions list, which is easily mistaken for "the bot couldn't do it".

New commands that touch the C++ command, the schema, `AddOnMain.cpp`, a Python example and a Grasshopper component routinely need more than 100 turns, so this will recur.

## Proposal (any of these)

1. **Raise the limit.** Raise `--max-turns` for `fix`/`reply` to, say, 200. The 60-minute `timeout-minutes` still bounds a run.
2. **Judge success by the outcome.** Decide what to do next from what the run produced, not from the step result:
   - Give the Claude step `continue-on-error: true`.
   - Add a plain-shell step afterwards that checks whether a new `claude/issue-<n>-…` PR or a bot comment appeared since the run started, and sets the job output that `next-part` and `start-steward` read.
   - Fail the job only when nothing was produced. This also covers the zero-turn failures of #977.
3. **Make the follow-ups tolerant.** Make `start-steward` run on `always()` and dispatch the steward whenever an open bot PR for the issue has a head with no build-check runs. It is idempotent: the sweep only acts when there is something to do.

Option 2 is the most robust, because it doesn't depend on the action's turn accounting.
author: parikshit99

title: Grasshopper components for MEP system groups and physical systems
body:
`GetMEPSystemGroups`, `CreateMEPSystemGroups` and `CreateMEPPhysicalSystems` (registered in
`AddOnMain.cpp`, 1.7.2, Archicad 29+) are the only user-facing commands without a Grasshopper
component. None of their names appears under `grasshopper-plugin/`.

Please add three components in `grasshopper-plugin/TapirGrasshopperPlugin/Components/MEPComponents/`:

- **GetMEPSystemGroups:** outputs the system groups (name, guid) and, per group, its physical
  systems (name, root element, MEP system).
- **CreateMEPSystemGroups:** input group names; outputs the created group ids or the per-item errors.
- **CreateMEPPhysicalSystems:** inputs the group, the name, and the optional root element and MEP
  system; outputs the created ids or errors.

Follow the existing MEP components, such as `CreateElectricalPanelsComponent.cs` and
`ConnectMEPElementsComponent.cs`, and the existing `GetMEPSystemsComponent.cs` for the MEP system
input. Take the input and output names from the commands' schemas in `MEPCommands.cpp`. No Add-On
change is needed. The example `archicad-addon/Examples/mep_systems.py` shows the command calls.

title: GetHotlinks: list the placed instances of each hotlink node
body:
`GetHotlinks` returns the node tree (`location`, `hotlinkNodeId`, `name`, `type`, `children`), but
not the hotlink instances placed from each node. A script therefore cannot find which instance
elements to move with `ChangeHotlinkInstances`, or what a delete or break (#924) would affect. Nothing on
`main` or in PR #956 lists instances.

Please add `instances: [{elementId}]` to every node in `GetHotlinks`, with the instance element GUIDs in
the order Archicad returns them.

API (AC27+, `ACAPI_Database.h`):
```cpp
__APIEXPORT GSErrCode ACAPI_Hotlink_GetHotlinkInstances (const API_Guid* hotlinkNodeGuid, GS::Array<API_Guid>* elementRefList);
// NoError; APIERR_BADPARS - any of the parameters is nullptr; APIERR_BADID - no hotlink element found by the specified Guid
// "retrieves the API_HotlinkType hotlink instance elements of the specified hotlink node."
```
AC25/AC26: `ACAPI_Database (APIDb_GetHotlinkInstancesID, (void*) &nodeGuid, &elementRefList)`
(`APIdefs_Database.h`: "par1: const API_Guid* (node), par2: GS::Array<API_Guid>* (hotlink elements)").
Add it to `MigrationHelper.hpp` like the other `APIDb_` shims.

Keep the existing fields unchanged; this only adds a field. Update the response schema and the example.
author: parikshit99

title: Add ZoomToElements (2D and 3D)
body:
There is `FitInWindow` (whole drawing), and `ZoomToBox` (#831, PR #833) for a 2D box, but no way to
zoom to given elements, especially in the 3D window.

Please add `ZoomToElements`:
- **Input:** `elements: [{elementId}]`, plus optional `keepSelection` (default `true`).
- **What it does:**
  1. Remember the current selection.
  2. Select the given elements (the same calls as `ChangeSelectionOfElements`).
  3. Zoom to the selection.
  4. Restore the previous selection when `keepSelection` is true.
- **Works in:** the current window, 2D or 3D.
- **Result:** an `ExecutionResult`. It's an error when none of the elements could be selected (for
  example, all of them are on another story or a hidden layer).

API (AC27+, `ACAPI_Automate.h`):
```cpp
__APIEXPORT GSErrCode ACAPI_View_ZoomToSelected ();   // "Zooming to the actual selection. (Even in 3D.)"
```
AC25/AC26: `ACAPI_Automate (APIDo_ZoomToSelectedID)` (`APIdefs_Automate.h`: "par1: --- par2: ---").
Add it to `MigrationHelper.hpp` the way `ACAPI_View_Rebuild` maps to `ACAPI_Automate (APIDo_RebuildID, ...)`.

Add a Python example and a Grasshopper component next to `FitInWindow`'s.

title: Classifications of attributes: get, add and remove
body:
Tapir reads and writes properties of attributes (`GetPropertyValuesOfAttributes` /
`SetPropertyValuesOfAttributes`), and classifications of elements (`GetClassificationsOfElements` /
`SetClassificationsOfElements`). It has no way to read or set the classifications of attributes,
such as building materials, composites or surfaces. Material classification is common in IFC and
quantity workflows.

Please add:
- **`GetClassificationsOfAttributes`:**
  - **Input:** `attributeIds`, as in `GetPropertyValuesOfAttributes`.
  - **Output per attribute:** `classificationIds: [{classificationSystemId, classificationItemId}]`, or an error.
- **`SetClassificationsOfAttributes`:**
  - **Input:** `[{attributeId, classificationId: {classificationSystemId, classificationItemId}}]`.
  - **Behaviour:** an item replaces the attribute's current item in the same system. A
    `classificationItemId` of null removes the classification in that system, mirroring
    `SetClassificationsOfElements`.
  - **Result:** an `executionResults` entry per item.

API (identical in AC25–AC30; AC25–AC27 add `__ACENV_CALL`; `ACAPinc.h`):
```cpp
__APIEXPORT GSErrCode ACAPI_Attribute_GetClassificationItems (const API_Attr_Head& attrHead, GS::Array<GS::Pair<API_Guid, API_Guid>>& systemItemPairs);
// systemItemPairs: "A list of classification system and classification item guid pairs, that represent the attribute's classifications."
// APIERR_BADINDEX - attrHead did not refer to a valid attribute; APIERR_GENERAL - internal error.

__APIEXPORT GSErrCode ACAPI_Attribute_AddClassificationItem (const API_Attr_Head& attrHead, const API_Guid& itemGuid);
// APIERR_BADINDEX; APIERR_READONLY - "can not be modified (i.e. from a hotlink) or you do not have the right to classify
// attributes in the current teamwork plan"; APIERR_BADID - inexistent item; APIERR_BADCLASSIFICATION - "not available for the given attribute".

__APIEXPORT GSErrCode ACAPI_Attribute_RemoveClassificationItem (const API_Attr_Head& attrHead, const API_Guid& itemGuid);
// APIERR_BADINDEX; APIERR_READONLY; APIERR_BADID; APIERR_BADPARS - "The attribute did not have the specified classification."
```
`attrHead` needs `typeID` and `index`. Resolve them from the attribute GUID the same way
`GetPropertyValuesOfAttributes` does. Wrap the writes in `ACAPI_CallUndoableCommand`. Add a Python
example and Grasshopper components next to the attribute property ones.
