title: Line and fill consolidation, and the list of used attributes
body:
These are attribute-maintenance tasks people script before a project is handed over:
- Archicad's **Line Consolidation** and **Fill Consolidation** menu commands;
- the list of attributes actually used, so unused ones can be removed with `DeleteAttributes`.

The API reaches all three through one call.

Please add:
- **`ConsolidateLines`** and **`ConsolidateFills`:** no input; run the menu command; result is an
  `ExecutionResult`.
- **`GetUsedAttributes`:** returns what Archicad reports for "usedAttributes".

API (AC27+, `ACAPI_Database.h`):
```cpp
__APIEXPORT GSErrCode ACAPI_Database_JsonQuery (const GS::UniString* query, GS::UniString* result);
// NoError; other error code - query is invalid. Available queries (from the DevKit remarks):
// "getTopWindow"            - The title of the top window.
// "lineConsolidation"       - Calls the Line Consolidation menu command.
// "fillNormalization"       - Calls the Fill Consolidation menu command.
// "usedAttributes"          - Returns the list of used attributes.
// "numberOfTraceReferences" - Returns the number of trace references.
```

Notes:
- **Result format:** the DevKit doesn't document the format of `result` for "usedAttributes". Parse it
  as JSON when it is valid JSON and map it to `[{attributeId, type, name}]`. If it isn't JSON, return the
  raw string as `raw` and note that in the schema. In the PR, ask the tester for a sample result.
- **Dialogs:** the consolidation commands may open a dialog. The tester must check that the command
  returns without waiting for user input; if it doesn't, leave those two out.
- **Versions:** make it Archicad 27+ only. The AC25/AC26 DevKits list `APIDb_JsonQueryID`, but their
  comment gives `const API_Guid*` for both parameters, which doesn't match the AC27+ `GS::UniString*`
  signature. Return the usual "Available from Archicad 27" error on older versions.
author: parikshit99

title: AddOnMain.cpp and CommonSchemaDefinitions.json are merge-conflict hotspots for every new command
body:
**For a maintainer.** This is a structural change to how commands are registered, not a single feature, so the issue bot shouldn't attempt it on its own.

## Problem

Every new command edits the same two files at the same few places:

- **`archicad-addon/Sources/AddOnMain.cpp` (1535 lines):**
  - a new `#include` at the end of the include list (lines 28–46);
  - a new `RegisterCommand<…>` block at the end of its group in `Initialize()`, just before that group's `AddCommandGroup (…)`.
- **`archicad-addon/Sources/RFIX/Images/CommonSchemaDefinitions.json`:** new shared schema definitions, one hand-edited resource file.

Two PRs that add commands to the same group therefore always touch neighbouring lines, and whichever merges second conflicts.

## Evidence (2026-10-17)

- **53 of the 87 `claude/*` branches** on the repository change `AddOnMain.cpp`, and 18 change `CommonSchemaDefinitions.json`.
- **#873** merged cleanly into `main` on 2026-10-16 (`claude/resolved-pr-873`, `2a4ce61`). One day later it conflicts again, only because `main` added `#include "GridElementCommands.hpp"` on the same line where #873 adds `#include "GraphicOverrideCommands.hpp"`.
- **Repeated `main` merges:**
  - #676 has had `main` merged in 3 times and #648 3 times.
  - `main` carries 16 commits since 2026-10-10 that are merges of `main` or conflict resolutions.

## Why it matters for the automation

Each conflict costs a steward fix round, out of the default 3 (`claude_bot_pr_steward.yml`). Each resolution push is a new head, so the auto-merge's 72-hour clock restarts: it counts from the first `claude-review` success on the current head (`claude_auto_merge.yml`, ~L204–224). With dozens of bot PRs open, merging any one of them pushes others back into conflict and resets their wait. A backlog then drains much more slowly than it fills.

## Proposal

1. **Register commands next to their implementation.**
   - Give each `*Commands.cpp` group file (or a small `*Registration.cpp` beside it) a function such as `GSErrCode RegisterElementCommands (CommandGroup& group)`, which holds that file's `RegisterCommand<…>` calls with their version and description.
   - `Initialize()` then calls one function per group.
   - A new command touches its own group file, and only adds a line to `AddOnMain.cpp` when it creates a new group file.
   - The registration order, and so the generated docs and the palette order, stays the same.
   - `tools/generate_addon_docs.py` parses the registrations. Check whether it reads `AddOnMain.cpp` directly, and point it at the new files if it does.
2. **Make the include list conflict-free.** Either include the group headers through one `AllCommands.hpp` that is rarely edited, or keep the list sorted alphabetically, so new lines land in different places instead of all at the end.
3. **Split `CommonSchemaDefinitions.json`.** Either one definitions file per command group, concatenated at build time by `Tools/CompileResources.py`, or keep definitions that only one group uses inside that group's schema.

   `Tools/` is maintainer-only, so this part needs a person.

## Rollout

Do it in one maintainer PR while few bot PRs are open, or right after a batch merges. Every open PR that adds a command will conflict once with the restructuring, and after that much less often.

Point 1 alone is the main win; points 2 and 3 can follow.
author: parikshit99

title: Proposal: let Archicad users help Tapir without writing anything (error reports, one-click reactions, votes, testing fixes)
body:
**For a maintainer.** This is a proposal that needs three decisions before any part is built. Please don't let the issue bot implement it from this text.

## Problem

Almost everything Tapir learns from its users comes from the few who are comfortable on GitHub or Discord:

- **Issues:** of the last 100, 51 were opened by one person and 7 by the next. The Discord bot has filed 14 issues in total.
- **The add-on itself:** the palette's only link is the Tapir button, which opens the repository page (`TapirPalette.cpp:578`). The repository has no issue templates.
- **Testing fixes:** the steward asks the issue's author to download test builds from GitHub. That needs a GitHub login, the macOS download is a zip inside a zip, and the add-on has to be swapped by hand. Discord-filed issues have no human author to ask.

Most users never write a report, and many don't use Discord. But they run Tapir commands and scripts every day, and that usage already shows what breaks and what's missing. The project just doesn't hear it. The result is that priorities are set by the contributors, while nothing in CI runs Archicad, so whether a fix works in Archicad is rarely checked by the people who use it.

## Proposal: the default contribution needs no typing, no account and no Discord

### 1. Opt-in anonymous error reports
- **What's recorded:** when a Tapir command returns an error, or a palette script exits with an error, Tapir records a *signature*: command name, error code or message key, Archicad version, Tapir version and OS.
  - Command errors can be caught centrally around the handlers installed in `RegisterCommand` (`AddOnMain.cpp`).
  - Script failures are visible where `TapirPalette::ExecuteScript` reads the exit code (`TapirPalette.cpp:~1070`).
- **Consent:** asked once ("Share anonymous error reports to help fix Tapir?"), changeable in the palette's settings, with a "view what will be sent" list.
- **What's never sent:** project data, parameter values, file paths or user names.
- **Counted, not filed one by one:** one GitHub issue per signature, with a running count, e.g. "`SetDetailsOfElements` → `APIERR_BADPARS` on AC29: 37 reports from 12 installs". The counts make the priorities.

### 2. One-click reactions in the palette
- **After a script run:** a quiet 👍 / 👎 "Did this do what you expected?", with an optional one-line note. A 👎 on a run that also produced an error attaches to that error's signature.
- **"Try the fix":**
  - The palette lists test builds of fixes waiting for a check, preferably ones touching commands this install has used or had errors with.
  - One click installs the build with the installer's existing update mode (`--addOnFile`), which already swaps the add-on and restarts Archicad.
  - "It works / It doesn't" lands on the pull request. "Back to the release version" undoes it.

### 3. One-click votes on feature requests
A short list of open feature requests in the palette, one click to vote. The count is recorded on the issue, so the request queue reflects what users want, not only what contributors propose.

**Writing stays possible but optional:** a "Tell us more" box for those who want it. GitHub and Discord remain extra channels, not the required ones.

## Decisions needed before building

1. **Transport.** GitHub accepts no anonymous writes, and a token inside a public add-on would be abused. This needs a small relay, the project's first hosted piece. For example, a free-tier serverless endpoint that:
   - checks the shape of each report and rate-limits per install;
   - holds the GitHub credential itself;
   - only updates counts and comments on GitHub, or appends to a data file that a scheduled workflow aggregates.

   Who hosts it, and under which account?
2. **What is collected, and the wording.** Tapir is used in offices, often under company IT policies. Decide the exact fields, how long they're kept, and the consent text and its default (off until asked). Anonymous install IDs are needed for "N installs" counts and rate limits; decide whether they reset.
3. **Test builds on users' machines.** Fix builds are code the issue bot wrote from public issue text. Offer only builds that:
   - come from this repository's own CI (never forks);
   - passed the build checks and the review;
   - are clearly labelled as previews.

   Is that bar enough, or should a maintainer approve each one before it's offered?

## How it fits the automation

- **Signatures, not single reports:** reports become signatures with counts, so a burst of reports adds to counts instead of starting dozens of parallel Claude runs (see #977).
- **Prioritising by reach:** the issue bot and the steward can work on the highest-count signatures and the most-voted requests first.
- **In-Archicad results:** "It works / It doesn't" gives the steward and the auto-merge a signal that today only #887's community test runner (scripted checks, on a tester's own machine) can approach.

## Possible parts, once the decisions are made

1. **Add-on:** the local error-signature log and the consent setting, with nothing sent yet. This is plain add-on code; the issue bot can build it.
2. **Relay plus aggregation workflow:** maintainer.
3. **Add-on:** sending the queued signatures, plus 👍/👎 after script runs.
4. **Add-on and installer:** the "Try the fix" list and one-click install/revert. Touches release-critical installer paths, so it needs a maintainer.
5. **Add-on:** the feature-request vote list.
author: parikshit99

title: Claude bots: match the model to the job (Sonnet for light work, Opus for hard work, Fable only when Opus fails)
body:
Every job that runs Claude passes `--model best`, which currently resolves to Fable 5.1, the most capable and most expensive model. The four places:

| Workflow | Job | Line |
|---|---|---|
| `claude_issue_triage.yml` | `fix` (new issues, `claude-fix`, `next-part`) | 332 |
| `claude_issue_triage.yml` | `reply` (every human comment on an issue) | 623 |
| `claude_pr_review.yml` | every review and re-review | 379 |
| `claude_bot_pr_steward.yml` | `fix` rounds on the bot's pull requests | 469 |

The run logs confirm it. Both a successful run (job 117300314424, a reply on #926 at 03:51 UTC on 17 Oct) and a failed one (run 39018723166, on #990) start with `"model": "claude-fable-5-1"`. The successful reply took 11 turns and reported `total_cost_usd` of about 0.93.

`best` was a deliberate choice in #713 (commit 955983b), so that the bots follow new models automatically. The cost shows in #977. All of these jobs draw on one subscription, and a burst of about 40 parallel runs on 17 Oct used it up in under an hour. Since then every run has failed after one turn.

## Prices

Anthropic's published API prices per million tokens:

| Model | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| Fable 5.1 (what `best` resolves to) | $10 | $50 |
| Opus 5.5 | $4 | $20 |
| Sonnet 5.5 | $2 | $10 |

A subscription isn't billed per token, but heavier usage still uses up its allowance faster. Fable 5.1 also tends to take longer turns and more of them on the same task.

## Proposal: three tiers

Use aliases rather than pinned IDs, so each tier still moves to new models automatically, as #713 intended.

**Sonnet (`--model sonnet`): reading and commenting**
- `reply` on issues: answering questions, pointing to a PR, asking the reporter for details.
- Re-reviews of a pull request after a push. These check whether earlier findings were addressed, against a small diff.

**Opus (`--model opus`): the hard work**
- `fix` in `claude_issue_triage.yml`: writing C++ against the Archicad API without the DevKit or a compiler.
- Steward `fix` rounds, except the last one (see below).
- The first review of a pull request, which is the main safeguard before auto-merge.

**Fable (`--model best`): only when Opus has failed**
- **Opus could not get it right.** The steward already counts fix rounds per PR (`countRuns`, at most `BOT_PR_MAX_FIX_ROUNDS`, default 3). It could pass the model with the dispatch, e.g. a `model` input next to `pr_number`:
  - rounds 1 to N-1 run on `opus`;
  - the last round before `needs-maintainer` runs on `best`.

  Fable is then spent only on PRs that Opus has already failed at least once, as one last attempt before a maintainer has to step in. The same applies to an issue whose Opus `fix` run ended without a PR or a comment, for example when it hit `--max-turns`: one retry on `best`.
- **Opus was unavailable.** Claude Code's `--fallback-model` option switches to another model when the main one is overloaded, e.g. `--model opus --fallback-model best`. This covers availability only, not quality.

Two cautions for the escalation:
- **Don't escalate on quota errors.** A run that fails in under a second with `num_turns: 1` and `total_cost_usd: 0` is the subscription being exhausted (#977), not Opus failing. Retrying it on Fable just spends another attempt. Only escalate runs that actually did work.
- **Fable draws on the same subscription.** It is a fallback for hard tasks, not for a used-up subscription.

## Making it adjustable

Read each tier from a repository variable, so a maintainer can change it without a PR. For example:
- `--model ${{ vars.CLAUDE_LIGHT_MODEL || 'sonnet' }}`
- `--model ${{ vars.CLAUDE_MODEL || 'opus' }}`
- `--model ${{ vars.CLAUDE_ESCALATION_MODEL || 'best' }}`

If Sonnet replies or reviews turn out too shallow, `CLAUDE_LIGHT_MODEL=opus` raises that tier without a code change.

## Measuring it

Each run's log already contains `num_turns` and `total_cost_usd`. To tell whether the change helped, compare before and after:
- the cost per issue;
- how many PRs need the Fable round;
- how many end with `needs-maintainer`.

## Notes

- This changes only `.github/`, which the issue bot must not touch, so it needs a maintainer PR. `claude_auto_merge` skips `.github/` changes, so that PR also needs a manual merge.
- It complements #977 (queueing and retry after the quota runs out). This issue is about using less quota per run, not about recovering once it is gone.
author: parikshit99

title: ModifySlabs / ModifyColumns move elements below the lowest story to story 0
body:
**Version:** 1.5.9 (AC29, macOS). Same code in 1.7.1 and `main`.

## What happens
When `zCoordinate` is passed to `ModifySlabs` or `ModifyColumns`, the floor index is
recalculated from the absolute Z via `GetFloorIndexAndOffset` (CommandBase.cpp).
If Z is below the level of the lowest story, no story matches and the function
returns `{ 0, zPos }` — the element is moved to **story index 0**, with the full
absolute Z as offset. The command reports success.

## Repro
Project with stories −1 (level −2.66) and 0 (level 0.00).
1. `CreateColumns` with `floorIndex: -1`, `coordinates.z: -2.41`, `height: 0.5` → floor −1.
2. `ModifyColumns` `{ elementId, zCoordinate: -2.71 }`.
3. `GetDetailsOfElements` → `floorIndex: 0`, `bottomOffset: -2.71`.

Same with `ModifySlabs` `zCoordinate: -2.71` on a slab created on floor −1.

## Expected
Element stays on its story (or on the lowest story) with a negative offset.

## Suggestion
In `GetFloorIndexAndOffset`, when no story is at or below `zPos`, fall back to the
lowest story: `return { lowest.index, zPos - lowest.level }`. Alternatively accept an
optional `floorIndex` in `ModifySlabs` / `ModifyColumns`, as the Create commands do.

## Workaround
Columns: write `bottomOffset` instead of `zCoordinate`.
Slabs: write `zCoordinate`, then reset `floorIndex` and move back by the story difference.

title: Graphic override rules: structured criterion, rule group and combination delete (on top of #873)
body:
## Summary

Builds on the graphic override commands merged in #873 instead of adding a separate command set. Supersedes #663, which predates #873/#880 and now conflicts with both.

- **Structured criterion**: `CreateGraphicOverrideRules` and `ModifyGraphicOverrideRules` accept a `criterion` object (schema `GraphicOverrideCriterion`) as an alternative to `criterionXML`. It is turned into Archicad's criterion XML by the generator in `GraphicOverrideCriterion.cpp`. Giving both is an error; giving neither keeps the current behaviour.
- **New commands** (1.7.2):
  - `GetGraphicOverrideRuleGroups`: rule groups with their rules, empty groups included (`GetGraphicOverrideRules` cannot show an empty group).
  - `DeleteGraphicOverrideRuleGroups`: groups found by name, like `ruleGroupName` in #873.
  - `DeleteGraphicOverrideCombinations`: the rules are kept.

## The criterion generator

Writing criterion XML by hand is hard: as the `criterionXML` description in #873 says, Archicad drops XML written from scratch without an error. The generator writes XML that Archicad keeps. Every field was decoded from a real rule built in Archicad's criteria editor (one rule per tool on AC29), never guessed. It covers element types, classification, layers and the Model View, Construction, Positioning, Plan and Section, Surfaces/Materials, ID/Categories and Geometry groups, custom properties, plus tool-specific fields for Wall, Column, Beam, Slab, Roof, Shell, Object/Lamp, Door/Window, Opening, Curtain Wall and Stair.

```python
aclib.RunTapirCommand ('CreateGraphicOverrideRules', {'graphicOverrideRules': [{
    'name': 'High walls', 'ruleGroupName': 'Checks',
    'criterion': {'and': [{'elementType': 'Wall'}, {'wallHeightGreaterThan': 2.5}]},
    'style': {'lineMarkerTextPen': 20}}]})
```

## Deleting a rule group keeps its rules unless asked otherwise

`ACAPI_GraphicalOverride_DeleteOverrideRuleGroup` deletes the rules of the group with it, and a rule cannot live outside a group. A group that still contains rules is therefore kept, with an error, unless the request says what happens to the rules:

- `moveRulesToGroup`: the rules are moved to that group (created when missing) with `ACAPI_GraphicalOverride_MoveOverrideRule`, in their order, then the group is deleted.
- `deleteRules: true`: the rules are deleted with the group.

## Tests

- Community test runner check `archicad-addon/Test/checks/graphic_override_structured_criterion.json`: **AC29 11/11, AC27 11/11** (`tapir_test_runner.py check`, blank French template).
- Read-back on AC29 and AC27: rules created from `criterion` keep their criterion (element type and property conditions present in the stored XML, not replaced by the default), `ModifyGraphicOverrideRules` with `criterion` changes it, empty groups are listed.
- New examples run on AC27: `create_graphic_override_rules_with_criterion.py`, `get_graphic_override_rule_groups.py`, `delete_graphic_override_rule_groups.py`, `delete_graphic_override_combinations.py`.
- Builds: AC25, AC27, AC29 (the code is behind `ServerMainVers_2700`, like #873).

## Not covered

- No Grasshopper components, like the other graphic override commands from #873 and #880. Components for the whole graphic override area would fit better in a follow-up.

- The criterion generator's element type table was captured on AC29; on AC27 the generated rules are kept by Archicad, but which elements they match was not checked element by element.
- Some fields stay out on purpose (decoded but ambiguous): the renovation status, and the three enum fields of Opening (shape, limits, orientation), whose stored values do not follow the editor's order.

title: Claude bots: survive a spent usage limit (throttle, report and retry refused runs)
body:
Fixes #977

Overnight on 17 October, a burst of about 40 issues used up the subscription's usage limit. From then on every Claude run failed on its first turn (`is_error: true`, 0 turns, $0), the logs didn't say why, and nothing ever started the lost runs again. Meanwhile the steward counted the failed runs as rounds and handed #918, #927 and #940 over.

## Throttle (all Claude runs)
- **Slot wait:** at most `CLAUDE_MAX_RUNS` (repository variable, default 4) runs call the model at the same time. This covers issue `fix` and `reply`, reviews, and steward fixes. Each one waits in a new **Wait for a model slot** step, first in first out, until fewer than that many runs that started before it are still in progress. It waits for at most two hours.
- **Low API cost:** each check is one API call (`actions/runs?status=in_progress`), and the gap between checks grows the further back a run is in the queue.
- **Soft limit:** runs that start in the same second, or a run still finishing after its model call, can go a little over it.
- **Timeouts:** jobs keep their working time plus the two hours of waiting (fix and reply 180 min, review 165 min, steward fix 180 min).

## Refused runs are recognised and reported
- **Job summary:** a new **Report the Claude result** step reads the run's execution file. It writes the subtype, `is_error`, turns and cost to the job summary, plus the error text when the run failed (tokens redacted), which the action otherwise hides.
- **Refused-run failure:** a run with an error, one turn and no cost then fails in **Stop on a refused run** and posts nothing.
- **Escalation unchanged:** the escalation job from #1078 uses the same turn count and still never escalates a refused run.

## Retry
- **Issue fixes:** a new hourly `retry` job in `claude_issue_triage.yml` restarts `fix` for open issues whose last fix run was refused or waited for a slot in vain. It only does so when:
  - nothing came of the issue since (no comment or PR by the bot);
  - no run for the issue is queued or in progress;
  - the issue has had fewer than 5 such failures in the last day.
- **Pace:** at most `CLAUDE_RETRY_BATCH` (default 3) issues per hour, oldest first. `CLAUDE_RETRY=false` turns it off.
- **Run names:** triage runs are now named `Issue #<n>: <title>`, so the retry job can tell which issue a run belonged to.
- **Not retried:** a refused `reply`; the next comment starts a new one.
- **Bot PRs (the steward, from this branch's earlier commits):**
  - only review and fix runs that succeeded count as rounds;
  - after a failed run, the next one waits for the next hourly sweep (50 minutes);
  - only ten failures within a day hand the PR over.

## Testing
- `actionlint` passes on all four Claude workflows. It reports the same 5 info-level `SC2016` notes as `main`, and `yaml.safe_load` parses them.
- **Slot filter:** checked against synthetic run lists. It counts earlier runs of the three workflows, and leaves out sweeps, the scheduled retry, other workflows and later runs. I also ran it live against the repository.
- **Report step:** checked on sample execution files:
  - refused run: flagged, token redacted;
  - max-turns run: not flagged;
  - successful run: not flagged;
  - missing file: not flagged.
- **Retry job:** checked against a mock `gh` covering every case: a restart, the bot answered since, a run in progress, a closed issue, 5 refusals in a day, a run that failed for another reason, and the batch limit. I also ran it live once (0 refused runs yet, because older runs have neither the new names nor the new steps).
- The workflows themselves only run once this is on `main`.

Changes only `.github/` and CLAUDE.md, so it needs a manual merge. Once it's merged, `needs-maintainer` can come off #918, #927 and #940.

title: Work through the live Archicad API coverage checklist automatically: one issue per open group
body:
A pull request from parikshit99's fork (link to follow) adds a **live Archicad API coverage checklist**:
- `tools/generate_api_coverage.py` and `.github/workflows/api_coverage.yml`;
- a searchable page at `docs/api-coverage/`, plus the data on an `api-coverage` branch;
- an "Archicad API request" issue form.

**It covers every item of the Archicad 25–30 DevKits:**
- every exported C function, with the versions that have it;
- the names those functions had before Archicad 27, and the AC25/26 command ids, attached to their current names;
- the whole C++ API (`ACAPI::` and `IFCAPI::`: MEP, DesignOptions, IFC, Keynote, RoomBoundary and others).

**Each item has a status:**
- ✅ used on `main`
- 🔀 merged, not yet in a release
- 🚧 an open PR adds it
- 🙋 an open issue names it
- ⬜ open
- ⛔ skipped by a maintainer
- ➖ not usable from a JSON command

The workflow refreshes it within minutes of every push, PR and issue event, and hourly. Today:

| Part of the API | Used | Applicable | ✅ | 🔀 | 🚧 | 🙋 | ⬜ | ➖ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| C functions | 34 % | 749 | 242 | 17 | 102 | 31 | 357 | 164 |
| C functions of Archicad 25/26 only, and their command ids | 21 % | 90 | 19 | | 4 | 2 | 65 | 49 |
| C++ API | 29 % | 1595 | 236 | 230 | 1 | | 1128 | 255 |

This issue proposes letting the bots work through the ⬜ open items on their own, without ever taking something a person or a PR already has.

## Proposal: `claude_api_coverage.yml`

A scheduled workflow (for example daily) plus `workflow_dispatch`. It runs no model and needs `issues: write` and `actions: write`.

1. **Hold back when the bots are struggling.** Skip the run when:
   - recent Claude runs failed the way an exhausted quota fails (#977): `is_error`, one turn, $0;
   - more than `BOT_COVERAGE_MAX_OPEN` (default about 15) bot PRs are open;
   - or `BOT_API_COVERAGE` is `false`.
2. **Read `api-coverage.json` from the `api-coverage` branch.** It is already live, so 🚧 and 🙋 items are never picked.
   - Take the first group with ⬜ items.
   - Cut a big group (Element, View, Attribute, LibraryPart, Navigator, C++ MEP and so on) into chunks of about 5–8 related items, by name prefix or class.
3. **File one issue in the "Archicad API request" format,** then dispatch `claude_issue_triage.yml` for it. Issues created with `GITHUB_TOKEN` start no workflow on their own, as with the Discord bot. The issue contains:
   - the items;
   - their declarations and doc comments, copied from the DevKit headers (the workflow downloads them, like the build checks). This also solves #976 for these issues;
   - for AC25/26, the older names or command ids;
   - the instruction to propose commands that fit Tapir's command groups, or to answer that an item is not useful as a JSON command. A maintainer then adds it to the skip list in `tools/api_coverage_rules.json`.

   The new issue names its items, so they turn 🙋 at once, and the next run moves on.
4. **Let the existing bots finish it.** Fix, split, review, the steward and auto-merge carry the issue to a merged PR, and the checklist moves it to 🔀 and then ✅.

At one issue a day, the open C functions alone become 60–80 issues over two to three months. One variable adjusts the rate.

## People and bots don't collide

- **People:** claim an item by filing an "Archicad API request" naming it (the page has a claim link next to every open item). It turns 🙋 within minutes, and the bot driver skips it.
- **Bot PRs:** bot PRs show as 🚧 as soon as they're opened, so people see that the work is underway.

## Until this exists

This is being done by hand from a Claude Code session: one group per day, picking only ⬜ items. #1013, #1014 and #1015 were filed this way.

## Notes

- This changes `.github/` and `tools/`, which the issue bot must not touch, so it needs a maintainer PR and a manual merge.
- Related: #976 (DevKit for the bots), #977 (quota and retries), #980 (split chains), #991 (model per job).
author: parikshit99

title: Bot PR steward: 6 fix rounds, reset counts when needs-maintainer is removed
body:
The steward's handover comment says to remove the `needs-maintainer` label to hand a PR back. But it counted fix rounds over the PR's whole life, so the next sweep counted the same 3 rounds and handed the PR over again right away. That happened on ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation#943.

Changes in `claude_bot_pr_steward.yml`:
- The sweep now counts fix rounds, and the "ten reviews without a verdict" limit, from the later of two times: when the PR was opened, or when someone last removed `needs-maintainer` (the latest `unlabeled` event in the issue events). Removing the label now resets both counts.
- If the events can't be read, the counts start from when the PR was opened, like before. The sweep keeps going.
- The default for `BOT_PR_MAX_FIX_ROUNDS` goes from 3 to 6.

`CLAUDE.md` is updated to match.

I checked the YAML parses and the sweep script passes `bash -n`. I also ran the "last removed" logic on sample event data, including the case where the events can't be read.

Note: if the `BOT_PR_MAX_FIX_ROUNDS` repository variable is set, it still overrides the new default of 6.

title: DeleteNavigatorItems: delete independent Worksheets and Details through ACAPI_Database_DeleteDatabase (today "Failed to delete navigator item.")
body:
**Environment:** Archicad 29 build 3200 (AUT), Tapir 1.7.0/1.7.1, solo project.

**Observed:** `DeleteNavigatorItems` on an independent Worksheet in the Project Map returns `Failed to delete navigator item.` The worksheet stays. Deleting it by hand in the Navigator works.

**Why, from the source** (`NavigatorCommands.cpp`, `DeleteNavigatorItemsCommand::Execute`): only Layout and Master Layout items go to `ACAPI_Database_DeleteDatabase`. Everything else goes to `ACAPI_Navigator_DeleteNavigatorView`, which handles View Map views only (same root cause as #690). `ACAPI_Database_DeleteDatabase` is documented for "independent detail, worksheet, layout, or master layout", so independent worksheets and details can use the same branch as layouts.

**Requested**
1. Project Map items whose database is an independent Worksheet (`APIWind_WorksheetID`) or Detail (`APIWind_DetailID`) → `ACAPI_Database_DeleteDatabase` with `navItem.db`.
2. Other Project Map viewpoints: as in PR #691 (`ACAPI_Navigator_DeleteNavigatorVPItem`). This issue only adds the worksheet/detail branch.
3. Execution result per item, as today.

**Use case:** cleaning up worksheets created by scripts (e.g. temporary worksheets for 2D checks, imported DWG worksheets) in a template-based project.

**Acceptance:** `CreateWorksheets` → `DeleteNavigatorItems` with the returned navigator item → success, and the item is gone from `GetNavigatorItemTree`.

title: GetDetailsOfElements: return the reference point of automatic Zones (today only stampPosition)
body:
**Environment:** Archicad 29 build 3200 (AUT), Tapir 1.7.1.

**Current state (main):** for Zones, `GetDetailsOfElements` returns `stampPosition` (`elem.zone.pos`) and `isManual`, but not the reference point an automatic zone was created from (`API_ZoneType::refPos`, DevKit to confirm the member name). `CreateZones` takes it as `referencePosition`.

**Requested**
1. `GetDetailsOfElements` for Zones: `referencePosition` (2D coordinate) when the zone is automatic (`isManual` false).
2. Optional: `SetDetailsOfElements` writes it (moves the reference point; the zone is recalculated on the next update).

**Use case:** recreating or refitting an automatic zone by script (after its walls change) needs the point that was clicked. The stamp is often moved away from it (e.g. to a room corner), and the polygon's centroid can lie outside an L-shaped room. Today we can't recreate the zone exactly the way it was created.

**Acceptance:** `CreateZones` with `referencePosition` (x, y) → `GetDetailsOfElements` returns the same (x, y).

title: Get3DBoundingBoxes returns a box for an element that DeleteElements has just deleted, instead of an error
body:
**Environment:** Archicad 29 build 3200 (AUT), Tapir 1.7.1, solo project (2026-10-17).

**Steps**
1. `CreateBeams` → 2 beams, keep the element ids.
2. `DeleteElements` with both ids → success. The beams are gone from the plan and from `GetElementsByType`.
3. `Get3DBoundingBoxes` with the same ids.

**Result:** both items return a `boundingBox3D` (the old box). Expected: an execution error per item ("element does not exist / is deleted"), as `GetDetailsOfElements` does for unknown ids.

**Why it matters:** we use `Get3DBoundingBoxes` to check that a delete or a temporary test element is really gone. A box for a deleted element makes the check pass by mistake.

**Possible cause (to confirm with the DevKit):** `ACAPI_Element_GetHeader` may still succeed for an element that is deleted but kept for undo. Checking for a deleted element (e.g. `ACAPI_Element_Get` returning `APIERR_DELETED`) before `ACAPI_Element_CalcBounds` would catch it. Other commands that start with `GetHeader` may have the same gap.

**Acceptance:** after step 2, step 3 returns an error for both ids.
author: thespatialist

title: GetDetailsOfElements floorPlanPolygons: composite wall skins are cut square at the reference line at joined L-corners, the corner area is missing
body:
**Environment:** Archicad 29 build 3200 (AUT), Tapir 1.7.0/1.7.1.

**Steps:** two composite walls (e.g. 4 skins: plaster, concrete, insulation, render), reference lines meeting exactly in an L-corner, joined correctly (the plan shows clean mitred/overlapping skins). `GetDetailsOfElements` with `fields: ["floorPlanPolygons"]` on both.

**Result:** each wall's skins end square at the end of its reference line. At the corner the outer skins (insulation, render) of neither wall cover the corner square, so the union of both walls' polygons has a notch at the outer corner. The plan drawing itself is correct.

**Requested (either is fine)**
1. Return the cut fill polygons as drawn, including the corner part the junction assigns to that wall; or
2. Document that the corner area is not included, and add a field to the junction info that says which wall owns the corner.

**Use case:** checking zone outlines and slab edges against the outer face of the walls (e.g. "slab edge = outside face of the concrete core", insulation running past it). With the notch, every outer corner reports a false deviation.

**Acceptance:** for a closed rectangle of 4 composite walls, the union of all `floorPlanPolygons` equals the outline drawn in Archicad (no notches at the corners).

title: CreateWalls / CreateBeams / CreateSlabs / CreateColumns: optional layerIndex (as CreateTexts, CreatePolylines, CreateHatches already have)
body:
**Environment:** Tapir main (2026-10-17).

**Current state:** `layerIndex` is accepted by CreatePolylines, CreateLineElements, CreateArcs, CreateCircles, CreateHotspots, CreateHatches, CreateSplines, CreateTexts (PR #878) and CreateLevelDimensions. It is missing in CreateWalls, CreateBeams, CreateSlabs, CreateColumns (and CreateZones, CreateObjects, CreateMeshes, CreateRoofs, CreateMorphs). New elements land on the tool's default layer or the favorite's layer, so every create needs a second `SetDetailsOfElements` call.

**Requested:** optional `layerIndex` per item in these Create* commands, written to `element.header.layer` before creation (same code as CreateTexts). Best in `CreateElementsCommandBase`, so every derived command gets it (as PR #906 does for the Element ID). Without `layerIndex` the current behaviour stays.

**Use case:** our layers follow a template rulebook (e.g. "220 Tragende Wände", "235 Dämmung"). Scripts that model a building from permit drawings create hundreds of elements and should put each on its layer in one step.

**Acceptance:** `CreateWalls` with `layerIndex: n` → `GetDetailsOfElements` returns `layerIndex: n`.

title: Set3DCutPlanes: allow switching cut planes off, add Get3DCutPlanes (split from #876)
body:
Split from #876 (part 3, by @ferencz-tamas), as suggested in the bot's assessment there.

**Current behaviour** (`archicad-addon/Sources/3DCutPlaneCommands.cpp`)
- `Set3DCutPlanes` always sets `isCutPlanes = true` and `useCustom = false`, and writes only `pa/pb/pc/pd`.
- The schema requires `minItems: 1`. `null`, `{}` and `[]` return `Invalid parameter: cutPlanes.` A script cannot put the 3D window back to "no cut". The workaround is two planes far away (±5000 m).
- There is no command that reads the current cut planes.

**Requested**
1. `Set3DCutPlanes` with `"cutPlanes": []` (or a flag such as `"enabled": false`) sets `isCutPlanes = false`.
2. New `Get3DCutPlanes`: returns `isCutPlanes` and the planes (`pa, pb, pc, pd`, plus `cutStatus`, `cutPen`, `cutMater`), and `useCustom`, `customPen`, `customMater`.
3. Optional on `Set3DCutPlanes`: `cutPen`, `cutMater`, `useCustom`, `customPen`, `customMater`.
4. Document in the description which side of the plane is kept, and that `pd` is in metres.

**Use case:** temporary 3D cuts during model checks (stairs vs. slab openings, wall/slab junctions), then restore the 3D window to its previous state. Round trip: `Get3DCutPlanes` → `Set3DCutPlanes` (check) → restore from the stored result.

title: GetViewSettings: return the "stored in this view" flags and the full transformation (split from #876)
body:
Split from #876 (part 1, small subset, by @ferencz-tamas), as suggested in the bot's assessment there.

**Current behaviour** (`NavigatorCommands.cpp`, `GetViewSettingsCommand::Execute`)
- Of the `API_NavigatorView` save flags, only `saveZoom` is returned. On write, `saveDScale` and `saveStructureDisplay` are set implicitly.
- Only the derived `rotation` is returned, not the transformation `tr`.

**Requested**

title: Get/Set3DDocumentSettings: read and write the settings of a 3D Document (split from #876)
body:
Split from #876 (part 2, 3D Documents only, by @ferencz-tamas), as suggested in the bot's assessment there.

**Gap:** no Tapir command reads or writes `API_DocumentFrom3DType`. According to #876, the API has been available since Archicad 26:
`ACAPI_View_GetDocumentFrom3DSettings (API_DatabaseUnId*, API_DocumentFrom3DType*)` and `ACAPI_View_ChangeDocumentFrom3DSettings (...)`. For a non-3D-Document database they return `APIERR_BADDATABASE`.

**Requested:** two commands, keyed by `navigatorItemId` or `databaseId` (resolved as `GetDatabaseIdFromNavigatorItemId` does):
- `Get3DDocumentSettings` returns:
  - `cutPlanes` (same shape as `Set3DCutPlanes`/`Get3DCutPlanes`)
  - `filterAndCut` (story range, trim to story range, filter mode)
  - `projection` (perspective/axonometric; reuse the schema of `Get3DProjectionSettings` if possible)
  - `window` (size, zoom)
- `Set3DDocumentSettings`: partial write, fields that are not given stay unchanged. `ChangeDocumentFrom3DSettings` is documented as non-undoable, so no `ACAPI_CallUndoableCommand`.
- Version gate: Archicad 26 or later.

A first version with only `cutPlanes` + `filterAndCut` (story range) would already cover most use cases. Projection and window can follow.

**Use case:** plans made as 3D Documents (e.g. a site plan with distance areas, per-storey axonometries, 3D sections for permit drawings). Today their story range, cut and projection can only be checked and changed by hand in the 3D Document Settings dialog. Acceptance: round trip Get → Set → Get returns identical data.

Not covered: saved 3D *views* and "Redefine image settings based on current" (#876 part 2 views / part 4). According to the bot there is no ACAPI for them, so they need Graphisoft.
author: thespatialist

title: Feature request: Export3DModel (OBJ, then glTF) with the cameras of saved 3D views
body:
## Goal
Keep an external renderer (Blender) in sync with the Archicad model without manual exports: export the 3D model of all or some elements to a file, with the cameras of the saved 3D views, then re-export automatically on element change notifications (`SetElementNotificationClient` already exists).

## Why a new command
- The API cannot drive Archicad's own 3D translators: `API_FTypeID` lists no 3DS, OBJ, FBX or glTF format (APIdefs_Automate.h, DevKit 27.3001 and 29.3000).
- Most of the work already exists: `Get3DGeometryOfElements` (1.7.2) walks the 3D bodies per element (vertices, faces with holes, surface of each face). An export command could share that traversal and write the file directly, instead of returning a huge JSON for the whole model.
- Cameras: `Get3DProjectionSettings` reads the 3D window camera; saved views do not expose their camera in `API_NavigatorView`, so the command could optionally switch to each saved 3D view, read the projection, and restore the original window.

## Suggested schema
```json
{
  "filePath": "C:/export/model.obj",
  "format": "obj",
  "elements": [{"elementId": {"guid": "..."}}],
  "includeSurfaces": true,
  "includeTextureCoordinates": false,
  "cameras": "current" 
}
```
- `format`: `obj` first (with `.mtl` from surface colors), `gltf` later.
- `elements`: optional, whole model when omitted.
- `cameras`: `none`, `current` (3D window), or `savedViews` (the saved 3D views of the View Map), written to a JSON file next to the model (position, target, view cone).
- Output: file paths written, counts of bodies, vertices and faces.

## Notes
- Archicad is Z-up, glTF is Y-up: convert on write.
- Related risk: #762 (crash on element modification while a notification client is registered) would affect the automatic re-export loop.

Use case: architectural visualization office (Guadeloupe) modelling in Archicad 27 and rendering in Blender; we would test it on a real 4-villa project.

title: Live Archicad API coverage checklist (AC25–30, C and C++ API)
body:
## Preview

**Open the page from this branch:** https://raw.githack.com/parikshit99/tapir-archicad-automation/api-coverage-preview/docs/api-coverage/index.html

| Desktop (light) | Phone (dark) |
|---|---|
| ![Coverage page, desktop](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/parikshit99/tapir-archicad-automation/api-coverage-preview/previews/coverage-desktop.png) | ![Coverage page, phone](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/parikshit99/tapir-archicad-automation/api-coverage-preview/previews/coverage-phone.png) |

The preview is this PR's `index.html` with a data snapshot from 2026-10-18. Both live on the fork's `api-coverage-preview` branch, which is not part of this PR and will be deleted after merge. Statuses that come from live GitHub data (🚧 in an open PR, 🙋 claimed) show up only once the workflow runs here.

## What it is

A checklist of every item of the Archicad API in the AC25–AC30 DevKits, and whether Tapir uses it:

- every exported C `ACAPI_*` function, with the Archicad versions that have it;
- the names a function had before Archicad 27, and the AC25/26 command ids called through `ACAPI_Database`, `ACAPI_Environment`, `ACAPI_Navigator`, …, attached to their current names when the match is unambiguous;
- the whole C++ `ACAPI::`/`IFCAPI::` API (MEP, DesignOptions, IFC, Keynote, RoomBoundary and others): exported classes, their public member functions, and exported free functions.

Files:

- `tools/generate_api_coverage.py` builds the checklist (standard library only).
- `tools/fetch_api_coverage_github_data.py` reads the open PRs (title, and the lines they add under `archicad-addon/Sources/`) and open issues through the API.
- `tools/api_coverage_rules.json` lists what is not applicable, with a reason. Its `skip` section is where maintainers mark items they decide not to do.
- `.github/workflows/api_coverage.yml` keeps it live.
- `docs/api-coverage/index.html` is the page over the published JSON (see below).
- `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/archicad-api-request.yml` is the form for claiming open items. Each open item on the page links to it.
- `CLAUDE.md` documents all of the above.

## The page

- **Overview first:**
  - the share of applicable items used, as a headline number;
  - one tile per status (used, merged, in an open PR, claimed, open), and clicking a tile shows only that status;
  - a stacked progress bar with a legend.
- **By part of the API** (C, AC25/26 only, C++) and **by group:** each row has its % used, a progress bar and its open items. The group table sorts by most open items, lowest coverage or name, and shows 12 groups until "Show all".
- **Sidebar:**
  - links to the sections;
  - buttons for part of the API (All, C, AC25/26 only, C++) and Archicad version (Any, 25–30);
  - every group with its open items, where selecting a group filters the checklist to it.
- **Checklist:** groups with their own progress bars, and items rendered when a group is opened. It has a sticky bar with search and status filters.
- **Phones:** the sidebar is a "Sections" drawer, and the status filters are icons only, so the sticky bar stays short.

Progress uses one blue ordinal ramp, checked for light and dark mode. Claimed items are hatched.

## Today's numbers

Generated locally against `main` (`0111fe8`): **2,902 items; 742 of 2,434 applicable used (30 %); 468 not applicable.** With the latest release's (1.7.1) sources, the 742 used split into 492 used on `main` and released and 250 merged but not yet released.

| Part | Applicable | Used |
|---|---|---|
| C functions | 749 | 257 (34 %) |
| AC25/26-only C functions and command ids | 90 | 19 (21 %) |
| C++ API | 1,595 | 466 (29 %) |

The first workflow run adds the in-PR (🚧) and claimed (🙋) split from the live GitHub data.

## How each status is decided

- ✅ **done:** the name appears in `archicad-addon/Sources` on `main` and in the sources of the latest release tag.
- 🔀 **merged:** it appears on `main` but not in the latest release.
- 🚧 **in progress:** a line an open PR adds under `archicad-addon/Sources/` names it.
- 🙋 **claimed:** an open issue's title or body names it.
- ⛔ **skipped:** a maintainer listed it in the `skip` section of the rules, with a reason.
- ➖ **not applicable:** the `notApplicable` rules match it (UI, event handlers, licensing, memory management, add-on infrastructure).
- ⬜ **open:** none of the above.

`#define`s and inline wrappers in `MigrationHelper.hpp` count only when the code calls them; then the AC25/26 names they expand to count too.

## Known limits

- A used function may not expose every option of it as a JSON command.
- C++ member functions count as used by name inside files that use their class.
- PRs and issues created by the bots with `GITHUB_TOKEN` start no workflow, so they show up at the next hourly run.

## Workflow and security

`api_coverage.yml` runs on:

- a push to `main` and a published release;
- PR events (`pull_request_target`) and issue events;
- hourly, and by hand.

A newer run cancels an older one. It downloads the six DevKits once and caches only their headers (about 15 MB).

It publishes `api-coverage.json`, `api-coverage.md` and `api-coverage-summary.md` as a commit on a separate `api-coverage` branch and never commits to `main`. When the `API_COVERAGE_ISSUE` repository variable is set, it also writes the summary into that issue. `API_COVERAGE=false` turns it off.

If the push to `api-coverage` is refused, the run fails, unless a newer run moved the branch meanwhile.

**Security:** `pull_request_target` runs the workflow file from `main` with a write token. It always checks out `main` and never checks out or runs pull request code. It reads PRs only through the API and treats them as text.

**Checks run locally:**

- The generator ran twice over the six DevKits and gave identical output, about 1.5 s per run, with the full DevKits and with headers only.
- actionlint is clean on `api_coverage.yml`, and both YAML files and the rules JSON parse.
- The page was tested in headless Chromium at desktop width (light) and phone width (dark) against real generator output:
  - the tiles, the part, version and group filters, sorting, "Show all" and search;
  - the drawer;
  - no page errors.

This PR changes `.github/`, so `claude_auto_merge` skips it and a maintainer merges it.

## Maintainer steps after merge

1. Run **API Coverage** once by hand (Actions → API Coverage → Run workflow). This creates the `api-coverage` branch.
2. Optionally, create and pin a tracking issue, and set its number in the `API_COVERAGE_ISSUE` repository variable.
3. Check that the docs site serves `/api-coverage/`.

#1017 proposes using this data to file issues for open items.

The screenshots are rendered from this branch and stored on the fork's `api-coverage-preview` branch, which is not part of this PR.

## Why

The command reference is a long column of collapsed commands. There is no overview of the groups, a command's description only shows after you open it, and on a phone the only way to find a command is to scroll.

## What changes

- **Overview:** a table at the top lists every command group with its number of commands and its newest version, and links to the group.
- **Sidebar:**
  - links to the overview and to every group, with live counts;
  - a version filter ("Any", "1.7+", …: commands added in that version or later);
  - it highlights the group being read.
- **Sticky toolbar:**
  - a search over command names, descriptions and group names;
  - Expand all / Collapse all, which act on the visible commands only.

  It shows how many commands match, and each group heading, sidebar link and overview row shows "n of m" while filtering.
- **Descriptions visible:** each command shows its description (up to two lines) under its name without opening it.
- **Faster load:** a command's input/output schemas render when it is first opened, instead of all of them at page load.
- **Narrow screens and phones:** below 1150 px the sidebar is a drawer opened by "☰ Sections" in the toolbar; it closes after following a link, on Escape or on a click outside. Jumping to a group or command (sidebar, overview link or `#CommandName` link) lands below the sticky toolbar, using its real height, which follows the toolbar when it wraps.

Existing `#CommandName` links still open that command, and opening a command still updates the URL. Expand all / Collapse all don't touch the URL.

Only `index.html` (the sidebar container), `renderer.js` and `style.css` change. `tools/generate_addon_docs.py` and the weekly release only rewrite `command_definitions.js` and `common_schema_definitions.js`, so they are unaffected.

## Testing

I tested in headless Chromium at 1280 px (light) and 412 px (dark) against the docs on `main`:

- no page errors, all commands and groups rendered;
- no schemas rendered at load;
- search ("zone": 7 commands in 2 groups; nonsense: "No matching commands");
- the version filter;
- Expand all / Collapse all on a filtered list, with no history entries added;
- opening a single command sets the hash;
- `#CreateWalls` opens and renders it;
- the group links and the overview links land below the toolbar on both widths, including at widths where the status text wraps the toolbar (300–310 px, 540–620 px).

title: Show the live API coverage summary in the README
body:
Shows the Archicad API coverage summary on the project's main page. The README changes once, in this PR; after that it never needs editing when the coverage changes.

## How it works
`tools/generate_api_coverage.py` now writes three more files. `api_coverage.yml` publishes them to the `api-coverage` branch together with the checklist, so nothing is ever written to `main`:

- `api-coverage-badge.json`: a [shields.io endpoint](https://shields.io/badges/endpoint-badge) badge, for example `Archicad API coverage | 30 % (742/2434)`.
- `api-coverage.svg` / `api-coverage-dark.svg`: the summary as an image. It has the headline number, a bar for each status, and one row per part of the API (C functions, Archicad 25/26 only, C++ API). It uses the same color ramp as the coverage page.

The README points at these files on `raw.githubusercontent.com/…/api-coverage/…`:
- The badge sits in the badge row and links to the coverage page.
- A new "Archicad API coverage" section shows the image. A `<picture>` element switches to the dark image in GitHub's dark theme, and clicking the image opens the full checklist.

`raw.githubusercontent.com` serves SVG as `image/svg+xml` with `max-age=300`, so the README shows each new update within a few minutes.

## Also fixes the workflow's first publish
[The first run on `main`](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/actions/runs/39111621460) failed with `error: the following files have changes staged in the index`. When the `api-coverage` branch doesn't exist yet, the step creates an orphan branch, and `main`'s files are staged in it. `git rm -rq .` refuses to remove staged files, so the branch was never created. The step now uses `git rm -rqf .`.

## Testing
- Reproduced the `git rm -rq .` failure in a scratch repo and confirmed that `-rqf` fixes it.
- Ran the workflow's publish step against a local bare origin three times: the first run creates the branch with all six files, a rerun with the same data prints "The checklist did not change.", and a run with changed data adds a commit.
- Ran `write_outputs` on synthetic items with the counts from the last run (742 of 2434 used). `api-coverage-summary.md` is unchanged, and both SVGs parse as XML. I rendered both in Chromium, light and dark, and checked the layout.
- The README image and badge show as broken until this is merged and the workflow has published once; the push to `main` starts that run.

title: Refine API schemas following Tapir 1.7.1
body:
This PR introduces named schemas for distinct payloads and reuses shared definitions where commands describe the same contract.

| Area | Changes |
|---|---|
| Beam holes | Introduces `BeamHoleModification` and reuses `BeamHoleType`. Keeps modification inputs separate from read results, which include `holeId` and have different dimensional constraints. |
| Slab creation | Reuses `SlabStructureType`, preserving the rules for selecting a structure from supplied attributes, tool defaults or favorites. |
| Wall story links | Reuses `LinkToSettings`. Explains creation-time behavior on `newCreationMode`, with only placement and readback details retained at the relevant callers. |
| Teamwork reservations | Shares `User` across four reservation/status responses and enables access to common definitions in those commands. |
| Mesh modification | Introduces `MeshModificationData` for partial updates, preserving the existing wrapper and the distinction between omitted and supplied fields. |
| Revision custom schemes | Introduces `RevisionCustomSchemeEntry` for individual key/value pairs within the existing shared array. |

The mesh and revision extractions address older naming gaps. The remaining changes follow the Tapir 1.7.1 schema review.

Fields, requiredness, constraints and accepted JSON payloads remain unchanged. Generated clients may consolidate or rename previously inline types when adopting the named definitions.

title: API coverage: complete claim issues, and renamed C++ classes as one row
body:
Two fixes to the API coverage checklist, both found through #1057.

## Claim links open a complete issue (5651722)

The "claim" link opened the "Archicad API request" issue form with the item prefilled. The GitHub mobile app ignores issue forms, so a claim made there became an issue with a title and no body. Even on the web, the form left the request empty, and the issue bot, which has no DevKit, had no declaration to work from.

- `tools/generate_api_coverage.py` now records each item's declaration and header in `api-coverage.json`, taken from the newest DevKit that has the item. Statuses and the other outputs are unchanged.
- `docs/api-coverage/index.html`: the claim link now writes the issue body itself (only `title` + `body`, no template), using the form's `###` layout. The body holds the item, a request to expose it through a JSON command, its header, brief and older names, the declaration in a `cpp` block, and its Archicad versions.

## Renamed C++ classes are one row (cdb6d3a)

MEP's `Bend` (Archicad 27–28) is `Elbow` from Archicad 29, but the checklist listed them as unrelated rows. Claiming one of them asked for a command that works in only some versions.

Two classes are treated as one renamed class when all of these hold:
- one ends in a DevKit and the other, from the same module, starts in the next;
- they share at least two member functions, and at least half of all their member functions;
- neither has another such candidate.

Their shared members become one row under the new name, with the old name listed as an older name. So do free functions whose names differ only by the class name (`CreateBendDefault` → `CreateElbowDefault`). The ambiguous `PreferenceTableBase`, which matches two later classes, is left alone.

## Verification

Run over the six DevKits (headers only) with the 1.7.1 release sources:
- Base `6dfc87d` gives 2902 items (492/250/1692/468). This branch gives 2883 (491/250/1674/468), and two runs gave the same output.
- Exactly 19 rows fold into their Elbow rows: 11 `Bend::`, 5 `BendDefault::`, `CreateBendDefault`, `CreateBendUIManager` and `IsBend`. Those rows now cover versions 27–30 (or 28–30) and keep their statuses. No other row changed.
- Every item has a declaration and a header.
- In headless Chromium the page rendered 1674 claim links, the longest 1508 characters, with no page errors. A generated body (`Elbow::GetFactorRadius`) was checked by hand.

---

title: Claude bots: match the model to the job instead of always using best
body:
Fixes #991

Every Claude job ran with `--model best`, the most capable and most expensive model. This PR gives each job a tier read from a repository variable, so a maintainer can change it without a PR. The defaults are aliases, so each tier still follows new models as #713 intended.

| Tier | Variable (default) | Jobs |
|---|---|---|
| light | `CLAUDE_LIGHT_MODEL` (`sonnet`) | issue `reply`; PR re-reviews |
| regular | `CLAUDE_MODEL` (`opus`) | issue `fix`; the first review of a PR; steward fix rounds |
| escalation | `CLAUDE_ESCALATION_MODEL` (`best`) | the last steward fix round before `needs-maintainer`; one retry of an issue `fix` run that did work but left nothing |

## How each part works
- **Review:** a run is a re-review when a summary from an earlier review is already on the PR. Every summary ends with the `claude-review-resolve` marker, so the review looks for that. If the comments cannot be read, the run counts as a first review and uses the regular model.
- **Steward:** a new `escalate` dispatch input (boolean). The sweep sets it when round `rounds + 1` is the last one allowed by `BOT_PR_MAX_FIX_ROUNDS`.
- **Issue fix:**
  - A new `escalate` dispatch input, plus a `started_at` time and the run's turn count. The turn count is read from the `result` message in the action's `execution_file`.
  - A new plain-shell `escalate` job dispatches the run once more on the escalation model when all of these hold:
    - the run took more than one turn;
    - the issue is still open;
    - since the run started, the bot left no comment on the issue and no `claude/issue-<n>-*` PR was created or updated.
  - It does not retry:
    - a split issue whose parts all have a PR, because "post nothing" is the instructed outcome there;
    - the retry itself;
    - a run that ended on its first turn. That is the quota case from #977, as the issue warns.
- CLAUDE.md's CI section describes the tiers.

## Not included
- `--fallback-model`. Claude Code exits when the fallback model equals the main model, so setting `CLAUDE_MODEL=best` would break every run.
- A run that hits the job's 60-minute timeout is not escalated: the job is cancelled before the turn count step runs.

## Things to know
- The light tier now covers the `reply` job. That job can also write fixes when a comment asks for one, and those fixes would now be written by Sonnet. The same goes for re-reviews after a push, whose clean verdict feeds auto-merge on the bot's PRs. If either turns out too weak, set `CLAUDE_LIGHT_MODEL=opus`.
- Only `.github/` and CLAUDE.md change, so `claude_auto_merge` will not merge this PR; it needs a manual merge.
- This PR touches the same sweep lines as #996. Whichever merges second has a small conflict: keep #996's `countRuns` arguments together with `startFix`.

## Testing
- `actionlint` passes on the three workflows, and `yaml.safe_load` parses them.
- I ran the jq for the turn count against sample execution files: `121` for a max-turns result, `0` with no result message.
- I ran the comment, PR and split-part checks against the live data of #933 (4 parts, 4 PRs: no retry).
- The workflows themselves have not run; the first issue, review and steward runs after merging will show the model they used in their logs.

---

title: Community test runner: setup wizard, window, recorder and brief output for Claude
body:
Follow-up to #887: makes the community test runner easier to set up and use, and lets Claude Code drive it cheaply.

## For testers

- **`setup`**: finds the installed Archicads and their stock templates, and shows which Tapir each one loads. It opens GitHub's token page, checks the token and keeps it in Windows Credential Manager, so no environment variable is needed. It suggests trusting your own fork and writes the configuration to `%LOCALAPPDATA%\TapirRunner\runner.json`. It can optionally open the window at logon. `--yes` asks nothing.
- **No more moving Tapir out of Program Files.** A test loads the pull request's build through Archicad's add-on list (`HKCU\…\Add-On Manager\Include` / `Disable`): the build is added and every other Tapir is left out. Afterwards both lists are written back exactly as they were. The previous lists are saved to a file first, so after a crash or a power cut the next run, or `restore`, puts them back. Configurations with `addonFile` still swap that file, as before.
- **`gui`**: a window listing the open pull requests with their checks, builds and last results. It can test the selected ones or everything due, pause the automatic pass, stop after the current test, and put your add-on back. A log shows what happens.
- **`record`**: a port (19800) that passes commands on to Archicad and writes a check from them. Guids are saved as `${g1}`…, and the answers' values become expectations. You don't need to write JSON paths by hand.
- `check` and `trial` default to this checkout's `archicad-addon/Test/checks`. The port is found per Archicad process (netstat), so another open Archicad is never sent anything.

## For Claude Code (fewest tokens)

- **`--brief`** prints one line per pull request and version, plus at most five failures: `#869 AC30 FAIL 10/12 build bf11c1e tapir 1.7.2` and `  x check / step / what: actual (want …)`.
- **`prs`** gives one line per open pull request: its branch or fork, commit, labels, checks, built versions and last results.
- **`test`** takes `869 870`, `--all`, `--ac 30`, `--every-check` (the whole check folder, for PRs without their own checks), `--no-post` and `--retest`. Exit codes are 0 for passed or skipped, 1 for a failed check, and 2 when the runner stopped.
- **The skill** `claude-skill/tapir-pr-test/SKILL.md` can be installed with `setup --install-claude-skill`, and CLAUDE.md points to it.

## Robustness

- A crash during the checks, or an Archicad that does not quit, becomes a row of the report; the results are no longer lost. A crash while quitting is shown as a warning.
- Teardown steps that use a value an earlier failed step never saved are skipped. Before, the whole run stopped with a `KeyError`; this happened with `graphic_override_structured_criterion.json` on a Tapir without those commands.
- The crash reporter (GSReport) in the Archicad folder no longer counts as "Archicad is running".
- GitHub's rate limit and a missing token give clear messages.
- `trustedForks` lets fork pull requests be tested from named owners only; `allowForks` still trusts all forks.

## Testing

- 19 unit tests (10 existing, 9 new): the add-on list install and restore against a fake registry (including from a new process), URL round trips, the recorder's steps and a replay of a recorded check, the brief output and fork trust.
- On Archicad 30 (Windows):
  - `setup --yes` found AC28–AC30, their templates and the Tapir each loads.
  - `trial` with the 1.7.0 release build ran 61 checks in 1 min 42 s and reported exactly the issues still open in 1.7.0 (#425, #749). The add-on list was identical before and after.
  - A start stuck at Archicad's project-recovery dialog and an interrupted run were both put back by `restore`.
  - `record` was replayed with `check`, and the window opens.
- On that machine, Archicad 30 crashed on every quit, even with no checks run. The report shows this as a warning, and the add-on is still put back.
- Not verified: posting results end to end (no PR is labelled `needs-test` yet), and macOS (`setup` and the add-on list are Windows only).

body:
### API functions

ACAPI_AutoText_GetAutoTextKeys
ACAPI_AutoText_InterpretAutoText

### What should Tapir let you do?

**Use case**
We build title blocks (Plankopf) on master layouts with `CreateTexts` and Autotext keys in the text (`<LAYOUTID>`, `<DRAWINGSCALE>`, `<PROJECTNUMBER>` … work). The drawing date comes from a Layout-Info custom field ("Erstellungsdatum", Layout Book > Layout Settings > Layout-Info). In the UI it is *Insert Autotext > Layout > Erstellungsdatum*. Through the API we cannot find its key.

**What we have today** (Archicad 29 AUT, Tapir 1.7.1)
- `GetAutoTextKeys` calls `ACAPI_AutoText_GetPropertyAutoTextKeyTable` only (ProjectCommands.cpp), so it returns `PROPERTY-…` keys (97 in our project), no layout, system or Layout-Info keys.
- `GetLayoutSettings` returns the field: `"customData":[{"customSchemeKey":"BA896E94-CCC8-4B57-B621-5CAC263BD1CA","customSchemeValue":"11.08.2026","customSchemeName":"Erstellungsdatum"}]`
- Guessed keys in `CreateTexts` on that layout, read back with `GetDetailsOfElements`:

| text sent | resolved |
|---|---|
| `<LAYOUTID>` (control) | `200.01` |
| `<autotext-BA896E94-CCC8-4B57-B621-5CAC263BD1CA>` | `####` |
| `<BA896E94-…>`, `<LAYOUTCUSTOM-BA896E94-…>`, `<CUSTOM-BA896E94-…>` | literal, not resolved |

**Request**
1. `ACAPI_AutoText_GetAutoTextKeys` (all keys and their values), e.g. as an option of `GetAutoTextKeys`, so we can see which key strings Archicad has besides `PROPERTY-…`.
2. `ACAPI_AutoText_InterpretAutoText` as a command, e.g. `InterpretAutoText {"autoText": "<LAYOUTID>", "elementId": {...}}` → the resolved value in the context of that element/layout. Then we can test a key before we write it into a title block, without creating test texts.

We do not know yet whether `ACAPI_AutoText_GetAutoTextKeys` lists the Layout-Info fields; these two functions would tell us.

title: Expose ACAPI_ModelAccess_GetConnectionTable (contact surfaces between elements, to check wall joins)
body:
### API functions

ACAPI_ModelAccess_GetConnectionTable

### What should Tapir let you do?

**Use case**
We check by script that walls are joined correctly after we create or move them (L and T corners, composite exterior walls 25 cm concrete + 20 cm ETICS). Today we compare reference lines and floor-plan polygons ourselves. We would like Archicad's own answer: which elements touch, and along which surface.

**What we tried** (Archicad 29 AUT, Tapir 1.7.1, test copy, read-only)
- `GetConnectedElements` returns hosted elements (windows of a wall, CW/stair/railing parts), not wall-to-wall contacts.
- `GetCollisions` on two 45 cm walls that are joined end to end in an L corner (reference lines meet exactly, angle 90°):
  ```json
  {"elementsGroup1":[{"elementId":{"guid":"45EDC17D-1FED-4FF7-A5A4-89953ABEC9D0"}}],
   "elementsGroup2":[{"elementId":{"guid":"89BEC9B9-E51D-45B2-8EC4-579C9C97CB84"}}],
   "settings":{"volumeTolerance":0.001,"performSurfaceCheck":true,"surfaceTolerance":0.001}}
  → {"collisions":[{"hasBodyCollision":true,"hasClearenceCollision":false}]}
  ```
  Same for a second L pair, and the same with `performSurfaceCheck: false`. So `GetCollisions` reports a collision for a correct join and gives no geometry: we cannot tell a clean join from an overlap or a gap.

**Request**
`ACAPI_ModelAccess_GetConnectionTable` (Archicad 28+), e.g. `GetConnectionTable {"elements": [...]}` → pairs of element ids with the connecting polygons (and their area). We expect that the contact face lets us tell a clean join from a gap or an overlap, but we have not seen this function's output yet.

### Declarations from the DevKit (optional)

```cpp

// elementList [in]: list of API_Guids, referencing elements from the active sight. Archicad will search connections among these elements.
// connectionTable [out]: pairs of element IDs as keys and an array of polygons representing the connecting surface between the respective pair of elements.
```

title: ModifyTexts fails or drops lines when the text starts with a Project Info Autotext key followed by a newline
body:
Archicad 29 AUT, Tapir 1.7.1, a Text on a layout (test copy, deleted afterwards). Before each row the text was reset with `ModifyTexts` `"text": "reset"` (success), then:

| `text` sent to ModifyTexts | result | text read back (GetDetailsOfElements) |
|---|---|---|
| `<PROJECTNUMBER> <SHORTDATE>` | success | `WKL519 18/10/2026` |
| `Zeile1\n<PROJECTNUMBER>` | success | `Zeile1\nWKL519` |
| `<SHORTDATE>\n<PROJECTNUMBER>` | success | `18/10/2026\nWKL519` |
| `<PROJECTNUMBER>\nZeile2` | error -2130312696 "Failed to modify the Text." | `reset` (unchanged) |
| `<PROJECTNUMBER>\n<SHORTDATE>` | error -2130312696 | `reset` (unchanged) |
| `<PROJECTNAME>\n<PROJECTNUMBER>` | success | `Wohnbebauung mit 5 Wohneinheiten\rin Kreuzbergl` (the `<PROJECTNUMBER>` line is missing; our project name contains a line break) |

`CreateTexts` with the same `<PROJECTNAME>\n<PROJECTNUMBER>` works: `Wohnbebauung mit 5 Wohneinheiten\rin Kreuzbergl\rWKL519`.

So it seems to fail when the FIRST line is a Project Info key and a newline follows (`<SHORTDATE>` first is fine, a key after a plain first line is fine). Cause unknown.

**Expected:** the same result as `CreateTexts` with the same text.

Related: #1092 (point 4), where this was first seen.

title: Community test runner: read the pull request list in parallel, say why it waits
body:
Follow-up to #1088 (this commit was pushed just after #1088 was merged).

## Problem

With 100 open pull requests, the runner's window looked stuck on "Reading pull requests ...". To fill the list it made three or four GitHub requests per pull request (changed files, the build check run, its artifacts, the comments), one after another. That took about three minutes, with no progress shown, and happened again after every pass.

An automatic pass with nothing to do also finished silently. Today no pull request is labelled `needs-test`, and while Archicad is open nothing is tested at all, so the window gave no sign of what it was doing.

## Change

- **`pull_rows`:**
  - The list appears at once from the single listing call.
  - Each row's details are filled in by eight parallel workers, about 30 s for 100 pull requests.
  - An optional `on_row` callback reports progress.
- **The window:**
  - Rows show `...` until their details arrive, and the top line counts up (`Reading pull requests 43/100 ...`).
  - Every refresh and pass ends with one sentence in the log, for example: *100 open pull request(s), 0 marked 'needs-test' for you to test - automatic testing has nothing to do until a developer marks one (you can still select a row and click Test selected). Archicad 30 is open: tests wait until you close it.*
  - A pass that tested nothing no longer re-reads the whole list, which would otherwise use about 400 requests every 15 minutes.
- **GUIDE.md:** the troubleshooting section now starts with "Nothing seems to happen".

## Testing

- The 19 unit tests pass.
- Against GitHub: 100 rows in 29.0 s, before about 3 minutes.
- In the window, launched with `Start Tapir Test Runner.bat`: rows appear immediately, the count goes up to 100/100, and the sentence above appears with Archicad 30 open.
