title: Community test runner: loading the build through the add-on list fails on AC26 and AC28 (GER)
body:
The runner from #1088 loads a test build by editing Archicad's add-on list in the registry (`HKCU\Software\GRAPHISOFT\Archicad\Archicad <v> GER R1\Add-On Manager\Include` and `\Disable`). On this machine that does not work for AC26 (GER, build 7004) or AC28 (GER, build 7006), Windows 11: Archicad starts with the dialog "Archicad-Umgebung: Einige Add-Ons konnten nicht geladen werden" (some add-ons could not be loaded), and Tapir is not loaded - the port answers, `GetAddOnVersion` does not.

`trial` then waits at that dialog until `startTimeout`. `restore` puts both lists back correctly afterwards (checked value by value).

What I tried on AC26, Archicad closed between each, lists restored after each:

| Include | Disable | Result |
|---|---|---|
| unchanged | the regular Tapir (`...\Add-Ons\Sonstiges\TapirAddOn_AC26_Win.apx`) | starts normally, no Tapir - as expected |
| + the build's file (`lan.flat:///C:/Users/.../TapirRunner/builds/AC26/TapirAddOn_AC26_Win.apx`) | the regular Tapir | dialog, no Tapir |
| + the build's folder | the regular Tapir | dialog, no Tapir |

The same with the official 1.7.1 `.apx` as the "build", so it is not the build. The values have the same type (String) and URL form as the entries Archicad writes itself; the file has no Zone.Identifier. AC28 behaves the same.

My guess, unverified: Archicad up to 28 recognises an add-on by its identity (MDID), not by its path, so the same Tapir on `Disable` (regular path) and `Include` (runner path) collides. #1088 was tested on AC30 INT. If someone has AC29/AC30 at hand, the same experiment there would tell whether this is version dependent.

Workaround: a configuration with `addonFile` (the file swap of the first runner version) works on both, with administrator rights for Program Files. That is how #750 and #751 were tested today.

Found while setting up the runner; the other setup problems are fixed in #1151.
author: weltmaister

title: Community test runner: localized Windows and Archicad (templates, backups, netstat), stair check
body:
Three things that stopped the community test runner on a German Windows with German Archicads (AC26 and AC28, GER). Each one is language or install specific; none shows up on an English system.

**1. `setup` found no template.** The stock templates are in `<Archicad>\Grundeinstellungen\Archicad\` on a German Archicad, not `Defaults\Archicad\`. `setup` printed "NO TEMPLATE FOUND" and wrote no Archicad into the configuration, so the runner had nothing to test. The layout below that folder is the same in every language, so it now looks in `*/Archicad/*.tpl`.

**2. Backup copies counted as loaded Tapirs.** A file like `TapirAddOn_AC26_Win.apx.bak-153` next to the add-on was listed by `setup` and put on the `Disable` list. Only `.apx`/`.bundle` files count now.

**3. `trial` never found Archicad's port.** `netstat` prints the socket state in the system language (`ABHÖREN` instead of `LISTENING`), so `ports_of` found no port and every start waited the whole `startTimeout` (300 s) for an Archicad that was already answering, then stopped with "did not answer with Tapir loaded". A listening socket is now the one without a foreign address (`0.0.0.0:0` or `[::]:0`), which is the same in every language.

**Also: the stair check compared riser counts that one template clamps.** Archicad clamps `stepNum` to the stair rules of the project's defaults. At a going of 0.25 and 2.75 m the German AC26 template allows up to 16 risers, the INT template of AC28 only 15, so 15 and 16 risers gave the same run (3.75 m) and `create_stairs_tread_depth.json` failed on AC28 although #750 works. Measured with the #750 build: AC26 3.90 / 4.15 / 4.40 / 4.40 m, AC28 3.50 / 3.75 / 3.75 / 3.75 m for 14-17 risers. It compares 14 and 15 risers now, inside the range of both.

**And: the result line names the language.** Checks run on every language version, each with its own template and defaults, so two testers can get different results without Tapir being at fault (the stair clamp above). The first line now reads `tapir-test: AC28 GER PASS 61/61 build … tapir …` (from `GetProductInfo`'s `languageCode`); it still starts with `AC28 `, so `already_reported` recognises earlier reports. The README's *Writing checks* asks authors to send every value a result depends on and to prefer differences over absolute values.

Tests: three new unit tests (localized defaults folder, backup copies, a German `netstat` output); all 22 pass. On the machine itself, with these fixes: `setup --yes` finds both Archicads and their templates, and `trial` on AC26 and AC28 runs the whole cycle (swap, start, 61 checks, quit, restore) - the results are on #750 and #751.

Not covered here: loading the build through Archicad's add-on list does not work on these AC26/AC28 installations - see #1150. These runs used a configuration with `addonFile` (the file swap).

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
author: weltmaister

title: Community test runner: file swap on Archicad 25-28 with Tapir in the Add-Ons folder; stop at a start dialog (#1150)
body:
Follows up #1150 (cause confirmed there): Archicad up to 28 does not load an add-on from the add-on list while the same add-on is on `Disable` at its usual place. It shows "some add-ons could not be loaded" and loads neither. The Tapir Installer puts Tapir into the `Add-Ons` folder, so on AC25–28 that is the normal case, and the runner waited out the whole `startTimeout` at that dialog.

**(a) Archicad 25–28 with Tapir in the `Add-Ons` folder uses the file swap**
- `setup` sets `addonFile` for such an Archicad and says it needs administrator rights.
- A configuration without it (written by an earlier `setup`) stops before touching anything, with a message naming `addonFile` and #1150.
- The file swap says plainly when administrator rights are missing, instead of a `PermissionError` traceback.
- Only for AC ≤ 28 (`COLLIDES_UP_TO`). **AC29 is not tested**; the add-on list worked on AC30 (#1088), and AC30 keeps using it. A Tapir that is only in the add-on list (no file in `Add-Ons`) keeps using the list on every version.

**(b) A dialog during the start stops the runner within seconds**
A modal dialog of the Archicad process, found by window class (`DGModalDlgClass`, or `#32770` for system dialogs) so it works in every language, seen in three polls in a row (10 s and more) while waiting for Tapir stops the start and names the dialog. This covers project recovery and licence dialogs too.

**Tested** on Windows 11, AC26 (GER) and AC28 (GER), together with #1151 (needed on a German Windows to find the port at all):
- A normal `trial` with the check, file swap, all 61 checks: AC28 59/61 in 156 s, AC26 59/61 in 170 s, not stopped (the two failures are #425, not in this build). The #1150 experiment logged every window of the Archicad process every 5 s through two normal starts: no modal dialog at any point.
- `setup --yes`: sets `addonFile` for both, with the note.
- `trial` with a list configuration: stops after 1 s with the message; registry export byte-identical before and after, no backup left.
- `trial` with `addonFile`, not elevated: the administrator message, nothing changed.
- The old list behaviour forced on AC26 to provoke the dialog: stopped after 51 s with two polls, now three (Archicad needs ~40 s to show it) with `Archicad 26 shows a dialog ('Archicad-Umgebung') …` instead of 300 s; the dialog closed, `restore` put the list back (registry byte-identical).
- Unit tests: 6 new (collision → refuse without changing the registry, AC30 unaffected, Tapir only in the list still uses the list, a list left pending by #1150, several Tapirs in the folder, dialog stop after three polls, administrator message); 25 pass on this branch.

The two PRs touch the same files but merge without conflicts in either order.

title: Bot PR reviews: always record a verdict, and stop re-dispatching empty reviews
body:
Since 7ca0b2c (#1078) moved re-reviews to the light model, no re-review has recorded a verdict. Each run succeeds after two to five turns (`refused: false`) and posts nothing, so the `verdict` job is skipped. This holds for every successful dispatched review in the last 40 runs, on #675, #676, #743, #750, #751, #756, #761, #763, #813, #825, #826, #827 and #649. It also happens on a push: this PR's own re-review of 91b1c95 ran 2 turns and posted nothing, although the prompt only allows silence when a comment started the run. First reviews, on `opus`, post as before (this PR's first review did). Before the change, the dispatched re-reviews on #813 posted `blocking` and `clean`.

The action hides the model's output, so the cause isn't visible yet. It points to the light model rather than the prompt alone.

The steward made it worse: it only waits after a *failed* run, so it re-dispatched the same empty review on every sweep, sometimes four minutes apart (five on #813 between 16:22 and 16:47 on Oct 18). That burns the usage limit. This morning, ten such reviews handed #813 over as "ten reviews recorded no verdict".

## Changes
- **Review prompt** (`claude_pr_review.yml`):
  - A run started by a comment may still post nothing when nothing is new.
  - Every other run (a push, or a dispatched run with no comment) **always** posts the summary with both markers, even when nothing changed.
- **Diagnosis** (`claude_pr_review.yml`): after every run, the log shows which model ran, the permission denials, and the final message (first 1,500 characters, tokens redacted). The next silent re-review will show why it stopped.
- **Steward wait** (`claude_bot_pr_steward.yml`):
  - After a review of the current head that left no verdict, the next review waits for the next hourly sweep (50 minutes), as after a failed run. An empty review now costs one run an hour, not one per sweep.
  - Reviews of an earlier head don't hold back a new head's first review.
- **Steward cap:** silent reviews count per head commit, since its push (or since `needs-maintainer` was last removed), and three of them hand the pull request over. Before, it was ten over the pull request's whole life, which a pull request with several fix rounds can reach legitimately.
- **CLAUDE.md:** the usage-limit bullet mentions the new wait.

## Until the cause is known
Setting the repository variable `CLAUDE_LIGHT_MODEL` to `opus` brings re-reviews back to the model that records verdicts. This needs no code change, and the workflow header already suggests it if re-reviews turn out too shallow.

## Testing
- `actionlint` (with shellcheck) on both workflows reports only the 4 info-level SC2016 notes that are already on `main`.
- Every `run` step passes `bash -n`.
- I ran the steward's `failedRecently` itself (with a stub `gh` that calls the API) against #813's real runs:
  - head pushed after the 11:48 review → start;
  - head pushed before it → wait;
  - only failed runs counted → start;
  - a PR with no runs → start.
  The no-runs case printed `null` before the `// empty` fix, which would have broken the sweep.
- The new log lines, on sample results (normal, token-bearing, empty): they print the expected values and redact the token.

Once this is merged, `needs-maintainer` can come off #813.

title: Discord bot: one 👀 checkpoint per channel, consecutive messages as one report
body:
Two changes to the Discord issue bot, plus a way to remove the 👀 reactions the old version left behind.

**One 👀 per channel.** Until now the bot put a 👀 on every message it classified as not actionable. Now each channel carries a single 👀, on the last message the bot checked, and the next run continues with the messages after it.
- The 👀 moves after every checked report, not only at the end of a run, so a run cut off by the job timeout keeps its progress.
- The new mark goes on before the old one comes off. If adding it fails, the old checkpoint stays.
- When a message has to wait for the next run (issue cap reached, duplicate search failed, issue creation failed), the scan of that channel stops there. The next run starts from that message, so nothing gets classified twice.
- When the classifier gives no usable answer for a message, the bot tries the next one. If that one also fails, the classifier is down and the scan stops at the first. If the next one gets an answer, the first message is skipped and listed on the borderline-reports issue, so one bad message can't hold up a channel.

**Consecutive messages from one author count as one report.** They are classified together and filed as one issue that quotes all of them. The reply and the ✅ go on the first message, and the 👀 goes on the last. The newest run of messages is left for the next scan while its last message is under 10 minutes old, because its author may still be typing.

**Removing the old 👀 reactions.**
- Regular runs remove older 👀 marks from the messages they scan (the last 24 hours).
- The new **cleanup seen marks** workflow input removes the bot's 👀 from each channel's entire history (up to 20,000 messages per channel). It keeps the newest one as the checkpoint and then exits without classifying anything. It also works with **dry run**, which only reports what it would remove.

**One-time trade-off when this is deployed:** the first run treats the newest old 👀 as the checkpoint. A message the old version had left unmarked for a retry, and that sits before that 👀, won't be retried. The old version only did that when it hit the issue limit or a failed classification or search, and it already dropped such messages after 24 hours.

Docs updated: the script's docstring, the README and the workflow header.

**Tests:** 16 new offline tests, covering grouping, merging, checkpoint moves, the cases where the scan stops (classifier down, failed search, issue cap), a single message the classifier can't answer, a failed add, the 10-minute wait for an unfinished run, dry run and the history cleanup. All 53 tests in `test_discord_issue_bot` pass.

title: Grasshopper: Add visual components for SearchProperties, SearchFavorites, and GetElementsByCriteria
body:
### Summary
With the addition of server-side search and criteria evaluation in the Tapir Add-On (`SearchProperties`, `SearchFavorites`, and `GetElementsByCriteria`), these endpoints are currently available via JSON and Python.

We propose adding matching visual components to the Grasshopper plugin under `TapirGrasshopperPlugin`:
1. **Search Properties Component**: Input keyword/group, outputs matching property GUIDs, names, and groups.
2. **Search Favorites Component**: Input keyword/element type, outputs matching favorite names and folder paths.
3. **Get Elements by Criteria Component**: Input element types, floor indices, and property criteria list; outputs matching element instances and count.

### Motivation
Allows computational designers in Rhino/Grasshopper to filter large Archicad models by story/property criteria without stalling Grasshopper canvases on large unprojected element geometry downloads.

### What should Tapir let you do?

Expose all 642 C++ MEP API (`ACAPI::MEP::`) functions that are still open on the [API coverage checklist](https://enzyme-apd.github.io/tapir-archicad-automation/api-coverage/) (group C++ MEPAPI; the other 354 are done) through Tapir JSON commands, in the existing MEP command group: a new option of an existing MEP command where one fits (most getters belong in the existing MEP element / preference table reads), otherwise a new command. Their parameters become the command's input and their results the response.

Suggested split (one PR per part):
1. **Routing elements and nodes** — RoutingElement, RoutingSegment, RoutingNode, their `*Default`s and modifiers (`Inject`, `PickUpDefault`, `Modify`), the `Create*Default` functions, `CollectAllMEPElements`.
2. **Segments and fittings** — RigidSegment, FlexibleSegment, Bend, Elbow, Branch, Transition, TakeOff, Accessory, Equipment, Terminal, Fitting, ElementBase/ElementDefault/ModifiableElement, with their defaults.
3. **Ports** — PortBase, PortDefaultBase, PipingPort, VentilationPort, CableCarrierPort and their defaults.
4. **Duct preference tables** — DuctBranch/DuctCircularSegment/DuctRectangularSegment/DuctElbow/DuctTransition preference tables, PreferenceTableBase, PreferenceTableContainerBase, AngleSetBase, ReferenceSetBase, the `Get*PreferenceTableContainer` functions.
5. **Pipe and cable carrier preference tables** — PipeBranch/PipeSegment/PipeElbow/PipeTransition and CableCarrierSegment preference tables.
6. **Systems, electrical and calculation** — PhysicalSystem, DistributionSystem, DistributionSystemsGraph(TreeNode), SystemGroup, ElectricalDevice, ElectricalPanel(Default), ElectricalProjectSettings, `IsElectricalCircuit`, GraphCalculationInterface, ICalculationResultColumn, `GetMEPModelCheckTypeId`, `GetLocalizedElemTypeName`, `FromAttributeEnum`.

Some of these may not fit a JSON command: the `*UIManager` classes and `Create*UIManager` (they convert to and from `TBUI::IAPIToolUIData` of a tool settings dialog), and `RegisterCalculationCallback` / `SystemBrowserCalculationCallbackInterface` / `GraphCalculationInterface` (add-on callbacks). Expose what makes sense and, for the rest, say in the PR why they cannot be JSON commands, so a maintainer can move them to the `notApplicable` section of `tools/api_coverage_rules.json`.

### Declarations from the DevKit (optional)

Left out: with 642 functions they do not fit in an issue (GitHub limits the body to 65,536 characters). The declaration of each function is on the API coverage checklist (expand the C++ MEPAPI group) and in `api-coverage.json` on the `api-coverage` branch (the `declaration` and `header` of each item).

### Archicad versions you need it in

27, 28, 29, 30

Not every function exists in every version: the ones without a version after them in the list exist in AC27–30, the others only in the versions named (guard with `ServerMainVers_*` / `AC_VERSION` checks).

title: Auto merge: evaluate every open PR; steward: larger batches and model cap
body:
## Why open PRs were not auto merged

**Auto Merge only ever saw the newest 30 pull requests.** `claude_auto_merge.yml` lists its candidates with `gh pr list --state open --base main` and no `--limit`. `gh` returns 30 by default, so the latest run's log covers exactly #1294 to #1239. Every older PR was never evaluated. That includes the five the steward reports as "green and reviewed - waiting for claude_auto_merge.yml": #763, #998, #1000, #1003 and #1005.

The steward's own list uses `--limit 200`, and 209 PRs are open now, so it already drops the oldest ones.

**The bot PR backlog grows faster than the steward clears it.** About 90 bot PRs were "left for a later sweep" in the last run, because a sweep starts new work on only 5.

## Changes

- `claude_auto_merge.yml`: the candidate list now uses `--limit 1000`.
- `claude_bot_pr_steward.yml`:
  - Its PR list now uses `--limit 1000`.
  - `BOT_PR_SWEEP_BATCH` default goes from 5 to **15**.
  - The sweep's timeout goes from 15 to **30** minutes. A PR the sweep starts work on, or has to wait for, costs about 30 seconds (the last sweep took 9 minutes for 5), so a full batch of 15 would overrun 15 minutes.
- `CLAUDE_MAX_RUNS` default goes from 4 to **8**. It is changed in all four "Wait for a model slot" steps (issue triage ×2, PR review, steward fix) and in the issue triage header.
- `CLAUDE.md` is updated with the new defaults.

- If the repository variables `BOT_PR_SWEEP_BATCH` or `CLAUDE_MAX_RUNS` are set, they still override these defaults.
- A higher model cap uses up the subscription's usage limit faster (#977). Refused runs are still retried by the existing `retry` job and steward logic.
- This touches `.github/`, so Auto Merge will not merge it. It needs a manual merge.
- The bot PRs that are now green still wait out `BOT_AUTO_MERGE_DELAY_HOURS` (72h) from their review's success, so the first merges are around Oct 21–22.

title: Get3DGeometryOfElements returns no bodies for Columns and Beams
body:
`Get3DGeometryOfElements` (new in 1.7.2) answers a Column or a Beam with an empty `bodies` list and no error, while a Slab or a Wall in the same call returns its body. The 3D model of a column or a beam belongs to its segments, and `CollectBodiesOfSubelements` in `ElementCommands.cpp` only collects the subelements of Stairs, Railings and Curtain Walls.

**To reproduce** (Tapir 1.7.2, Archicad 30 and 29, new project from the template)

1. Create a column and a beam:
   - `CreateColumns` with `{"columnsData": [{"coordinates": {"x": 0, "y": 0, "z": 0}}]}`
   - `CreateBeams` with `{"beamsData": [{"begCoordinate": {"x": 0, "y": 5}, "endCoordinate": {"x": 5, "y": 5}, "zCoordinate": 3}]}`
2. Call `Get3DGeometryOfElements` with both.

Result: `{"geometries3D": [{"bodies": []}, {"bodies": []}]}`. Nothing tells the caller that these elements were not handled, so the answer reads as "no geometry".

**Workaround:** pass the segments instead. `GetSubelementsOfHierarchicalElements` returns them as `columnSegments` and `beamSegments`, and `Get3DGeometryOfElements` answers each segment with its body, a slanted column included.

**Suggested fix:** add `API_ColumnID` and `API_BeamID` to the type check in `CollectBodiesOfSubelements` and collect `memo.columnSegments` and `memo.beamSegments` the same way as the stair and railing parts.

### What should Tapir let you do?

Expose all 284 C++ Archicad API (`ACAPI::`, group C++ ArchicadAPI) functions that are still open on the [API coverage checklist](https://enzyme-apd.github.io/tapir-archicad-automation/api-coverage/) through Tapir JSON commands, in the command group each belongs to: a new option of an existing command where one fits, otherwise a new command. Their parameters become the command's input and their results the response. The rest of the group is already done, in progress or claimed (Favorites: #1231, #1232, #1252; Library and GSM objects: #1217, #1219, #1220, #1222, #1223, #1249, #1250, #1265; zone labeling: #1156; opening: #959), so build on those commands where they overlap.

Suggested split (one PR per part):
1. **Openings** — `ACAPI::Element::Opening`, `OpeningDefault`, `OpeningGeometry`/`ModifiableOpeningGeometry`, `OpeningExtrusionParameters`/`ModifiableOpeningExtrusionParameters` (AC29–30 element commands, next to #959's opening reads).
2. **Opening floor plan parameters** — `OpeningFloorPlanParameters` / `ModifiableOpeningFloorPlanParameters`.
3. **GSM objects, part 1** — the open `ACAPI::Library::GSMObject` getters (next to #1220/#1223/#1250).
4. **GSM objects, part 2 and the library manager** — the open `GSMObject` modifiers, `LibraryManager`, `Library`, `LibraryTreePath`, `LibPart`.
5. **Favorites** — the open `ACAPI::Favorite` functions (create, change, rename, move folder, import/export, list all or by element type, preview image).
6. **Everything else** — Cutaway (cutting planes, 3D cutaway), LicenseInfo (product version info), ZoneLabelingSettings, `ElementBase`/`ElementDefault`, `IsDomainAvailable`, `GetCEIPProjectID`, `UniqueID::GetToken`, Tracking.

Some of these may not fit a JSON command: the add-on plumbing (`CallUndoableCommand`, `CallUndoableModifier`, `CallNotUndoableModifier`, `CallDefaultModifier`, `ExecuteUndoableScope`, `ExecuteNotUndoableScope`, `Err`, `CreateInputHandler`, `AddonServiceInterface`, `AttributeManagerImportCallback`) and the model check callbacks (`GetModelCheckManager`, `ModelCheckManager::RegisterGroup`, `ModelCheckMethodCallback`, `ModelCheckResult`). Use the plumbing where it helps and, for whatever cannot be a command, say in the PR why, so a maintainer can move it to the `notApplicable` section of `tools/api_coverage_rules.json`.

### What should Tapir let you do?

`GetIFCPropertiesOfElements` returns the property sets mapped by the preview export translator, but some IFC data is not available through Tapir:

1. **IFC attributes** (Name, Description, ObjectType, Tag, PredefinedType, LongName…). Please add a `GetIFCAttributesOfElements` command based on `PropertyAccessor::GetAttributes`, returning `name`, `value` (null when empty) and `valueType` for each attribute.
2. **Value types of IFC properties.** Values are only returned as strings. Please add to each item of `GetIFCPropertiesOfElements`, keeping `value` unchanged:
   - `valueType` (`Value::GetType`, e.g. `IfcLengthMeasure`),
   - `propertyType` (SingleValue / ListValue / BoundedValue / EnumeratedValue / TableValue),
   - `source` (preview / local).
3. **IFC classification references.** Please add a `GetIFCClassificationReferencesOfElements` command based on `GetPreviewClassificationReferences` / `GetLocalClassificationReferences`, returning for each reference:
   - identification, name, location and description,
   - referencedSource (name, source, edition),
   - source (preview / local).

They should also work for subelements (curtain wall panels, stair and railing parts), as `GetIFCPropertiesOfElements` does. Archicad 28+; an error item on older versions is fine.

title: GetIFCExportTranslators marks the wrong translator as preview
body:
Archicad 29, Tapir 1.7.2.

GetIFCExportTranslators returns `"preview": true` for the first translator returned by
ACAPI_IFC_GetIFCExportTranslatorsList ("Exportación a Scia Engineer" in our project).
In the IFC Translators dialog, however, the preview translator is "Exportación General ACAT":
it has the Archicad icon, and "Set Preview" is disabled when it is selected. GetIFCPropertiesOfElements
also returns the ACAT property sets, which matches ACAT being the preview translator.

The DevKit remark says the first item of the list is the preview translator, but that does
not hold here. Please don't derive `preview` from the list index. If the API offers no
reliable way to identify the preview translator, consider removing the field or documenting
that it may be wrong.

### What should Tapir let you do?

Expose the last 296 items that are still open (⬜) on the [API coverage checklist](https://enzyme-apd.github.io/tapir-archicad-automation/api-coverage/): 172 C functions, 39 C functions that only exist in older versions, 17 AC25/26 command ids and 68 C++ functions (IFCInOutAPI, DesignOptionsAPI, DesignVariantAPI, KeynoteAPI). Expose each through a Tapir JSON command in the command group it belongs to: a new option of an existing command where one fits, otherwise a new command. Its parameters become the command's input and its result the response. For an older-only function or an AC25/26 command id, add the call to the existing command that does the same thing in newer versions, behind an `AC_VERSION` / `ServerMainVers_*` check, rather than a new command.

Suggested split (one PR per part):
1. **Elements** — the open Element, ElementLink, Selection, Classification, Renovation, ElementGroup, ElementList, ModelAccess, Conversion, Body and Polygon items.
2. **Library parts** — LibraryPart, LibraryManagement and LibPart.
3. **Attributes and project** — Attribute, AttributeList, ListData, ProjectSetting, ProjectOperation, Preferences/SetPreferences, Teamwork, Database, Navigator, View, Window, Drawing, Sight, CuttingPlane and the AC25/26 `APIDb_`, `APIDo_`, `APIIo_` and `APIEnv_` command ids.
4. **IFC** — the C++ IFCInOutAPI functions, the IFC C functions and the AC25 `APIAny_` IFC command ids.
5. **Design options, design variants and keynotes** — the C++ DesignOptionsAPI, DesignVariantAPI and KeynoteAPI functions.
6. **Add-on objects and the rest** — AddOnObject, General and `APIAny_ElemTypeToNeigID`.

Some of these may not fit a JSON command: add-on plumbing (`ACAPI_ActivatePropertyObjectHandler`, the AddOnObject store of an add-on, `ACAPI_Navigator_RegisterCallbackInterface`, `ACAPI_LibraryPart_RegisterESYM`/`RegisterSubtype`, the IFC `HookManager` hooks and the keynote event handlers, which are callbacks), dialogs (`APIIo_NewSettingsDialogID`, `ACAPI_IFC_InvokeIFCExportSettingsDlg`, `APIAny_InvokeIFCDifferenceExportSettingsDlgID`, `ACAPI_LibraryManagement_NewLibDial`) and licensing (`APIEnv_CheckDongleID`, `APIEnv_ProtectionDataID`). For each item that cannot be a command, say in the PR why, so a maintainer can move it to the `notApplicable` section of `tools/api_coverage_rules.json`.

title: Expose element info strings and library part / creator tool IDs
body:
### API functions

ACAPI_Element_GetElementInfoString
ACAPI_Element_GetCompoundInfoString
ACAPI_Element_GetElemCreatorToolUnId
ACAPI_LibraryPart_GetElemLibPartUnId

### What should Tapir let you do?

Scripts that build schedules or check models need the same text Archicad shows for an element: its **Element ID / info string**, the **compound info string** (e.g. the composite or profile summary), and which **library part** and **tool** made it. Today a script has to combine `GetDetailsOfElements` with library part lookups to guess this.

**Proposed commands**

Add four optional output fields to `GetDetailsOfElements` (Element Commands), requested by a new `additionalFields` input so existing callers are unchanged:

```json
{"elements": [{"elementId": {"guid": "…"}}], "additionalFields": ["infoString", "compoundInfoString", "libraryPartUnId", "creatorToolUnId"]}
```
Each entry of `detailsOfElements` then also has
```json
{"infoString": "W-012", "compoundInfoString": "Brick 300 + Insulation 100", "libraryPartUnId": "{…}-{…}", "creatorToolUnId": "{…}-{…}"}
```
A field the element type does not have (e.g. `libraryPartUnId` on a wall) is left out, not an error.

**To verify in Archicad**

- What `GetCompoundInfoString` returns for a composite wall, a profiled column and a basic slab.
- That `GetElemLibPartUnId` and `GetElemCreatorToolUnId` work on objects, doors/windows, lamps and on elements of non-library tools.
- `GetDetailsOfElements` already reads the info string through `APIMemoMask_ElemInfoString`; check that `GetElementInfoString` returns the same text.

**Example:** add `archicad-addon/Examples/GetElementInfoStrings.py` that runs the new commands on the test project and prints the results.

Split out of #1311.

title: Expose SetZoom and ResetZoom (zoom to a box, zoom back)
body:
### API functions

ACAPI_View_SetZoom
ACAPI_View_ResetZoom (AC27–30)
APIDb_ReSetZoomID

### What should Tapir let you do?

Scripts that take screenshots (`SaveCurrentWindowAsImage`), review issues or walk through elements need to **zoom the current window to a given area** and **go back** afterwards. Tapir has `FitInWindow` (zoom to all or to elements) but no way to zoom to a box or to step the zoom back.

**Proposed commands**

Two new commands in the Navigator / View group:

`SetZoom`
```json
{"zoomBox": {"xMin": 0.0, "yMin": 0.0, "xMax": 20.0, "yMax": 12.0}}
```
→ `{"success": true}`. Model coordinates of the current 2D window, in meters. Without `zoomBox` it behaves as Archicad's plain zoom.

`ResetZoom`
```json
{"numberOfStepsBack": 1}
```
→ `{"success": true}`. Steps back in the window's zoom history, like Archicad's *Zoom Back*.

On AC25–26 `ResetZoom` calls `ACAPI_Database (APIDb_ReSetZoomID, &numOfStepsBack)` through `MigrationHelper.hpp` (next to the existing `ACAPI_View_GetZoom` wrapper); from AC27 `ACAPI_View_ResetZoom`.

**To verify in Archicad**

- That `SetZoom` works in floor plan, section and layout windows, and what it does in 3D (likely an error to return).
- That `ResetZoom` with 2 steps undoes two zooms, and the error when the history is shorter.
- The optional `tranmat` parameter of `ACAPI_View_SetZoom`: leave it out unless a rotated view needs it.

**Example:** add `archicad-addon/Examples/ZoomToBox.py` that runs the new commands on the test project and prints the results.

Split out of #1311.

### Declarations from the DevKit (optional)

title: Expose skylight hole polygons, polygon triangulation, 3D surface types and texture coordinates
body:
### API functions

ACAPI_Element_GetSkylightHolePolygon
ACAPI_Polygon_TriangulatePoly
ACAPI_Polygon_PolygonId2SurfaceType
ACAPI_ModelAccess_DecomposePgon
ACAPI_ModelAccess_GetTextureCoord
ACAPI_ModelAccess_GetNum (AC27–30)

### What should Tapir let you do?

Daylight and area scripts need the **roof hole cut by a skylight**, renderers and exporters to web viewers need **triangles** instead of polygons with holes, and analysis scripts need to know whether a 3D polygon is the **top, bottom or side** of a slab or roof (e.g. to sum roof areas or find façade faces).

**Proposed commands**

`GetSkylightHolePolygons` (Element Commands)
```json
{"elements": [{"elementId": {"guid": "…"}}]}
```
→ `{"polygons": [{"coordinates": [{"x": 1.0, "y": 2.0}, …], "holes": []}]}`; an error item for an element that is not a skylight.

`TriangulatePolygonsOfElements`
```json
{"elements": [{"elementId": {"guid": "…"}}]}
```
→ `{"triangulations": [{"triangles": [[{"x": …, "y": …}, {"x": …, "y": …}, {"x": …, "y": …}], …]}]}`; for elements with a polygon memo (slab, zone, hatch, roof, mesh…).

`Get3DGeometryOfElements` gains an optional `"surfaceType"` per polygon (`"Top"`, `"Bottom"`, `"Side"`, …, from `API_SurfaceTypeID`), filled by `ACAPI_Polygon_PolygonId2SurfaceType`, behind a new `includeSurfaceTypes` input flag. Two more flags: `includeTextureCoordinates` adds a `uv` per vertex (`ACAPI_ModelAccess_GetTextureCoord`), and `convexPolygons` splits concave polygons into convex ones (`ACAPI_ModelAccess_DecomposePgon`), which many viewers need. `ACAPI_ModelAccess_GetNum` (AC27–30) gives the counts to size the response up front.

**To verify in Archicad**

- The coordinate space of the skylight hole polygon (roof plane or plan projection).
- Who owns the `coords` handle `TriangulatePoly` returns (dispose it with `BMKillHandle`).
- Which element types `PolygonId2SurfaceType` supports, and what the polygon id refers to (the 3D `ipgon` of `Get3DGeometryOfElements`).
- What `API_TexCoordPars` needs for `GetTextureCoord`, and who frees the `cpoly` handle of `DecomposePgon`.

**Example:** add `archicad-addon/Examples/GetSkylightHolesAndTriangles.py` that runs the new commands on the test project and prints the results.

Split out of #1311.

body:
### API functions

ACAPI_LibraryManagement_GetGDLDate
ACAPI_LibraryManagement_ChangeGDLDate

ACAPI_LibraryManagement_GetLibPartOrigLocation (AC27–30)
APIDo_LoadLibrariesID (AC25–26)

### What should Tapir let you do?

Library maintenance scripts (office standards, template updates) need to **organize the embedded library into folders**, **copy many files at once**, **check and reset the loaded libraries**, find where an embedded object **originally came from**, and read or set the **GDL date** (the date GDL scripts see, used to test date-dependent objects).

**Proposed commands**

In the Library group:

* `GetGDLDate` → `{"date": …}` and `SetGDLDate` `{"date": …}` (the `Int32` as the API documents it).
* `CheckLibraries` → `{"success": true}` or the error; `ResetLibraries` → `{"success": true}`.
* `CreateFolderInEmbeddedLibrary` `{"folderPath": "Office/Doors"}` → `{"success": true}`.
* `AddFilesToEmbeddedLibrary` gains an optional `"targetFolder"` and `"overwriteIfExists"`, done with one `ACAPI_LibraryManagement_CopyFilesIntoLibrary` call for all files.
* `DeleteEmbeddedLibraryItems` deletes all items with one `ACAPI_LibraryManagement_DeleteEmbeddedLibItems` call (today it loops `DeleteEmbeddedLibItem`).
* `GetLibraryPartOriginalLocations` (AC27–30) `{"libraryParts": [{"index": 12}]}` → `{"locations": [{"path": "C:/…/Door 26.gsm"}]}`.
* `AddLibraries`: use `ACAPI_LibraryManagement_AddLibraries` where it fits; on AC25–26 load the given list with `APIDo_LoadLibrariesID` through `MigrationHelper.hpp`.

**To verify in Archicad**

- The format of the GDL date, what `ChangeGDLDate` affects and how to restore the real date.
- That `CheckLibraries` and `ResetLibraries` do not show dialogs.
- Whether `CopyFilesIntoLibrary` and `CreateFolderInLibrary` take paths inside the embedded library or any loaded library.

**Example:** add `archicad-addon/Examples/OrganizeEmbeddedLibrary.py` that runs the new commands on the test project and prints the results.

### What should Tapir let you do?

Library audits compare objects by **unique ID** (main GUID and revision GUID), find all objects **derived from a subtype** by name pattern, check whether an object file is **locked / on a BIMcloud server**, and read an object's **sections** (scripts, parameters, previews) without opening it in the GDL editor.

**Proposed commands**

In the Library group:

* `GetLibraryPartIdentities` `{"libraryParts": [{"path": "C:/…/Chair.gsm"}]}` → `{"identities": [{"unId": "{…}-{…}", "refGuid": "…", "lockStatus": "Editable", "isServerLibraryPart": false}]}`.

* `GetBuiltInLibraryPartUnId` only if the template resource ids it takes can be listed for a script; otherwise say so in the PR.

ACAPI_AttributeList_DeleteProperty (AC25–26)

### What should Tapir let you do?

Building material audits need to know **which properties a material has** (not only the values of properties the script already knows), whether a property is **available, editable and visible** for it, and to **set one value on many materials** in one step. `GetPropertyValuesOfAttributes` / `SetPropertyValuesOfAttributes` handle known property ids one attribute at a time.

**Proposed commands**

In the Property group:

* `GetPropertyDefinitionsOfAttributes` `{"attributeIds": [{"attributeId": {"guid": "…"}}], "filter": "UserDefined" | "FundamentalBuiltIn" | "All"}` → `{"propertyDefinitionsOfAttributes": [{"propertyIds": [{"propertyId": {"guid": "…"}}]}]}`.
* `GetPropertyValuesOfAttributes` gains, per value, `"isAvailable"`, `"isEditable"`, `"isVisible"` behind an `includeStatus` flag, read with one `ACAPI_Attribute_GetPropertyValues` call per attribute.
* `SetPropertyValuesOfAttributes` uses `ACAPI_Attribute_SetProperties` (one call per attribute), and a new `SetPropertyValueOfAttributes` `{"propertyId": …, "propertyValue": …, "attributeIds": [...]}` sets one value on many attributes with `ACAPI_Attribute_ModifyPropertyValue` (AC27–30) / `ACAPI_AttributeList_ModifyPropertyValue` (AC25–26).
* `AddPropertyToAttributes` / `RemovePropertyFromAttributes` for custom (non-classification-driven) properties: `ACAPI_Attribute_AddProperty`/`DeleteProperty` on AC27 and `ACAPI_AttributeList_AddProperty`/`DeleteProperty` on AC25–26; on AC28+ say in the PR what replaces them.

**To verify in Archicad**

- Which attribute types have properties (building materials only, or more in newer versions).
- What `AddProperty`/`DeleteProperty` do to a definition that is already available through classification.
- That `ModifyPropertyValue` on many attributes is one undo step.

### What should Tapir let you do?

IFC coordination scripts on Archicad 25–28 need to **read and set IFC attributes** (Name, Description, ObjectType, Tag…) and **IFC classification references** of elements, **remove** IFC properties and references, and **convert** between Archicad GUIDs and IFC GlobalIds. Tapir has `GetIFCPropertiesOfElements`, `SetIFCPropertiesOfElements`, `GetIFCIdsOfElements` and `GetElementsByIFCIds`, but no attributes, classification references or removal.

**Proposed commands**

In the IFC group:

* `GetIFCAttributesOfElements` `{"elements": [...], "storedOnly": false}` → `{"ifcAttributesOfElements": [{"attributes": [{"name": "Name", "value": "…", "isValueSet": true}]}]}`.
* `SetIFCAttributesOfElements` `{"elementAttributes": [{"elementId": …, "name": "ObjectType", "value": "…"}]}`.
* `GetIFCClassificationReferencesOfElements` / `SetIFCClassificationReferencesOfElements` / `RemoveIFCClassificationReferencesOfElements` with `{"location", "identification", "name", "referencedSource": {"name", "edition", "editionDate", "description", "location"}}`.
* `RemoveIFCPropertiesOfElements` `{"elementProperties": [{"elementId": …, "propertySetName": "…", "propertyName": "…"}]}`.
* `GetIFCIdsOfElements` / `GetElementsByIFCIds`: on AC25 use the `APIAny_*IFCGuid*` ids and on AC26–27 `ACAPI_IFC_APIGuidToIFCGuid`/`IFCGuidToAPIGuid` where they give a different answer from what the commands do today; otherwise say why in the PR.
* `ACAPI_Element_GetIFCPropertyValuePrimitiveType` (AC25–27) to validate the value types `SetIFCPropertiesOfElements` takes.

These functions exist up to AC28 (some only to AC27). For AC29–30 return a clear "not available in this Archicad version" error unless the PR finds the replacement.

**To verify in Archicad**

- What `storedOnly` changes in the returned attributes.
- What the replacement of these functions is in AC29–30 (the IFCAPI C++ API only works inside export hooks).
- That setting an attribute is undoable and survives saving.

### What should Tapir let you do?

Teamwork scripts need to know **whether the project is shared and online** before sending or reserving, **what the current user may do** (create, modify/delete, the role's access rights), **who owns** a view/layout database or the hotlink cache management, and (AC29–30) **upload or remove BIMcloud libraries** as part of a library rollout.

**Proposed commands**

In the Teamwork group:

* `GetTeamworkStatus` → `{"isShared": true, "isOnline": true, "users": [...], "hotlinkCacheManagementOwner": {"userId": 3, "userName": "…"}}`, with the fields of `API_SharingInfo` from `ProjectSharing`, `HasConnection` and `GetHotlinkCacheManagementOwner`.
* `GetTeamworkAccessRights` `{"accessRights": ["CreateLayers", …]}` → `{"results": [true, …]}` (names from `API_TWAccessRights`; with no input, all of them).

**To verify in Archicad**

- What each call returns in a solo project (no errors expected, just `isShared: false`).

body:

### What should Tapir let you do?

Scripts and Grasshopper definitions need somewhere to **keep their own data inside the .pln/.tpl**: settings, the last sync state with an external database, IDs mapping elements to outside systems. Add-on objects are exactly that: named blobs stored in the project by Tapir, shared in Teamwork (with reserve/release like other Teamwork data) or kept per client.

**Proposed commands**

A new **Project Data** group, storing UTF-8 text (scripts put JSON in it) in Tapir's add-on objects:

* `GetProjectDataKeys` → `{"keys": [{"name": "my-tool/settings", "guid": "…", "clientOnly": false}]}`.
* `GetProjectData` `{"names": ["my-tool/settings"]}` → `{"values": [{"name": "…", "content": "…"}]}`.
* `SetProjectData` `{"values": [{"name": "…", "content": "…", "clientOnly": false, "unique": false}]}` creates (`CreateObject`, `CreateUniqueObject(More)`, `CreateClientOnlyObject`) or modifies (`ModifyObject`).
* `DeleteProjectData` `{"names": [...]}`.
* Teamwork: `ReserveProjectData`, `ReleaseProjectData`, `RequestProjectData` (with a mail text), `GrantProjectData` (to a user id), and the owner in `GetProjectDataKeys` (`GetTeamworkOwnerId`).
* `SetUIProperties` gives Tapir's add-on objects a readable name in the Teamwork palette; call it once at startup rather than exposing it, and say so in the PR.

Names are namespaced by the caller (`"my-tool/..."`) so scripts do not overwrite each other.

**To verify in Archicad**

- The size limits of an add-on object's content.
- That data survives save/open, and how client-only objects behave in a solo project.
- That Teamwork reserve/release of add-on objects works and how conflicts are reported.

**Example:** add `archicad-addon/Examples/ProjectDataStore.py` that runs the new commands on the test project and prints the results.

### What should Tapir let you do?

Modeling scripts need to **apply a solid operation and get new elements** (e.g. subtract a morph from a slab and keep the result as morphs), audit scripts need **when a solid link was made**, quantity takeoff needs the **composite / profile / GDL parameter quantities** `GetMoreQuantities` gives in one call for many elements, and scripts working with external hierarchical elements (e.g. MEP or add-on elements) need their **sub-elements**.

* `GetSubelementsOfHierarchicalElements` (AC27–30) supports external hierarchical elements with `ACAPI_Element_GetMemo_ExternalHierarchical`.

Template cleanup scripts **delete hundreds of unused attributes** (e.g. after purging a merged project) and list **all attributes of a type** in large projects. Deleting one by one is slow and makes one undo step each.

**Proposed commands**

* `DeleteAttributes` (Attribute group) deletes all attributes of one type with a single `ACAPI_Attribute_DeleteMore (attrTypeID, indexList)` call (one undo step), grouping the input by type.
* `GetAttributesByType` lists with `ACAPI_Attribute_EnumerateAttributesByType` on AC27–30 where it is faster than today's index loop, and uses `ACAPI_Attribute_GetFirstValidAttribute` to report a valid default (e.g. for scripts that must fall back to an existing pen table or fill).

**To verify in Archicad**

- That `DeleteMore` replaces references to deleted attributes the same way the existing delete does.
- That `EnumerateAttributesByType` returns the same attributes as today's loop (including folders' contents).
- What `GetFirstValidAttribute` returns when the type has no attributes.

**Example:** add `archicad-addon/Examples/DeleteUnusedAttributes.py` that runs the new commands on the test project and prints the results.

Split out of #1311.

### Declarations from the DevKit (optional)

```cpp
// Inc/ACAPinc.h
__APIEXPORT GSErrCode ACAPI_Attribute_DeleteMore (API_AttrTypeID attrTypeID, const GS::Array<API_AttributeIndex> &attrIndexList)
__APIEXPORT GSErrCode ACAPI_Attribute_EnumerateAttributesByType (API_AttrTypeID typeID, const std::function<void (API_Attribute &)> &processor)
__APIEXPORT API_AttributeIndex ACAPI_Attribute_GetFirstValidAttribute (API_AttrTypeID typeID)
```

### Archicad versions you need it in

25, 26, 27, 28, 29, 30

Items with versions after them in the list exist only in those versions (guard with `ServerMainVers_*` / `AC_VERSION` checks).

title: Bot PRs: stop losing review verdicts, hand over far less often
body:
## Why so many PRs get `needs-maintainer`

90 open bot PRs had the label. The latest hand-over reason on each:

| Reason | PRs |
|---|---|
| N reviews of its latest commit recorded no verdict (incl. the older "ten reviews" wording) | 81 |
| fix run pushed nothing | 8 |
| fix rounds did not make the builds and the review pass | 1 |

The empty reviews were not caused by the PRs. Of the 98 review runs the steward dispatched since 2026-10-19 20:00 UTC, **38 posted no summary**, so no verdict was recorded. This happened on both Opus and Sonnet. Even the same PR could come back empty in one run and fine in the next (#1181 at 04:50 and 07:15). The empty runs had more refused tool calls (5–8, against 2–4 in runs that posted), which points at the posting step. The job logs don't show which command was refused.

## Changes

- `claude_pr_review.yml`
  - The review writes its summary to `.review-context/summary.md` and posts it with `gh pr comment --body-file`.
  - `Edit(./.review-context/summary.md)` is the only file write it is allowed.
  - A new step, **Post the summary the review wrote**, posts that file when the review didn't post it itself. It only does so if the file carries this run's nonce verdict marker and no comment from this run carries the nonce, so the verdict and resolve steps work as before.
- `claude_bot_pr_steward.yml`: a head is handed over after `BOT_PR_MAX_EMPTY_REVIEWS` empty reviews (new repository variable, default **8**) instead of 3. The 50-minute wait after an empty review stays.
- `CLAUDE.md` documents both.

The other hand-over rules are unchanged. "Fix run pushed nothing" remains a real hand-over: a DevKit check, a PR body edit, or merging `main` when it brings `.github/` changes are all things the bot's token cannot do.

## Validation

- Both workflows parse as YAML.
- `bash -n` is clean on the new step and on the edited sweep script.
- The review change can only be confirmed on real runs once this is merged: dispatched reviews should then show "Posted the summary…" or "The review posted its summary itself."

title: Place Detail and Worksheet markers, and change their settings
body:
Detail and Worksheet **markers** (the elements that cut a detail or worksheet out of a plan, section or elevation) cannot be placed through Tapir 1.7.2, and their own settings cannot be changed; reading, moving and deleting work. Checked on Archicad 28 (GER, 7006), Tapir 1.7.2, on a Detail marker placed by hand in a section. Worksheet markers share the schema (`DetailWorksheetDetails`) but were not tested.

**What works today**

| | Command | Result |
|---|---|---|
| list | `GetElementsByType {elementType:"Detail"}` | the markers of the **current window's** database; markers in other views need `databases` (a section's marker is not found while the floor plan is active, and vice versa) |
| read | `GetDetailsOfElements` | `DetailWorksheetDetails`: basePoint, angle, markerId, detailName, detailIdStr, isHorizontalMarker, clipPolygon, linkData |
| move / rotate | `MoveElements`, `RotateElements` | moved and rotated, marker and clip polygon together |
| layer | `SetDetailsOfElements {details:{layerIndex}}` | changed and read back |
| delete | `DeleteElements` | marker deleted; Archicad deletes its Detail viewpoint with it (Project Map: 2 Details → 1) |

**What is missing**

1. **Placing a marker.** `CreateDetails` creates an independent Detail database only, without a marker. There is no way to place a Detail or Worksheet marker with its clip polygon on a floor plan, section or elevation - neither one that creates a new viewpoint nor one linked to an existing Detail/Worksheet.
2. **Changing a marker's own settings** - name, reference ID, clip polygon, marker type and size. `SetDetailsOfElements` has no settable fields for Detail/Worksheet.
3. **A silent success:** `SetDetailsOfElements` with `typeSpecificDetails: {detailName: "..."}` or `{detailIdStr: "X-99"}` on a Detail marker returns `success: true`, and the read back is unchanged. It should fail like other unsupported fields, so a caller does not believe the change was made.

**Possible shape** (following how #995 does it for Sections and Elevations, and extending existing commands rather than adding parallel ones):

- `CreateDetails` / `CreateWorksheets`: an optional marker block per item (`floorIndex` or a database, `basePoint`, `angle`, `clipPolygon`, optionally the marker favorite) that places the marker together with the new viewpoint; optionally an existing Detail/Worksheet to link the marker to instead.
- `SetDetailsOfElements`: a `DetailWorksheetSettings` variant of `typeSpecificDetails` with `detailName`, `detailIdStr`, `clipPolygon`, `angle` and the marker settings; fields that cannot be set reported as failed.

The Archicad API has what this needs: `ACAPI_Element_CreateExt` and `ACAPI_Element_ChangeExt` place and change Detail and Worksheet elements with their marker, and `ACAPI_Element_GetDefaultsExt` gives the marker defaults.

Related: #995 (Sections and Elevations, the same pattern), #1039 (deleting independent Details/Worksheets), #1128 (listing all viewpoint databases).
author: weltmaister

title: GetProjectInfo: report whether the open project has unsaved changes
body:
**What we ask.** An output field of `GetProjectInfo`, for example `hasUnsavedChanges` (boolean), that says whether the project open in Archicad has changes that are not saved. For an untitled project: whether anything was drawn in it since it was made.

**Why.** A client that automates Archicad through Tapir needs to know whether `OpenProject` would discard the user's work. Today it cannot tell a clean document from a changed one:

- `GetProjectInfo` answers `isUntitled`, `isTeamwork` and, for a saved project, `projectLocation`, `projectPath` and `projectName`. Nothing in it says whether the open project has unsaved changes.
- `OpenProject` over an open project with unsaved changes answers success with no dialog, and the changes are gone. Seen on Archicad 28 build 7006 INT with Tapir 1.7.2 (TapirAddOn_AC28_Win.apx), 2026-10-20: a saved project open, one wall drawn and not saved, then `OpenProject` of the same `.pln`: the reply was `{"succeeded":true,"result":{"addOnCommandResponse":{"success":true}}}`, no dialog appeared, and afterwards the wall was not in the plan. The same open made by hand (File > Open) shows Archicad's "Save Changes" dialog first.
- An open over an untitled project with nothing drawn also answered success with no dialog. An untitled project with unsaved work was not tried.

So a client must either never send `OpenProject` while a project is open, and ask the user to open the file by hand, or risk discarding work without notice. With a field that says whether there are unsaved changes, a client could send the open only over a document that has none, and ask the user otherwise.

**Related question (no change asked).** Is the silent discard of unsaved changes by `OpenProject` intended? If it is, a sentence in the command's description would warn other clients. If it is not, an option of `OpenProject` that refuses when unsaved changes exist would be an alternative to the field above.

**Environment.** Archicad 28 build 7006 INT, Windows 11; Tapir 1.7.2; requests sent as HTTP POST to the Archicad JSON interface (`API.ExecuteAddOnCommand`, namespace `TapirCommand`) on 127.0.0.1:19723.

title: API coverage: C++ items never become "in progress" from open pull requests
body:
## Problem

On the [API coverage checklist](https://enzyme-apd.github.io/tapir-archicad-automation/api-coverage/), C++ items named in an issue stay **claimed** even after open pull requests implement them. They never reach **in progress**. The current `api-coverage.json` (2026-10-21 01:04 UTC) shows:

- C++ member functions: 993 claimed, 418 done, **0 in progress**
- C functions: 284 in progress

The workflow itself runs fine and publishes every hour. The problem is how the checklist is generated.

## Cause

In `tools/generate_api_coverage.py` (`build`, the C++ loop), `search_names` for a C++ item holds only its fully qualified name, `<namespace>::<Class>::<Member>`. `mentioned ()` looks for names containing `::` as plain substrings of the pull request's added text. Code never calls members that way. It uses `modifier.SetWallThickness (…)`, `transition.Get (…)` and so on, so the check never matches. Issues do spell out the qualified names, so the same items do match as **claimed**.

"Done" doesn't have this problem because it uses `cpp_used ()`: the member is called by name (`\bName\s*[(<]`) in a file that also uses its class (short class name) or includes its header. The pull request check was never given the same rule.

Example: the six open part PRs of #1287 (`claude/issue-1287-part*`) and of #1298 (`claude/issue-1298-part*`) add calls such as `.SetWallThickness (`, `.SetFlangeSize (` and `Transition::Get`. Their items still show as claimed.

## Proposed fix

Count a C++ item as **in progress** when an open pull request's added lines in `archicad-addon/Sources`:
1. call the member by name (`\bName\s*[(<]`, the regex `cpp_used` uses), and
2. use its short class name (or the class's header).

For C functions and AC25/26 command ids, keep the current identifier match.

Ideally the C++ check should share one helper with `cpp_used ()` so "done" and "in progress" follow the same rule. Optionally, `tools/fetch_api_coverage_github_data.py` could also record each pull request's changed filenames. Then the class or header check could also use the main-branch version of the touched files, since an added call is often inside a function whose class is named in lines the PR didn't add.

A quick test of rule (1)+(2) on the 12 open part branches of #1287 and #1298 alone moves about 245 claimed C++ items to in progress. Short member names such as `Get` or `Modify` can match too broadly, but "done" already accepts the same trade-off.

## Constraints

- `api_coverage.yml` runs on `pull_request_target`. Keep reading pull requests only through the API, as text. Never check out or run PR code.
- `fetch_api_coverage_github_data.py` stays standard-library only.
- After the change, the counts in the summary, the badge and the SVGs should all agree.

## Not in scope

#1287 (642 items), #1298 (282) and #1202 (52) are umbrella issues. Their six part PRs cover only part of the functions, so the rest should correctly stay **claimed** until more parts are opened.

title: Drawing details: read/write the printable border (`hasBorderLine`, `borderLineType`, `borderPen`, `borderSize`)
body:
## Summary

Drawing Settings › **Frame** has an **Add Printable Border** checkbox with a line type, a pen and a border offset/size. `GetDetailsOfElements` / `SetDetailsOfElements` (Drawing) already cover `isCutWithFrame` and `clipPolygon` (thanks to #651 / #653), but not the border, so today it needs the dialog on every drawing.

We want to apply one office standard to every drawing of a layout book (in our case 146 drawings on 33 layouts of a design-development set):

| Dialog (Frame panel) | Our standard | Tapir today |
|---|---|---|
| Frame behavior: Manually resized frame + Clip drawing to frame | on | `isCutWithFrame` ✅ (read + write) |
| Add printable border | on | ❌ |
| Border line type | Solid | ❌ |
| Border pen | 2 | ❌ |
| Border offset | 2 mm | ❌ |

## Proposed

Mirror `isInNumbering` / the #817 change. The members already exist in `API_DrawingType` (`APIdefs_Elements.h`, documented in the AC30 reference: https://graphisoft.github.io/archicad-api-devkit/struct_a_p_i___drawing_type.html):

```cpp
bool               hasBorderLine;   // Show drawing border?
API_AttributeIndex borderLineType;  // Line type of the border.
short              borderPen;       // Pen attribute index of the border.
double             borderSize;      // Thickness of the border in 'm'.
```

- `GetDetailsOfElements` (Drawing `typeSpecificDetails`): add `hasBorderLine` (boolean), `borderLineType` (attribute index, or `AttributeIndexAndGuid` like other commands), `borderPen` (integer) and `borderSize` (number, metres on the paper).
- `SetDetailsOfElements` (`DrawingSettings`): accept the same four fields, each with its `ACAPI_ELEMENT_MASK_SET (mask, API_DrawingType, <member>)`.
- `CreateDrawings`: optionally accept them too, so new drawings do not inherit whatever the Drawing tool defaults hold (same problem #651 described for `isCutWithFrame`).
- `CommonSchemaDefinitions.json`: add the properties to `DrawingDetails` and `DrawingSettings`, plus an example that reads, flips and restores them.

Example call:

```json
{"elementsWithDetails": [{"elementId": {"guid": "<drawing>"}, "details": {"typeSpecificDetails": {
  "isCutWithFrame": true,
  "hasBorderLine": true,
  "borderLineType": 1,
  "borderPen": 2,
  "borderSize": 0.002
}}}]}
```

## Open points for a maintainer with the DevKit

1. **`borderSize` vs. "Border offset".** The DevKit describes `borderSize` as "thickness of the border in 'm'", while the dialog field next to the border is labelled *Border Offset* (Spanish UI: *Desplazamiento del Límite*, in mm). Please confirm that `borderSize` is that dialog field, and whether it is in paper metres.
2. **"Fit frame to drawing" vs. "Manually resized frame".** We cannot find a separate member for this radio button. Is it only `isCutWithFrame` plus `poly` (i.e. manual frame without clipping is not representable through the API)? If there is a member, exposing it read-only would already help.
3. Whether changing the border via `ACAPI_Element_Change` needs the drawing to be updated afterwards to show the new border.

## Current state, verified live

Archicad 29 SPA (build 5101), Tapir 1.7.0, macOS, through `API.ExecuteAddOnCommand`. On one layout with 3 drawings, `GetDetailsOfElements` returns `isCutWithFrame: true` + `clipPolygon` for the clipped plan and `isCutWithFrame: false` for the other two, and nothing about the border. The `DrawingDetails` / `DrawingSettings` schemas on `main` have no border field either, so a drawing set in the dialog to *Add Printable Border* (Solid, pen 2, 2 mm) cannot be read or matched through Tapir.

Thanks for Tapir!
author: Sofiorellana-Winteri

title: SetGDLParametersOfElements takes Angle parameters in degrees, GetGDLParametersOfElements returns radians
body:
### What happens

`SetGDLParametersOfElements` takes the value of an `Angle`-type GDL parameter in **degrees**, but `GetGDLParametersOfElements` returns the same parameter in **radians**. Writing back a value you just read silently changes the angle, so any read-modify-write script corrupts every angle it touches.

### Steps

On an object with an `Angle`-type parameter (here a copy of "Standard grid marker", parameter `AC_Angle`):

1. `SetGDLParametersOfElements` `{"name": "AC_Angle", "value": 30}` → `success: true`
2. `GetGDLParametersOfElements` → `"value": 0.523598776` (30° in radians)
3. `SetGDLParametersOfElements` `{"name": "AC_Angle", "value": 0.523598776}`, the value just read → `success: true`
4. `GetGDLParametersOfElements` → `"value": 0.009138523` (0.52° in radians)

Same on the other versions:
- Archicad 29: `labelRot` on a placed object, set 30 → read 0.523598776.
- Archicad 30: `gs_alpha` ("Pitch Angle") on a placed "Awning", set 30 → read 0.523598776. The awning's `zzyzx` also became 1.0 (2 m × sin 30°), so the object really took 30 degrees.

### Expected

Set and get use the same unit. Radians would match the rest of the API (element `angle`, `stampAngle` and angle property values are all radians). If degrees on input is intentional, the `SetGDLParametersOfElements` schema should say so; at the moment it says nothing about units.

### Versions

Tapir 1.7.2 on Archicad 27, 29 and 30, macOS (via tapir-archicad-mcp 0.6.6).

title: CreatePropertyDefinitions fails without defaultValue, which the schema marks optional
body:
### What happens

A property definition sent to `CreatePropertyDefinitions` without `defaultValue` is not created. The schema marks `defaultValue` optional (`anyOf ... null`, default `null`). The error gives no reason.

### Steps

In one call, create three definitions in a new property group, all with `availability: []`:

| Definition | Result |
|---|---|
| string, with `defaultValue` `{"basicDefaultValue": {"type": "string", "status": "normal", "value": "x"}}` | created |
| string, no `defaultValue` | `{"error": {"code": -2130313104, "message": "failed to create the property"}}` |
| number, no `defaultValue` | same error |

### Expected

Definitions without `defaultValue` are created with an empty or undefined default. If a default really is required, the schema should mark it required and the error should name the missing field.

### Versions

Tapir 1.7.2 on Archicad 27, 29 and 30, macOS (via tapir-archicad-mcp 0.6.6). Also seen on Archicad 29 with Tapir 1.7.0.
author: signzero

title: ModifyMeshes: omitting holes deletes them, and holes sent alone are ignored
body:
### What happens

The `ModifyMeshes` schema says "Only provided fields are changed; omitted fields are left as-is", but `holes` doesn't behave that way:

1. Sending `polygonCoordinates` without `holes` **deletes every hole** in the mesh.
2. Sending `holes` without `polygonCoordinates` returns `success: true` but **adds no hole**.

Holes are only applied when sent together with the outline.

### Steps

1. `CreateMeshes`: a 10 × 10 m outline (z 0, 0.1, 0.2, 0.3) with one 2 × 2 m hole.
2. `GetDetailsOfElements` → `holes` has one entry.
3. `ModifyMeshes` with `polygonCoordinates` only (same four points) → `success: true`.
4. `GetDetailsOfElements` → `"holes": []`.
5. `ModifyMeshes` with `holes` only (the same hole) → `success: true`.
6. `GetDetailsOfElements` → still `"holes": []`.
7. `ModifyMeshes` with both `polygonCoordinates` and `holes` → the hole is back.

Steps 1–4 reproduced on Archicad 27, 29 and 30; steps 5–7 on 29 and 30.

### Expected

Omitting `holes` keeps the existing holes, and `holes` sent alone replaces them, as the schema describes. If replacing the outline has to replace the holes too, the `polygonCoordinates` description should say so (today it only says it "replaces the existing boundary entirely"), and `holes` sent alone should be applied or rejected rather than reported as a success.

### Versions

Tapir 1.7.2 on Archicad 27, 29 and 30, macOS (via tapir-archicad-mcp 0.6.6).
author: signzero

title: Error entries in batch results carry no elementId (GetDetailsOfElements error has no GUID at all)
body:
### What happens

In commands that take a list of elements, a failed entry has a different shape from a successful one and carries no `elementId`. For `GetDetailsOfElements` the error message does not contain the GUID either, so the only way to tell which input failed is its position in the array.

### Steps

`GetTypesOfElements` with [valid object, made-up GUID, valid mesh]:

```json
{"typeOfElement": {"elementId": {"guid": "…"}, "elementType": "Object"}}
{"error": {"code": 7204, "message": "Element not found (element guid: \"00000000-1111-2222-3333-444444444444\")"}}
{"typeOfElement": {"elementId": {"guid": "…"}, "elementType": "Mesh"}}
```

`GetDetailsOfElements` with [made-up GUID, valid element] and `fields: ["type"]`:

```json
{"error": {"code": -2130313115, "message": "Failed to get the details of element"}}
{"type": "Object"}
```

Successful `GetDetailsOfElements` entries carry no `elementId` either.

### Expected

Every entry, success or error, carries the `elementId` it refers to, or at least the documentation guarantees that results keep the input order. Scripts that join results to inputs by `elementId` lose track of failures today.

### Versions

Tapir 1.7.2 on Archicad 27, 29 and 30, macOS (via tapir-archicad-mcp 0.6.6).
author: signzero

title: API coverage: see C++ members in open PRs, mark non-command C++ API not applicable
body:
The checklist showed almost everything as claimed by an issue, but only about 44% as done or in a pull request, even though nearly every claiming issue has PRs. There were two causes. This PR fixes the first and trims the second.

## 1. C++ members in open PRs were invisible

`main` counts a C++ member as used when a file that uses its class calls it by name (`cpp_used`). For an open PR, however, a member counted only when the PR's added lines contained its fully qualified name (`ACAPI::MEP::RoutingSegment::GetBeginNodeId`). Code calls it as `segment->GetBeginNodeId ()`, so practically no C++ member was ever "in progress". If an issue named the member, it fell to "claimed".

- `fetch_api_coverage_github_data.py` now keeps each PR's added lines per file (`addedFiles`). It makes the same API calls as before.
- `generate_api_coverage.py` now runs `cpp_used` on those files: the call must be in the added lines, and the class or header can come from the same file's lines on `main`. The fully-qualified-name match still applies too. The workflow still never checks out PR code; this only reads the diff text it already fetched.
- An out-of-class member definition (`template <…> Result<void> Accessory::Modify (…)`) was also listed as a free function `ACAPI::MEP::Modify`. Four such phantom rows are gone.

## 2. Umbrella issues claim API that cannot be a command

#1287 (MEP) and #1298 (C++ `ACAPI::`) each list every remaining function of a module. Their part PRs implement only part of that list. Some of the rest cannot be a JSON command at all, so I added `notApplicable` rules for those (151 items):

- MEP tool `*UIManager`s
- interfaces an add-on implements or registers (model checks, MEP calculation, keynote handlers, add-on services)
- IFC export hooks
- undo scopes and `Err`
- the tracker
- `LibraryManager` filter predicates
- settings dialogs, licensing and add-on preferences

None of these items is used on `main` or in an open PR. I checked that no rule hides a done or in-progress item, because rules take precedence over usage.

## Result

I ran it locally against the AC25–AC30 DevKits and the live GitHub data:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| done | 748 | 748 |
| in progress | 321 | 669 |
| claimed | 1199 | 753 |
| open | 146 | 89 |
| not applicable | 469 | 620 |
| done + in a PR | 44% | 63% |

The new "in progress" set is a subset of what `main`'s rule finds when run on full checkouts of all 268 open PR heads. Seven members it misses are called only through templates that already exist on `main`.

The 753 still claimed are real remaining work. Most come from #1287 (453), #1298 (96) and #1202 (52), whose split plans cover only part of their lists. They will show as "open" once those issues close after their last part merges.

This touches `tools/`, a release-critical path, so it needs a maintainer to merge it.

  - its `GetDetailsOfElements` key and its `CreateWalls`/`ModifyWalls` key, which differ for some fields (e.g. `begThickness` vs `thickness`);
  - the `API_WallType` member, with the DevKit's description of it;
  - the `label`, `group` (dialog panel) and `subgroup` (heading inside the panel) of its control in the Wall settings dialog, with the source of the label.
- **`tools/check_tool_settings.py`** (standard library only, no Archicad needed) – checks each table against the Add-On sources:
  - every key is covered exactly once, and the table has no key the Add-On doesn't have;
  - labels are unique (case-insensitive) and each one names its source.

  It reads the keys from the wall case of `GetDetailsOfElementsCommand::Execute` and from the CreateWalls/ModifyWalls schemas, evaluated the same way `generate_addon_docs.py` does. `--markdown` prints the table for review.
- **`grasshopper-plugin/TapirGrasshopperPlugin/ToolSettings/README.md`** – the format and the rules.
- **`CLAUDE.md`** – two new sections under "Grasshopper plugin":
  - *Naming from the Archicad GUI*: names come from these tables, and a label is never invented.
  - *Archicad tool components (target architecture)*:
    - one component per tool, placed in Design / Document / Viewpoint Tools;
    - Refresh / Execute / Create buttons, with one JSON input and output per dialog panel;
    - Execute and Create share one apply-function;
    - delete stays in its own component;
    - old components are retired in steps.

## Where the labels come from

The labels come from Graphisoft's Archicad 29 help: the text and dialog screenshots of these pages.
- Wall Tool Settings
- Element Display in Floor Plan and Section, with its sub-pages Show On Stories, Floor Plan Display, Show Projection, and Cut Surfaces and Outlines
- Relation to Zones

They are also cross-checked with the DevKit comments that name a control. A label is only written when a source shows it word for word, and `labelSource` names the page and the heading, text or screenshot.

Result: **24 of 52 fields have a label**, and every dialog control has its panel and subheading:

| Panel | Subheading | Labelled fields |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Geometry and Positioning | – | Wall Top, Wall Height, Home Story, Bottom Elevation, Wall Structure, Building Material, Composite, Profile, Geometry Method, Wall Thickness, Wall Complexity, PolyWall Corners Can Change, Reference Line Location |
| Floor Plan and Section | Floor Plan Display | Show on Stories, Floor Plan Display, Show Projection |
| Floor Plan and Section | Cut Surfaces | Cut Fill Foreground Pen |
| Floor Plan and Section | Outlines | Uncut Lines, Overhead Lines, Overhead Line Pen |
| Model | – | Align Texture to Wall Edges, End Surfaces: Override using Adjoining Walls, Junction Order, Relation to Zones |

Still `null`:
- **Dialog controls whose label the help pages don't show**: top/bottom offset, end thickness, slant angles, reference line offset/flip, cut line and pen, cut fill background pen, the three surface overrides and their chain, log height. They have their panel, keep their API names, and can be filled in once checked in Archicad.
- **Fields that are not controls of the dialog**: coordinates and polygon (drawn in Archicad), output-only values, junction priorities.

Run `python tools/check_tool_settings.py --markdown` for the full table.

## Testing

- `python tools/check_tool_settings.py` → consistent.
- Breaking the table on purpose (duplicate label, label without source, missing key, unknown keys) gives one clear error for each.
- No C#/C++ code changed.

title: API coverage: retry GitHub API requests refused for the rate limit
body:
## Why

`tools/fetch_api_coverage_github_data.py` lists the files of every open pull request on each API Coverage run. A burst of PR events can use up the Actions token's API limit. When that happens, the first refused request fails the run with a bare `urllib.error.HTTPError: HTTP Error 403: Forbidden` traceback. This happened on #1410 and #1411, twice in a row, including the one re-run.

## What

`get ()` now retries a request that GitHub refuses because of its rate limit (403 or 429), up to 5 times. The wait depends on what GitHub sends:

| GitHub's answer | Wait before the retry |
| --- | --- |
| `Retry-After` header | that many seconds |
| `X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0` (limit used up) | until `X-RateLimit-Reset` |
| secondary limit naming no wait (403 whose body says "rate limit") | 1 minute, then 2, 3, … |

Other cases:
- **Total wait per run:** the waits of one run share a budget of 8 minutes (`WAIT_BUDGET_SECONDS`), well inside the job's 20-minute timeout. A wait that doesn't fit isn't held: the script stops at once with a clear message saying when the limit resets, and the next run (hourly at the latest) fetches the data.
- **A 403 that is not about the rate limit** (a permission error) and every other HTTP error still fail at once, as before.

Standard library only, as before. The workflow itself is unchanged.

## Testing

Tested against a local fake GitHub API, with `time.sleep` stubbed:

| Case | Result |
| --- | --- |
| 403 with `Retry-After: 30` | waits 30 s, retries, succeeds |
| 403, limit used up, reset in 90 s | waits 91 s, retries, succeeds |
| 403 secondary limit, no headers | waits 60 s, retries, succeeds |
| 429 with `Retry-After: 5` | waits 5 s, retries, succeeds |
| 403, limit used up, reset in 50 min | stops at once with "…it resets at HH:MM UTC…" |
| 403 "Resource not accessible by integration" | raises at once |
| 404 | raises at once |
| rate limited 6 times in a row | 5 retries, then raises |
| four requests each asking for 150 s | the first three wait (450 s), the fourth stops the run (budget 480 s) |
