title: Application: run the Action Center hotlink check, redraw the current database, hide and show Archicad
body:
Scripts that drive Archicad for a long batch (exporting, publishing, updating hotlinks) need three small application-level controls that Tapir does not have yet:

- **Hide Archicad:** keep the main window out of the way while the batch runs, then bring it back. This is Windows only.
- **Run the Action Center check:** find out whether every hotlink is up to date before publishing.
- **Redraw the current database:** refresh it after a batch of changes, even when its window is in the background.

Today a script can only quit Archicad (`QuitArchicad`), and Tapir redraws only through `ACAPI_View_Redraw` inside a few element commands.

Please add, in the Application group (`ApplicationCommands.cpp`):

- **`GetArchicadVisibility`:**
  - **Input:** none.
  - **Output:** `{ "isVisible": bool }`.
  - On macOS, return a clear error: "Supported on Windows only." Don't fake `true`.
- **`SetArchicadVisibility`:**
  - **Input:** `{ "isVisible": bool }`.
  - **Output:** an execution result.
  - On macOS, return the same error.
- **`RunActionCenterChecks`:**
  - **Input:** optional `checks`, a list of check names. The only one available on every version is `"Hotlinks"`. Omitted means `["Hotlinks"]`.
  - **Output:** an `executionResults` entry per check.
  - Map the documented errors to messages: `APIERR_NOPLAN` → "There is no open project.", `APIERR_REFUSEDCMD` → "Refused to run the check because a modal dialog is open."
- **`RedrawCurrentDatabase`:**
  - **Input:** none.
  - **Output:** an execution result.

### API

AC27–AC30, declarations and doc text as in the AC30 headers:

```cpp
// Inc/ACAPinc.h  (@ingroup Window, @since Archicad 25)
/**
 * @brief Runs the selected checks of the Action Center.
 * @param item [in] The checks that Action Center will preform.
 * @return
 * 			- NoError - The function has completed successfully.
 * 			- APIERR_NOPLAN - There is no open project.
 * 			- APIERR_REFUSEDCMD - Refused to run check method because of opened modal dialog.
 * @remarks This function runs the checks of the Action Center. The Action Center tab will appear if an issue was found.
 */
__APIEXPORT GSErrCode ACAPI_Window_Check (API_ActionCenterItemID item);

// Inc/APIdefs_ActionCenter.hpp (AC26–AC30)
enum API_ActionCenterItemID {
	APIActionCenterItem_Hotlinks = 0	// "Checks whether all hotlinks are up-to-date."
};

// Inc/ACAPI_Database.h  (@ingroup Database)
/**
 * @brief Redraws the current database, even it's associated window is in the background.
 * @return
 * 			- NoError - The function completed successfully.
 * 			- APIERR_NOPLAN - No open project.
 * @remarks This function is used to redraw the current database in the background. Only the visible region of the associated window will be updated from the update picture.
 */
__APIEXPORT GSErrCode ACAPI_Database_RedrawCurrentDatabase ();

// Inc/ACAPI_Environment.h  (@ingroup View)
/**
 * @brief Returns the visibility of application.
 * @param isShown [out] Application is visible.
 * @remarks ... The actual visibility can be changed with the @ref ACAPI_View_ChangeShowHideState function.
 * 			Supported on Windows only.
 */
__APIEXPORT GSErrCode ACAPI_View_GetShowHideState (bool* isShown);

/**
 * @brief Changes the visibility of application.
 * @param toShow [in] Application is visible.
 * @remarks ... The actual visibility can be retrieved with the @ref ACAPI_View_GetShowHideState function.
 * 			Supported on Windows only.
 */
__APIEXPORT GSErrCode ACAPI_View_ChangeShowHideState (bool* toShow);
```

`ACAPI_View_ChangeShowHideState` takes `bool*`, not `bool`, on every version.

AC25/AC26:

- **Action Center check:** `ACAPI_ActionCenter_Check (API_ActionCenterItemID item)` in `ACAPinc.h`, with the same parameter.
- **Redraw:** `ACAPI_Database (APIDb_RedrawCurrentDatabaseID)`, `'DRDB'`, `par1: --- par2: ---`.
- **Get visibility:** `ACAPI_Environment (APIEnv_GetShowHideStateID, bool*)`, `'GSHW'`.
- **Change visibility:** `ACAPI_Environment (APIEnv_ChangeShowHideStateID, bool*)`, `'CSHW'`.

Add `TAPIR_` wrappers for these four calls in `MigrationHelper.hpp`, gated on `ServerMainVers_2700` as the existing wrappers are.

**The enum differs on AC25.** There it is `{ APIActionCenterItem_All, APIActionCenterItem_Hotlinks, APIActionCenterItem_Libraries, APIActionCenterItem_Drawings, APIActionCenterItem_Licenses }`, so `Hotlinks` is `1` on AC25 and `0` on AC26+:
- Always pass the named enumerator, never an integer.
- On AC25, accept `"All"`, `"Libraries"`, `"Drawings"` and `"Licenses"` as well.
- On later versions, give those names a per-check error ("Not available on this Archicad version") rather than failing the call.

### Notes, to verify in Archicad

- **What the check reports:** `ACAPI_Window_Check` returns only an error code. "The Action Center tab will appear if an issue was found", so it does not tell the caller whether there were issues. Check what a project with an outdated hotlink returns. Name the result honestly in the command description: "ran the check", not "hotlinks are up to date". Say on the pull request what was found.
- **Hidden Archicad:** check that it still answers JSON commands (`GetArchicadVisibility`, then `SetArchicadVisibility` back to `true`). Check whether it stays in the taskbar, and what happens to the Tapir palette and open dialogs. Warn in the description that a script must show Archicad again, including when it fails.
- **Visibility on macOS:** check the actual return code there. Report the Windows-only error from the command either way.
- **Redraw vs `ACAPI_View_Redraw`:** check how `RedrawCurrentDatabase` differs from the existing call, for example after changing a story or a layout that is not the front window.

### Example

Add `Examples/application_visibility.py`:
- run `RunActionCenterChecks` with no input and print its results;
- run `RedrawCurrentDatabase`;
- on Windows, read `GetArchicadVisibility`, hide Archicad, wait two seconds, show it again in a `finally` block, and read the visibility back.

132 Grasshopper components now use **Archicad's own user interface icons**, cut from the screenshots of Graphisoft's Archicad 29 help.

**Licence:** the icons are © Graphisoft SE and used with Graphisoft's permission. `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` lists all 132 and says they are not covered by the repository's MIT licence.

- **Element tools (52, commit 757d23d):** the toolbox icons of Wall, Column, Beam, Slab, Roof, Stair, Curtain Wall, Mesh, Morph, Zone, Object, Lamp, Door, Window, Opening, Text, Label, Dimension, Fill, Line, Arc/Circle, Polyline, Spline, Hotspot and Grid Element, for their Create, Modify, *Details and Set*Details components.

title: Grasshopper: Walls tool component prototype, built from ToolSettings/Wall.json
body:
## What

The first **Archicad tool component**, as a prototype: one component that reads, writes and creates walls, with the settings grouped and named like the Wall Settings dialog (CLAUDE.md, "Archicad tool components").

It comes in two variants in the new **Design Tools** group:
- **Walls**: the JSON keys are the dialog labels of `ToolSettings/Wall.json` (e.g. `Wall Thickness`, `Home Story`, `Floor Plan Display`).
- **Walls_API**: the same component with the Add-On's own keys, for testing against the commands.

### Inputs → outputs

| Input | Refresh | Execute | Create |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ElementGuid` | elements to read | elements to write | – |
| `ElementID` | – | sets the Element ID (built-in `General_ElementID` property) | same, on the new walls |
| `LayerIndex`, `DrawOrder` | – | set via `SetDetailsOfElements` | same, on the new walls |
| `GeometryAndPositioning_JSON`, `FloorPlanAndSection_JSON`, `Model_JSON` | – | settings to write | settings of the new walls |
| `FavoriteName` | – | – | Favorite the new walls start from |
| `StartPoint`, `EndPoint` | – | – | required, X/Y only |

**Outputs:**
- the four basics, the three JSON objects and `StartPoint`/`EndPoint`, with Z as the bottom elevation;
- `Errors`: one message per element, empty when the element succeeded.

After Execute and Create, the outputs show the real state, read back from Archicad.

### How it works

- **`ElementToolComponent`** is generic: the inputs and outputs come from the tool's `ToolSettings/<Tool>.json`, now embedded in the plugin. There is one JSON per dialog panel (the table's `group`), and a field without a group, such as the coordinates, isn't in any JSON. `WallsComponent` only names the tool, the CreateWalls/ModifyWalls keys and the two geometry inputs.
- **Refresh:** `GetDetailsOfElements`. An element that isn't a wall gets a null entry and a message in `Errors`, so the positions stay aligned with the input.
- **Execute:**
  - settings go to `ModifyWalls`;
  - Home Story, layer and draw order go to `SetDetailsOfElements`;
  - the Element ID goes to `SetPropertyValuesOfElements`.

  Only the given keys are written. Read-only keys are skipped, so a JSON from Refresh can be fed back unchanged. A key that only Create can take, such as Bottom Elevation, gives one remark.
- **Create:**
  - `CreateWalls` gets the keys it accepts, plus begCoordinate/endCoordinate from the points (these always override the JSON) and `favoriteName`;
  - right afterwards, the settings only `ModifyWalls` takes (top link, slant, surfaces, …) are written to the new walls.

  A wall read by Refresh carries both Home Story and Bottom Elevation. CreateWalls would read the elevation as an offset when Home Story is also given, so the elevation is left out in that case, and `bottomOffset` is written after creation.
- **Inputs and keys:**
  - Every list input takes none, one (applied to every element) or one item per element; anything else is an error.
  - Writing accepts both labels and API names, case-insensitively.
  - An unknown key or invalid JSON is reported in that element's message.
- **Buttons:** writes and creates only happen on a button press (Refresh / Execute / Create, also in the context menu). The requests are taken once per solution in `BeforeSolveInstance`, so a press is never lost and works for every branch.

## Not in this prototype

- Classification and Properties panel; Serialize/Deserialize JSON components; aligning outputs to inputs; Document/Viewpoint Tools groups.
- Polygonal walls can be read, but CreateWalls/ModifyWalls only make straight or trapezoid ones.
- The old wall components stay as they are.

## Testing

- Builds with no errors or warnings for `net7.0`, `net48` and `net7.0-windows` (`dotnet build`).
- The embedded `ToolSettings.Wall.json` resource is in all three builds.
- **Not yet run in Grasshopper/Archicad.** Please check in Rhino before relying on it:
  - Refresh a few walls;
  - change `Wall Thickness` in `GeometryAndPositioning_JSON` and press Execute;
  - Create from the same JSON with two points;
  - try one wrong list length and one invalid JSON.

**Checker change:** `tools/check_tool_settings.py` now reads the `GetDetailsOfElements` keys from the tool's details schema (`WallDetails`, `BeamDetails`, … in `CommonSchemaDefinitions.json`). It no longer parses the wall case in `ElementCommands.cpp`, which can't follow the helper functions most other types use. For walls, the schema and the code list the same 51 keys. In `Wall.json`, `commands.getCase` becomes `commands.getSchema`.

## Where the labels come from

The rules are the same as for Wall (CLAUDE.md, "Naming from the Archicad GUI"):
- **Source:** a label is only written when Graphisoft's Archicad 29 help shows it word for word, in the page text or a dialog screenshot of that tool or of a shared page that lists it, or when a DevKit comment names the control. `labelSource` names the page and the screenshot.
- **Verification:** before committing, every label was searched for in the downloaded help pages. 163 of 168 appear in the page text, and the other 5 were checked against their screenshots:
  - Column: Reference Axis of Core;
  - Object / Lamp: Symbol Line Pen;
  - Morph: Cover Fill Pen, Cover Fill Background Pen.

### Left `null` on purpose

Each of these keeps its panel and subgroup:
- **Object/Lamp "Override Object's …" checkboxes:** `useObjLtypes`, `useObjPens` and `useObjSectAttrs` mean the opposite (true = don't override).
- **Slab/Roof `level`:** reading gives the offset from the home story, but Create/Modify take an absolute Z.
- **Beam/Column width/height:** the help only has a combined heading, and the dialog fields are icons.
- **Door/Window sill height:** the dialog value depends on the chosen anchor, while `lower` is only the parapet.
- **Fill foreground/background pens:** no control label in the help.
- **Objects that bundle several controls:** cover fills, surface sets, label text style.

### Fixed

The AC29 header swaps the comments of `API_LabelType::parent` and `parentType`, so `Label.json` gives each member its own sentence.

## Testing

`python tools/check_tool_settings.py` → 24 tables consistent with the Add-On. Each table covers every key exactly once, its labels are unique and each label has a source.

title: View Map: DeleteNavigatorItems rejects folders/TOC items, and item ordering within a folder is unreliable
author: MathiasJon

title: Add a command to reorder Navigator items (works around MoveNavigatorItem's same-parent no-op)
body:
### Summary

Follow-up to #1418/#1419. Confirmed live (AC27, Mac) that `MoveNavigatorItem` (`ACAPI_Navigator_SetNavigatorItemPosition`) **cannot reposition an item within its current parent** - asking it to move an item to the same parent it already has, with a `previousNavigatorItemId` to set its new position, either gets refused (`APIERR_BADPARS`, seen for story-based View Map items) or silently does nothing (seen for plain View Map folders, before #1419 made that failure honest instead of a false `success: true`).

But a **genuine re-parent** (moving an item to a *different* parent, with `previousNavigatorItemId` set) works reliably and respects the requested position exactly - verified repeatedly: created folders `B, A` in a parent `P` (order `[B, A]`), moved an unrelated folder `Q` into `P` with `previousNavigatorItemId: A` → result `[B, A, Q]`, exactly as asked.

That means **a item can always be given its own folder's own slot in the order by bouncing it through a different parent first**:
1. Move the item OUT of its current parent, to any other folder (no position needed - this always succeeds, it's a genuine re-parent).
2. Move it back IN to its original parent, with `previousNavigatorItemId` set to whatever sibling should precede it (another genuine re-parent, into the real target - also always succeeds).

Verified end-to-end: folder `P` had `[B, A, Q]`; bounced `B` out to a different folder then back into `P` with no `previousNavigatorItemId` (meaning "first") → result `[B, A, Q]` unchanged (B was already first, but the bounce itself worked and didn't disturb anything). This is a reliable, repeatable workaround - not a one-off.

### Suggested command

A new command (e.g. `ReorderNavigatorItems` or `SetNavigatorItemsOrder`) taking a parent folder and the full ordered list of its children's `navigatorItemId`s, that:

1. Creates a temporary scratch folder somewhere (e.g. via the same mechanism `CreateViewMapFolder` uses - a sibling of the target parent, or the View Map root), to bounce items through. Must be created fresh each call and deleted at the end, not reused across calls, since there's no guarantee a leftover one from a previous call is still there/empty.
2. Walks the requested order front to back. For each item:
   - If it's already directly after the correct previous sibling in the live tree, skip it (no-op, nothing to do).
   - Otherwise, move it to the scratch folder (`parentNavigatorItemId` = scratch, no `previousNavigatorItemId` needed), then immediately move it back to the real parent with `previousNavigatorItemId` = the previous item in the requested order (or omitted, for the first position).
3. Deletes the scratch folder at the end (works fine for a freshly-created, now-empty folder - confirmed in this session, see #1418's later comments: fresh `CreateViewMapFolder` folders delete without issue, only some pre-existing/corrupted ones didn't).
4. Reports per-item success/failure, similar to other batch commands in this codebase (`#/ExecutionResults`).

### What needs confirming with the DevKit

- Whether `CreateViewMapFolder`'s existing default-parent resolution (when `parentNavigatorItemId` is omitted) is a safe, always-available scratch location, or whether the command should take an explicit location to bounce through to avoid assumptions.
- Whether this works the same way for Layout Book subsets (`SubSetItem`) as for View Map folders - not tested there, only in the View Map.
- Whether story-based views specifically should be excluded/rejected up front (since the re-parent-based bounce moves an item out of its folder temporarily, and a story view might behave differently if its "folder" bounce target isn't a real View Map folder it's allowed in - not tested, since all my repro was with plain folders, not stories, for the actual reordering-via-bounce test specifically).

### Context

Archicad 27 (Mac), live-tested this session while trying to reorder a real project's View Map to match a reference copy - `MoveNavigatorItem`'s same-parent limitation (#1418) blocked that directly, this bounce-based workaround is what would unblock it.

title: Is creating a new Master Layout possible via the API?
body:
## Context

Same use case as #1422 (replicating a Layout Book from one project file to another). The project I'm copying *from* has 13 Master Layouts that don't exist at all in the target project (different `-AR-...-Cartouche...` names).

## What I found

`CreateLayout` takes `masterLayoutName` / `masterNavigatorItemId`, but looking at `DocumentCreationCommands.cpp`, it only *references* an existing Master Layout via `FindMasterLayoutDatabaseByName` (`ACAPI_Database_GetMasterLayoutDatabases`) — I don't see a path that creates a brand new one if the name isn't found.

## Question

Is there any way — via Tapir or the official ArchiCAD JSON API — to create a new Master Layout (not just place/edit content on an existing one)? If not directly, is there a known workaround (e.g. some database-creation call I'm missing, or is this just not exposed by the API at all and has to be done by hand in ArchiCAD)?

Not asking for a new command necessarily — just trying to find out if this is possible at all before I tell the person I'm helping that it has to be done manually.

title: Archicad crashes (internal assertion) after CreateLayout + RenameNavigatorItem + DeleteNavigatorItems in quick succession
body:
### Summary

Hit two Archicad crashes (AC27, Mac) in the same session while scripting Layout Book changes through the JSON API. Got a full stack trace for the second one before Archicad's own bug-report tool auto-sent and deleted the report file. This looks like a genuine Archicad-internal assertion failure, not obviously a bug in Tapir's own code, but the exact call sequence that triggers it is squarely something Tapir callers would do.

### Crash stack (from the Archicad bug report, `.rpt`, before it was deleted)

```
ProjectManager::FindGroup(GS::Guid)
  -> ODB::CommonRefUntyped::TypeCompatibilityViolation()
  -> GS::AssertFailed(...)
  -> ODB::TerminateProgram(...)
  [caller chain:]
APICore::GetNavigatorItem(const API_Guid*, API_NavigatorItem*, ...)
  <- ACAPI::APINavigator(...)
  <- DeleteNavigatorItemsCommand::Execute(const GS::ObjectState&, GS::ProcessControl&) + 0x290
  <- APICommand::ExecuteAddOnCommand::DoExecute(...)
```

So the crash happens inside Archicad's own `ProjectManager::FindGroup`, called from `ACAPI_Navigator_GetNavigatorItem` - the very first call `DeleteNavigatorItemsCommand::Execute` makes (`NavigatorCommands.cpp`) to resolve the guid it was given. `TypeCompatibilityViolation` is an internal Archicad sanity check that something stored under a guid is not the type the code expected - this is Archicad's own state getting inconsistent, not an obviously-invalid guid passed in (the guid was a real, just-created layout's navigator item id).

### Repro sequence (reconstructed from the session, not yet isolated to a minimal case)

1. `CreateLayout` with a `masterLayoutName` that does not exist yet (lets the command auto-create a new master layout) - a throwaway regular layout + a new master layout are both created.
2. `RenameNavigatorItem` on the **newly created master layout's** navigator item, right after.
3. `DeleteNavigatorItems` on the **throwaway regular layout's** navigator item (a different, unrelated item, created in step 1) - **this call crashes**.

This is the second crash of the session; an earlier, less precisely diagnosed one (report auto-deleted before I could inspect it) happened during a *batch* `CreateLayout` call where several entries referenced the same (not-yet-existing) `masterLayoutName` - possibly a related or the same underlying issue, since both involve master layout creation followed quickly by another Navigator-mutating call.

### What I don't know

- Whether this is specific to `DeleteNavigatorItems`, or any Navigator-mutating call would crash the same way if it immediately follows a `CreateLayout` + `RenameNavigatorItem` pair.
- Whether a delay, an explicit redraw/database-switch, or wrapping these in separate undoable commands (rather than back-to-back calls from script) avoids it - haven't had the chance to test a workaround yet given the crash itself blocks further testing in the same session.
- Whether this reproduces on a fresh/minimal project, or is specific to the fairly large, long-lived project state (233+ Layout Book items, created/renamed/moved extensively via the API earlier in the same session) this was running against.

### Context

Archicad 27 (Mac), Tapir built from a mix of `upstream/main` + PR #825 (`claude/issue-818-layout-master`) + my own `ReorderNavigatorItems` addition, live-tested against a real project copy while syncing its Layout Book structure to match a reference. Filing this now while the stack trace is still available, since Archicad's own bug-report tool auto-sends and deletes the `.rpt`/`.rpta` files within roughly a minute of a crash - a maintainer with a similarly large test project may want to try reproducing the exact 3-call sequence above to narrow it down further.
author: MathiasJon

title: Grasshopper coverage checklist of the Tapir commands
body:
This adds a checklist like the Archicad API coverage one. It shows which Tapir Add-On commands the Grasshopper plugin covers, and whether the components cover each command's parameters.

## What it shows

For every command registered in `AddOnMain.cpp` (read the way `tools/generate_addon_docs.py` reads it):
- **Status:** ✅ a component calls it on `main`, 🔀 merged but not yet released, 🚧 an open PR adds a component for it, 🙋 an open issue asks for one, ⬜ open, ⛔ skipped, ➖ not applicable (from `tools/gh_coverage_rules.json`).
- **Parameters** of a used command: 🟢 every parameter of its input schema has an input, 🟡 the rest is reachable through a JSON input (`AdditionalSettings`, …), 🟠 some parameters are missing. Each row lists its components and the parameters they don't name.

Current state: **288 of 317** commands have a component (90 %). Of those, 234 are 🟢, 37 🟡 and 17 🟠. Most 🟠 rows are the `fields` filter of the attribute getters, plus `SetDetailsOfElements` (`floorIndex`/`layerIndex`/`drawIndex`) and `GetZoneBoundaries` (`zones`).

## How it is detected

`tools/generate_gh_coverage.py` reads the plugin's C# code without running it (standard library only):
- A command counts as used when a class names it, for example as `CommandName => "X"`, and sends it with `ToAddOn`. The send can be in the class itself or in a base class. A same-named official command sent with `ToArchicad` does not count. Navigator commands such as `CreateViewMapFolder` go through the official API, so they stay open.
- A parameter counts as covered when the code names it. That can be a string literal or a dotted part of one, a member of an anonymous object (`new { zoneElementId }`), or a `[JsonProperty]` of a type the component uses. The code searched is the sending class, its base classes, the classes derived from an abstract sender, and the helper classes they call directly.
- This only shows that the code names a parameter, not that the parameter works.

## Changes

- `tools/generate_gh_coverage.py` and `tools/gh_coverage_rules.json` (`GenerateDocumentation` is not applicable).
- `.github/workflows/api_coverage.yml` runs the new generator in the same job, compares against the plugin at the latest release tag, and publishes `gh-coverage.{json,md}`, `gh-coverage-summary.md`, `gh-coverage-badge.json` and `gh-coverage{,-dark}.svg` to the `api-coverage` branch. It still never checks out PR code.
- `tools/fetch_api_coverage_github_data.py` now also collects the lines open PRs add to `grasshopper-plugin/**/*.cs`. `generate_api_coverage.py` filters those out, so the API checklist is unchanged.
- `docs/gh-coverage/index.html` is the searchable page, adapted from the API coverage page: filter by parameter coverage, components and missing parameters on each row, and a "claim" link that opens an issue asking for a component.
- README badge and summary image, and notes in CLAUDE.md.

## Testing

- Ran the generator on the plugin, against the 1.7.2 release, and with sample PR and issue data. Each status came out where expected.
- Spot-checked the detection by hand: the `Resources.Designer.cs` resource names, `ToArchicad` navigator components, anonymous-object parameters, the electrical placement helper and the abstract `AbsGetDetails`.
- Checked the page in Chromium at 1280 px and 390 px (no script errors, no horizontal scroll) and the light and dark SVGs.
- The page and badge will show data after the first workflow run on `main` once this is merged.

title: Built-in scripts: fix "Can't find a usable init.tcl" on macOS
body:
A user on macOS got this error when starting a built-in script (AutomaticNumberingBasedOnPolyline) from the Tapir palette:

```
_tkinter.TclError: Can't find a usable init.tcl in the following directories:
/tools/deps/lib/tcl8.6 ~/.cache/uv/environments-v2/automaticnumberingbasedonpolyline-…/lib/tcl8.6 …
This probably means that Tcl wasn't installed properly.
```

## Cause

uv runs each script in its own virtual environment (`~/.cache/uv/environments-v2/…`). The macOS builds of uv's Python (python-build-standalone) link Tcl statically into Python and have no `libtcl` next to `lib/tcl8.6`. So Tcl searches for `init.tcl` in two places: next to the running executable, and in its build-time path `/tools/deps/lib/tcl8.6`. Neither is the Python installation (`~/.local/share/uv/python/cpython-3.12.11-macos-aarch64-none`), which is where `lib/tcl8.6/init.tcl` and `lib/tk8.6/tk.tcl` are. I checked that layout in the macOS aarch64 build of 3.12.11. Linux builds ship `libtcl8.6.so` and find the scripts on their own.

## Fix

At import, `builtin-scripts/utilities/ui.py` sets `TCL_LIBRARY` and `TK_LIBRARY` to the installation's `lib/tcl8.*` and `lib/tk8.*` (under `sys.base_prefix`). It only does this when those folders exist and the user has not set the variables. Windows is skipped, because Windows Python sets these variables itself. All three built-in scripts open their windows through `ui.py`, so they all get the fix.

## Testing

- In a uv script environment with uv's Python 3.12.11 on Linux, the variables point at the installation's `lib/tcl8.6` and `lib/tk8.6`, and Tcl initializes: `tk.Tk()` gets past Tcl and stops only at the missing display. With a wrong `TCL_LIBRARY` the same setup gives the reported error.
- Not run on macOS yet. Please check on a Mac that a built-in script opens its window from the Tapir palette.

title: Built-in scripts: Property Highlighter, Project Health Check, Solid Operation Explorer, Batch Publisher
body:
Adds four built-in scripts to the Tapir palette. They are similar to BIMDots' Property Highlighter, Project Health Check and Solid Operation Explorer add-ons, plus a scheduled batch publisher. All four use tkinter and the shared `ScriptWindow`, like the existing scripts, and need only the standard library.

## Scripts

- **Property Highlighter**: pick a property (with search) and a scope (selection, current story or whole project, plus an optional element type). Elements are coloured by value, with a legend that shows a colour swatch and an element count for each value.
  - Number values can be grouped into 2–12 ranges on a blue→red gradient. Displayed values such as `1 234,50 m²` or `1,234.5` are parsed.
  - Selecting legend rows highlights only those values; double-clicking a value selects its elements. "Wireframe in 3D" is an option.
- **Project Health Check** offers 9 checks you can switch on and off:
  - elements without an Element ID
  - zones with the same number
  - unclassified elements in a chosen classification system
  - duplicate elements in the same place (same type, story and 3D box)
  - elements under 1 cm
  - elements more than N m from the origin
  - elements on hidden layers
  - stories without elements
  - layers that no floor plan element uses

  Findings are grouped by check and coloured by severity. Selecting a finding highlights it and double-clicking selects it. Findings can be exported to `.xlsx` (written with the standard library) or CSV, and "Create Issues" makes one Issue per check with the elements attached. Hotlinked elements are skipped.
- **Solid Operation Explorer**: lists each target / operation / operator link with the operator's layer. A link whose two elements' 3D boxes don't touch is marked "Do not touch". For the upwards and downwards subtractions only the plan overlap and the side facing the target count. Targets are highlighted blue and operators orange. Chosen links can be removed with `RemoveSolidElementLinks` (one undo step).
- **Batch Publisher**: publishes the checked Publisher Sets now, every N minutes or hours, or daily at HH:MM on chosen weekdays.
  - Before publishing it can receive Teamwork changes (`TeamworkReceive`) and update the drawings on all layouts (`UpdateDrawings`).
  - Output goes to each set's own folder, or to a chosen folder with an optional dated subfolder per run and one folder per set.
  - Settings are saved per project in `Documents/Tapir/BatchPublisher.json`, and runs are logged in the window and in `Documents/Tapir/BatchPublisher log.csv`.
  - The schedule runs while the window is open, and closing the window asks first. The palette runs one script at a time, so no other script can run meanwhile. The schedule stops if Archicad stops answering.

## Shared changes
- `utilities/archicad.py`: `batched`, `get_story_names`, and `get_elements(scope, types, filters)`. `get_details_of_elements` now sends its calls in batches of 1,000 elements, with the same result.
- `utilities/export.py`: `write_table` writes CSV, or an `.xlsx` with a bold, frozen header row and an autofilter.
- `utilities/ui.py`: `ScriptWindow(keep_on_top=...)` and `run(can_close=...)`, both optional; the existing scripts are unaffected.

## Testing
No Archicad was available, so the scripts were run under Xvfb against a mock Archicad JSON server with a small test project. They were driven through their methods and checked with screenshots:
- **Property Highlighter**: the legend, colours, range grouping, number parsing, highlight of selected legend rows, and selection.
- **Project Health Check**: every check found its planted problem. The export opens in openpyxl and LibreOffice. Issues were created.
- **Solid Operation Explorer**: listing, the "Do not touch" detection, the filter, and link removal.
- **Batch Publisher**: receive, drawing update, publish to a chosen folder, the failure path, the interval schedule actually firing, daily next-run computation, input validation, and settings saved and reloaded.

Still to test in real Archicad: the publish and drawing-update commands on a real project, `RemoveSolidElementLinks` undo, and how the windows look on Windows and macOS.

title: ShowScriptUI: let the palette get smaller than 600x450
body:
## Symptom

`ShowScriptUI` never makes the Script UI palette smaller than 600 x 450:

- `width` / `height` below 600 / 450 are ignored for that dimension. For example, `Examples/test_script_ui_layers.py` asks for 380 x 480 but gets a palette 600 px wide (measured on Archicad 30, see below).
- `autoHeight: true` grows the palette for a long page, but a short page stops at 450 px with empty space below it.

## Cause

The palette's `GDLG` resource (`ID_SCRIPTUI_PALETTE` in `RINT/AddOn.grc`) is 600 x 450. That size is meant as the starting size, but DG also keeps it as the dialog's minimum client size, so every `SetClientSize` / `SetClientHeight` below it is clamped.

## Fix

In `ScriptUIPalette::ShowWithHTML`:

- `SetGrowType` is moved up, so the grow type is set before the size.
- `SetMinClientSize (160, 60)` lowers the minimum before `SetClientSize` applies the requested size.

160 x 60 is only a floor so the palette cannot collapse to nothing; any small value works. With `resizable: true`, this is also the new limit when the user drags the palette smaller.

I first tried `SetMinClientSize` in the constructor, before `BeginEventProcessing`. It had no effect on Archicad 29, so the call is in `ShowWithHTML` and runs on every show.

## How to test

1. Run `Examples/test_script_ui_layers.py`. The palette should open 380 px wide (before: 600 px).
2. Call `ShowScriptUI` with `width: 300, height: 200` and a page that reports `window.innerWidth` / `window.innerHeight` through `ACAPI.SubmitResult`. The values should be 300 / 200 (before: 600 / 450).
3. Call `ShowScriptUI` with `autoHeight: true` and a page a few lines tall. The palette should shrink to the page height (before: stuck at 450 px).
4. Sizes of 600 x 450 and above, and `resizable: false`, give exactly the requested size.

## Tested

- Builds: Archicad 29 and Archicad 30, Windows, Release, VS 2022. No warnings.
- Archicad 29 (Windows) with the same change on my fork:
  - `width` 300 / 400 / 500 give a page `window.innerWidth` of 300 / 400 / 500.
  - `autoHeight` shrinks the palette to a 159 px page.
- Archicad 30 (Windows): see below.
- Not run on macOS.

## Run on Archicad 30

Archicad 30.3001 JPN, Windows, display scaling 125 %. I put this PR's build in place of the installed Tapir for the test, then put the original back. "Before" is a 1.7.2 build whose Script UI sources and `GDLG` resource are the same as in `main`.

The page reported `window.innerWidth` x `window.innerHeight`. The palette's Windows client rectangle was 1.25 times these values in every case. Each build ran the same list of calls twice in a row, in this order:

| Requested | Before, run 1 | Before, run 2 | This PR, runs 1 and 2 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 300 x 200 | 600 x 450 | 600 x 450 | 300 x 200 |
| 400 x 300 | 600 x 450 | 700 x 550 | 400 x 300 |
| 500 x 400 | 700 x 550 | 600 x 450 | 500 x 400 |
| 380 x 480, `resizable: false` | 600 x 480 | 600 x 482 | 380 x 480 |
| 300 x 200, `resizable: false` | 300 x 200 | 300 x 200 | 300 x 200 |
| 700 x 500 | 600 x 480 | 600 x 482 | 700 x 500 |
| 400 x 600, `autoHeight: true`, page 46 px tall | 600 x 450 | 600 x 450 | 400 x 60 |

- Before, the size also depended on the earlier calls: the same request gave different sizes in the two runs. 700 x 500 right after a `resizable: false` call came out as 600 x 482, even though it is above the minimum. With `SetGrowType` before `SetClientSize`, every request gives exactly the requested size, the same in both runs.
- With `autoHeight`, the 46 px page now stops at the new 60 px minimum instead of 450 px.

title: Elements: read and set the legacy property objects (by criteria / individual) and their descriptors
body:
Projects migrated from older Archicad versions still link **property objects** (the GDL library parts of the old listing system) to construction elements, either **by criteria**, **individually**, or both. The same links exist on the tool defaults. These links drive the old component/descriptor listings and are invisible to the new property API. Scripts cleaning up an old template need to:
- find which elements and defaults still carry a property object,
- see which descriptors those objects contribute,
- and unlink them in bulk.

Tapir can't read or change any of this today.

Please add, in the Element group:

- **`GetPropertyObjectsOfElements`:**
  - **Input:** `elements`.
  - **Output per element:** `propertyObjects`, a list of `{libraryPartIndex, isIndividuallyAssigned}`, or an error.
  - Each entry also carries the library part's `name` and `guid`, read with `ACAPI_LibraryPart_Get`, so scripts don't have to resolve indices themselves.
- **`GetLinkedPropertyObjectsOfElements`:**
  - **Input:** `elements`, where each entry can also be `{ "elementType": "<type>" }` instead of an `elementId`. That form reads the element defaults (`guid` = `APINULLGuid`).
  - **Output per entry:** `{ linkByCriteria: bool, individualLibraryPartIndex: int (0 = none), criteriaLibraryPartIndices: [int] }`, plus names and guids as above, or an error.
- **`SetLinkedPropertyObjectsOfElements`:**
  - **Input:** `[{ elementId | elementType, linkByCriteria: bool, individualLibraryPartIndex: int }]`, where `0` removes the individual link.
  - **Result:** an `executionResults` entry per item.
  - Run everything in one `ACAPI_CallUndoableCommand`.
- **`GetDescriptorsOfElements`:**
  - **Input:** `elements`.
  - **Output per element:** `descriptors`, a list of `{libraryPartIndex, setIndex, index, status}`, or an error. `status` is one of `Normal`, `Deleted`, `Local`, from `APIDBRef_*`.

Use the same `libraryPartIndex` as the `index` returned by `GetAvailableLibraryParts`, so the outputs can be joined.

### API

AC27–AC30, declarations and doc text from the AC30 `Inc/ACAPinc.h`. AC27–AC29 have only the pointer overloads:

```cpp
/**
 * @brief Returns property objects of the element.
 * @param elemHead [in] The element to get the properties for.
 * @param propRefs [out] List of property objects.
 * @param nProp [out] Number of the property objects.
 * @return
 * 			- NoError - The function has completed with success.
 * 			- APIERR_BADPARS - propRefs or nProp is nullptr
 * 			- APIERR_BADID - Incorrect elemHead was specified
 * 			- APIERR_MEMFULL - Not enough memory to get the properties
 * @remarks This function is used to get the list of property objects for a linked element. The properties can be associated with construction elements by criteria or by individual direct assignment. This applies to all construction elements.
 */
__APIEXPORT GSErrCode ACAPI_Element_GetPropertyObjects (const API_Elem_Head *elemHead, API_PropertyObjectRefType ***propRefs, Int32 *nProp);
// AC30 only, the pointer overload above is [[deprecated]] there:
__APIEXPORT GSErrCode ACAPI_Element_GetPropertyObjects (const API_Elem_Head &elemHead, std::vector<API_PropertyObjectRefType> &propRefs);

/**
 * @brief Returns the descriptors of an element.
 * @param elemHead [in] The element you want to get the descriptors for.
 * @param descRef [out] List of the descriptors.
 * @param nDesc [out] Number of the descriptors in the list.
 * @return
 * 			- APIERR_BADPARS - descRef is nullptr or nDesc is nullptr.
 * 			- APIERR_BADID - Incorrect elemHead was specified.
 * 			- APIERR_MEMFULL - Not enough memory to get the descriptors.
 * @remarks This function is used to get information for every descriptor of an element. These descriptors are in the property objects of the element. This applies to all the construction elements.
 */
__APIEXPORT GSErrCode ACAPI_Element_GetDescriptors (const API_Elem_Head *elemHead, API_DescriptorRefType ***descRef, Int32 *nDesc);

/**
 * @brief Retrieves property objects linked to an element or the element default.
 * @param head [in] Header of the element (only field guid is used). Properties linked to the default element are retrieved when guid is APINULLGuid
 * @param criteria [out] Determines whether the matching properties by criteria are linked to the element
 * @param individuallyLibInd [out] Library index of individually assigned property (value zero means no individual property assigned)
 * @param critLibInds [out] Aray of the library indices of linked properties matching the criteria
 * @param nCrits [out] Number of linked properties matching the criteria
 * @remarks ... at most one individual assignment can be applied to an element ... If no element is specified (ie. guid is APINULLGuid), the default settings of the given element type are retrieved.
 * 			Any of the arguments except head can be nullptr, in this case the function retrieves only the rest of the parameters.
 * 			Remember to free the critLibInds array when not needed any more.
 */
__APIEXPORT GSErrCode ACAPI_ElementLink_GetLinkedPropertyObjects (const API_Elem_Head *head, bool *criteria, Int32 *individuallyLibInd, Int32 **critLibInds, Int32 *nCrits);
// AC30 only, the pointer overload above is [[deprecated]] there:
__APIEXPORT GSErrCode ACAPI_ElementLink_GetLinkedPropertyObjects (const API_Elem_Head &head, bool &criteria, Int32 &individuallyLibInd, std::vector<Int32> &critLibInds);

/**
 * @brief Link property objects to an element or the element default.
 * @param head [in] Header of the element (only fields type and guid are used). The setting is applied to element defaults if guid is APINULLGuid.
 * @param criteria [in] Determines whether the matching properties by criteria need to be linked to the element
 * @param individuallyLibInd [in] Library index of individually selected property to be linked to the element (value zero means no individual property is to be assigned)
 * @return
 * 			- NoError - The function has completed successfully.
 * 			- APIERR_BADPARS - head is nullptr
 * 			- APIERR_BADID - Incorrect type was specified, or an element with the specified guid was not found.
 * 			- APIERR_MEMFULL - Not enough memory to set the properties
 */
__APIEXPORT GSErrCode ACAPI_ElementLink_SetLinkedPropertyObjects (API_Elem_Head *head, bool criteria, Int32 individuallyLibInd);
```

Structs, from `APIdefs_Elements.h` (same fields in AC25–AC30; a `typedef struct` on AC25):

```cpp
#define APIDBRef_Normal   0   // exists in database
#define APIDBRef_Deleted  1   // referenced, but deleted from the database
#define APIDBRef_Local    2   // defined in the Library Part

struct API_PropertyObjectRefType {
	Int32  libIndex;     // "Index of the library part, this is a property object"
	bool   assign;       // "This member is true, if the property object is invidually assignment."
	char   filler_1;  short filler_2;  Int32 filler_3[2];
};

struct API_DescriptorRefType {
	Int32  libIndex;     // "Index of the library part, place of the descriptor declaring"
	Int32  setIndex;     // "Index of the listing database set, if status equals APIDBRef_Normal."
	Int32  index;        // "If status equals APIDBRef_Normal, then index is index of the descriptor in the set, if status equals APIDBRef_Local, then index is index of the descriptor in the library part."
	Int32  status;       // "APIDBRef_Normal, APIDBRef_Local, APIDBRef_Deleted"
	Int32  filler_3[8];
};
```

AC25/AC26:
- `ACAPI_Element_GetPropertyObjects` and `ACAPI_Element_GetDescriptors` have the same names and pointer signatures.
- The link functions are named `ACAPI_Element_GetLinkedPropertyObjects` and `ACAPI_Element_SetLinkedPropertyObjects`, with the same parameters (spelled `inviduallyLibInd`).
- Add `TAPIR_` wrappers in `MigrationHelper.hpp`, gated on `ServerMainVers_2700` as the existing ones are.

Use the pointer overloads on every version, so one code path builds everywhere. Free the handles and the `critLibInds` pointer with `BMKillHandle` / `BMKillPtr`. If the AC30 deprecation warnings fail the build, use the AC30 `std::vector` overloads behind `#ifdef ServerMainVers_3000`.

### Notes, to verify in Archicad

- **Test project:** use a project with an old-style property object, for example a template migrated from Archicad ≤ 20, or a property GDL object assigned in the element's Listing and Labeling panel. Confirm that `GetPropertyObjectsOfElements` and `GetLinkedPropertyObjectsOfElements` agree. Say on the pull request whether projects without any property objects just return empty lists.
- **The `0` index:** check that `individualLibraryPartIndex = 0` really removes the individual link. Check that `linkByCriteria = false` keeps the individual link.
- **Element defaults:** check that `SetLinkedPropertyObjectsOfElements` with `elementType` changes the tool defaults, and needs no undoable command or does not break inside one.

- **Descriptor status:** check what `status` and `setIndex` look like for a `Local` descriptor, and document that in the schema.

### Example

Add `Examples/property_objects.py`:
- list all walls and print their property objects, linked objects and descriptors;
- remove the individual property object from the first wall that has one;
- read the wall back.

title: Palette: stop a running script when Archicad quits (crash on quit)
body:
## Symptom

If a script started from the Tapir palette is still running when Archicad is closed, Archicad crashes while quitting and the Bug Reporter opens. Any long-running script does it, for example one that keeps a Script UI page and a relay loop alive until the user closes the page.

Reproduced on Archicad 29 every time with this script in the custom scripts folder:

```python
import sys, time
sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8", line_buffering=True)
for i in range(600):
    print(f"test {i}")
    time.sleep(1)
```

Run it from the palette, wait a few seconds, close Archicad.

## Cause

Two things outlive the add-on:

1. `TapirPalette::ExecuteScript` runs `UIUpdaterThread` on the palette's `GS::ThreadedExecutor`. The thread loops on `process.WaitFor (10 ms)` / `ReadFromChannels ()` until the script exits. `FreeData` does not stop the script or the thread, so after the add-on is unloaded the thread keeps running on the destroyed palette. In the crash dump the faulting call is `GS::Process::GetStandardErrorChannel`, called from the address range the add-on had occupied.
2. For each piece of output the thread posts an `OutputUpdateTask` (and `IconUpdateTask` at start and end) to `GS::MessageLoopExecutor`. Tasks posted while Archicad is already closing are no longer run. Archicad destroys them after the add-on is unloaded, and the main thread crashes in `GS::CountedPtrImpl<GS::Runnable,...>::~CountedPtrImpl`, because the tasks' destructors are in the add-on. This one shows up once (1) is fixed.

## Fix

- New `TapirPalette::StopRunningScriptOnQuit ()`, called first in `FreeData`. It:
  - sets a `quitting` flag,
  - kills the running script with `process.Kill ()`, as the palette's Stop button does,
  - waits up to 2 seconds for the output reader to return.
- The output reader returns as soon as `quitting` is set, without touching the process, and posts nothing to the message loop after that.
- The palette keeps a reference to each task the reader posts until the task has run. In normal use, the reference is dropped after the task has run (on the next post, not inside the task's own `Run`). Tasks still queued at quit are kept alive on purpose and never freed, so that Archicad discarding them later does not call into the unloaded add-on.

## How to test

1. Put the script above in the custom scripts folder and reload the scripts.
2. Run it from the palette, wait a few seconds, then close Archicad.
3. Before: Archicad crashes while quitting and the Bug Reporter opens. After: Archicad quits normally, no crash report is written, and the script's process is gone.
4. Normal use: run a short script. The Run button switches to Stop and back, and the output and `ExitCode: 0` appear in the Session Report as before. Closing Archicad afterwards does not crash.

## Tested

- Builds: Archicad 29 and Archicad 30, Windows, Release, VS 2022, on `main`. No warnings.
- Archicad 29.0 JPN (5101), Windows, with the same change on my fork:
  - Before: crash on quit with the script running. The crash was in `GS::Process::GetStandardErrorChannel`, in the same place as a crash a user hit while closing Archicad with a long-running palette script open.
  - With only part (1) of the fix: crash on quit in `~CountedPtrImpl<GS::Runnable>` on the main thread.
  - After: no crash with the script running. No crash when quitting after a short script had finished. In both cases there was no new crash report.
- Archicad 30.3001 JPN, Windows, with the same change on my fork: no crash with the script running, and no new crash report. I did not run the "before" case on Archicad 30.
- Not run on macOS. The change itself is platform-independent: `std::atomic`, `std::mutex` and the existing `GS::Process` / `GS::ThreadedExecutor` calls.

title: Add MoveGraphicOverrideRules
body:
## Summary

Adds **`MoveGraphicOverrideRules`** (1.7.3, Archicad 27+), which exposes `ACAPI_GraphicalOverride_MoveOverrideRule`. It is the one rule group operation of the Graphic Overrides dialog that no command or open PR covers yet: moving a rule to another group, or to another place in its own group.

- Input: `graphicOverrideRules: [{ graphicOverrideRuleId, ruleGroupName, beforeGraphicOverrideRuleId? }]`, processed in the given order.
- The target group is found by name and created when no group has that name, like `CreateGraphicOverrideRules` does. A group created for an item whose move fails is deleted again.
- `beforeGraphicOverrideRuleId` puts the rule in front of a rule of the target group. If it is left out, the rule becomes the last rule of the group. If the given rule is not in the target group, the item is refused.
- Response: `executionResults`, one per item. All moves run in one undoable command. The error message names the reason when the target group already holds a rule with the same name, and for built-in rules (the renovation rules), which Archicad refuses to move (`APIERR_NOACCESSRIGHT`).

## Implementation note

Archicad refuses to move a rule into the group it is already in: `MoveOverrideRule` returns `APIERR_NAMEALREADYUSED`, because the rule's own name is taken in the target group. When the target group is the rule's own group, the command therefore builds the new order of that group and calls `ACAPI_GraphicalOverride_SetOverrideRuleOrder` instead.

## Testing

Tested live on Archicad 29 (macOS, arm64 build of this branch), 13/13 checks passing:

- Moving into a group that does not exist yet creates the group.
- Moving in front of a rule of the target group.
- Inside the own group: moving to the end and to the front; moving in front of itself changes nothing.
- Two moves in one call are applied in input order.
- Refused, with nothing changed:
  - a rule whose name is already used in the target group;
  - a `beforeGraphicOverrideRuleId` from another group;
  - an unknown rule;
  - a rule of the built-in renovation group (message names it; the target group created for it is removed again).
- Error messages for a taken name and a built-in rule.
- Cleanup leaves the project's groups as before.

The example `archicad-addon/Examples/move_graphic_override_rules.py` was run against the same build. The branch also builds for Archicad 30.

title: Auto Merge: ignore the API Coverage check, ask again when mergeability is UNKNOWN
body:
Two bugs in `claude_auto_merge.yml` hold back bot PRs that clear every other gate.

**1. The cancelled API Coverage check.** `api_coverage.yml` runs on `pull_request_target` for every PR event, with one global `cancel-in-progress` group. With 250+ open PRs, its `update` check on most PR heads ends up cancelled, and gate 2 treats that as not green. In the 23 Oct 21:13 UTC sweep, 16 of the bot PRs for parikshit99's issues were skipped only for `cancel update`, among them #1018, #1019, #1016, #952 and #967–970. API Coverage never tests the PR's code, so gate 2 now leaves that workflow out.

**2. Mergeability read only once.** GitHub recomputes mergeability in the background after every push to `main`, and the first read is often `UNKNOWN`. The sweep read it once and skipped the PR: 25 of those PRs showed `mergeable=UNKNOWN`. The REST API reports `mergeable: true` for #1204, #1157, #1167, #1289 and #1304. The sweep now asks again up to 3 times, 5 seconds apart, before skipping.

No other gate changes: who the author is, the review delay, protected paths and labels are all as before. The file is under `.github/`, so a maintainer has to merge this by hand.

title: Steward: merge main with an App token, act on why a fix pushed nothing
body:
Of the 129 open bot PRs labelled `needs-maintainer`, 125 were handed over by "Hand over if nothing was pushed". There were two causes:
1. About 100: the fix run's `git merge origin/main` could not be pushed, because `GITHUB_TOKEN` may not push main's `.github/workflows` changes.
2. About 25: the run pushed nothing on purpose. The finding was wrong, the CI failure was transient, or the PR waits for an unmerged earlier part.

This PR changes **release-critical paths** (`.github/`), so it needs maintainer review. It will not auto-merge.

## Changes
**`claude_bot_pr_steward.yml`**
- **Merging main (fix job).** A new step, "Merge main", runs without a model before the model step. It runs when the PR conflicts with main, or when the sweep asks for a merge (new input `merge_main`).
  - A clean merge is pushed at once with a GitHub App installation token (Contents and Workflows write). The model does not run.
  - On conflicts, the model only resolves them in the working tree. It gets a narrower tool set: `git add`/`git rm`, no commit, merge or push.
  - The push happens in a separate job, `push-merge`, on a fresh runner that never ran the model. The model's allowed `git show/diff/log --output=` can write any file on its own runner, so the token never goes there. `push-merge`:
    - merges the same two commits again in a new clone;
    - takes only the conflicted files from the model's working tree (uploaded as an artifact, treated as data);
    - refuses leftover conflict markers, symlinks and missing resolutions;
    - commits and pushes with `core.hooksPath=/dev/null` and `core.fsmonitor=false`. The token appears only on the command line of the fetch and the push, never in a config file. The push is never forced.
  - A conflict under `.github/`, `tools/`, `archicad-addon/Tools/` or `archicad-addon/Installer/` is never given to the model, so those folders are always exactly what git's merge produced.
  - **Without the App secrets:** if main brings workflow changes, the PR is handed over straight away, without a model run: "merge main into it with Update branch (or set up the steward's GitHub App …)". Otherwise the model merges main as before.
- **No double runs.** A push with the App token starts the build checks' `pull_request` runs by itself (a `GITHUB_TOKEN` push does not).
  - The sweep now looks at `actions/runs?head_sha=` and treats any queued or running build on the head as started or still running. This also covers the moment before its check runs exist, and a re-run of failed jobs.
  - The sweep's "build checks refuse a dispatch" handover now starts a merge-only fix when the App is set up.
- **Outcome markers.** The fix prompt now ends the comment with `<!-- steward-fix-outcome: OUTCOME NONCE -->`. A step without a model reads it; only this run's comment with this run's nonce counts. The decision moved from the fix job to `restart`, which runs no model:
  - `transient-ci`: re-runs the failed jobs of the failed build checks (`gh run rerun --failed`), at most twice per PR.
  - `review-disputed`: dispatches a fresh review, at most twice per PR, then hands over. While that review is queued or running, the sweep starts no fix.
  - `waits-for:#N`: sets the commit status `steward-fix` to pending ("waits for #N"). That also holds auto-merge back. The sweep skips the PR, with no label, until #N is merged, then sets the status to success and carries on. If #N was closed unmerged, the PR is handed over.
  - `merge-blocked`, `stuck` or no marker: handed over at once, as before.
  - Every such run still counts as a fix round, so `BOT_PR_MAX_FIX_ROUNDS` still bounds everything.
- `mergeable` is now read again while it is `UNKNOWN`.

**`claude_pr_review.yml`**
- Skips the `pull_request_target` run when a bot pushes to an issue-bot PR (that is the App's merge push). The steward dispatches the review once the builds are green. A person's push is still reviewed.
- On a re-review, the steward fix run's comment counts as a reply to each finding it answers, so a disputed finding gets judged again.

**`claude_auto_merge.yml`**: comment only. It said only the verdict job holds `statuses: write`; now it says only jobs without a model do.

**`CLAUDE.md`**: CI section updated.

## Setup the maintainer has to do
1. Create a GitHub App owned by the ENZYME-APD organization:
   - repository permissions **Contents: Read and write** and **Workflows: Read and write** (Metadata read is implied);
   - no webhook.
2. Install it on this repository only.
3. Add these repository secrets:
   - `TAPIR_BOT_APP_ID`: the App ID;
   - `TAPIR_BOT_APP_PRIVATE_KEY`: a generated private key, the whole `.pem`.
4. If a ruleset restricts pushes to `claude/**` branches, allow the App.

Until the secrets exist, the steward behaves as it does today, except that the handover message is clearer and comes without a wasted model run.

## Not done here
- **The 129 PRs already labelled:** the steward doesn't touch them until the label is removed. Once the App is set up, removing `needs-maintainer` hands each one back with its counts reset.
- **Testing:** the YAML parses and every `run:` script passes `bash -n`, checked locally. actionlint wasn't available. I ran the `push-merge` script against a throwaway local repo: it refused a leftover marker and a missing resolution, and pushed a correct merge commit with main's workflow change and a resolved deletion. Nothing here has run on GitHub yet.

title: Do not open an empty Script UI palette when Archicad starts
body:
## What changed

`ScriptUIPalette::PaletteControlCallBack` now ignores `APIPalMsg_OpenPalette` until a script has shown a page with `ShowScriptUI` in the current session, which is when the palette instance gets created.

## Why

The Script UI palette is registered with `ACAPI_RegisterModelessWindow`, so Archicad saves whether it was open in the work environment. If it was open at the last quit, the next start sends `APIPalMsg_OpenPalette`. The old handler then created the palette and showed it. The HTML a script loaded is never saved, and that script isn't running any more, so Archicad started with an empty "Tapir Script UI" window.

When the request is ignored, `APIPalMsg_IsPaletteVisible` reports the palette as hidden, so Archicad should save it as closed at the next quit. Restoring a window layout after a script has shown a page still brings the palette back with that page.

## For reviewers

- The only other code that creates the instance is `ShowScriptUI`. Every other caller checks `HasInstance ()` first, so `HasInstance ()` is enough to tell whether a page was shown.
- Only the AC29 build was compiled locally; the other versions are covered by CI.

## Tested in Archicad 29

Each run quit Archicad with the Script UI palette open, then started Archicad again with a new project.

| Step | Released Tapir | This build |
|---|---|---|
| Start after quitting with the palette open | Empty palette appeared, `GetScriptUIResult` reported `isOpen: true` (bug reproduced) | No palette, `isOpen: false` |
| `ShowScriptUI` with a page | — | The page is displayed |
| Page calls `ACAPI.SubmitResult` and `ACAPI.ClosePalette` | — | `GetScriptUIResult` returned the result, then `isOpen: false` |

body:
This continues #1298. Five of its six parts (#1299, #1300, #1301, #1304, #1305) are merged; part 4 (#1302) is still open. Each part left items out, saying they needed a DevKit check or a design decision. Below are the 95 functions of #1298 that no merged or open pull request uses yet. Each comes with its declaration from the AC28–AC30 DevKits, and the enum values and design decisions the parts asked for. As the requester, I've made those decisions. Everything here is Archicad 28+ or 29+, as marked, and must be gated with `ServerMainVers_2800` / `ServerMainVers_2900` like the existing commands.

## 1. The Opening enums, and small additions

`GetOpeningDetails`, `SetOpeningDetails`, `GetOpeningFloorPlanParameters` and `SetOpeningFloorPlanParameters` (AC29+) get the settings parts 2 and 3 left out. Enum values go over JSON as their DevKit names:
- `constraint`: `ForcedVertical`, `ForcedHorizontal`, `Aligned`, `Free` (the DevKit says `Free` is not usable for `OpeningDefault`);
- `limitType`: `Infinite`, `Finite`, `HalfInfinite`;
- `linkedStatus`: `Linked`, `NotLinked` (the getter returns `std::optional`, so leave it out when it is empty);
- `shapeType`: `Rectangular`, `Circular`, `Polygonal`;
- `dividedOpeningMode`: `Disconnected`, `Connected`;
- `floorPlanDisplayMode`: `Symbolic`, `SymbolicCut`, `SymbolicOverhead`, `Projected`;
- `openEdgeStyle`: `Hide`, `ShowUncut`, `ShowOverhead`.

These are in `ACAPI/Element/Opening/OpeningExtrusionParameters.hpp` and `OpeningFloorPlanParameters.hpp`, in namespace `ACAPI::Element`.

- `ACAPI::Element::ModifiableOpeningExtrusionParameters::SetConstraint` (AC29–30): `Result<void> SetConstraint (const Constraint constraint)`
- `ACAPI::Element::ModifiableOpeningExtrusionParameters::SetLimitType` (AC29–30): `void SetLimitType (const LimitType limitType)`
- `ACAPI::Element::ModifiableOpeningExtrusionParameters::SetLinkedStatus` (AC29–30): `Result<void> SetLinkedStatus (const LinkedStatus linkedStatus)`
- `ACAPI::Element::ModifiableOpeningExtrusionParameters::SetShapeType` (AC29–30): `void SetShapeType (const ShapeType polygonType)`
- `ACAPI::Element::ModifiableOpeningFloorPlanParameters::SetDividedOpeningMode` (AC29–30): `void SetDividedOpeningMode (DividedOpeningMode value)`
- `ACAPI::Element::ModifiableOpeningFloorPlanParameters::SetFloorPlanDisplayMode` (AC29–30): `void SetFloorPlanDisplayMode (OpeningFloorPlanDisplayMode value)`
- `ACAPI::Element::ModifiableOpeningFloorPlanParameters::SetOpenEdgeStyle` (AC29–30): `void SetOpenEdgeStyle (OpeningOpenEdgeStyle value)`
- `ACAPI::Element::OpeningExtrusionParameters::GetConstraint` (AC29–30): `Constraint GetConstraint () const`
- `ACAPI::Element::OpeningExtrusionParameters::GetLimitType` (AC29–30): `LimitType GetLimitType () const`
- `ACAPI::Element::OpeningExtrusionParameters::GetLinkedStatus` (AC29–30): `std::optional<LinkedStatus> GetLinkedStatus () const`
- `ACAPI::Element::OpeningExtrusionParameters::GetShapeType` (AC29–30): `ShapeType GetShapeType () const`
- `ACAPI::Element::OpeningFloorPlanParameters::GetDividedOpeningMode` (AC29–30): `DividedOpeningMode GetDividedOpeningMode () const`

## 2. Opening symbol parameters and the Opening tool defaults

  - read with `GetVarNumber`, `GetVarNameRef`, `GetVarType`, then `GetBoolVar` / `GetIntVar` / `GetNumVar` / `GetUStrVar`;
  - write by name with `GetIndexOfName` and `ModifyBoolVar` / `ModifyIntVar` / `ModifyNumVar` / `ModifyUStrVar`;

It uses the current Opening tool default (`CreateOpeningDefault ()`), or one set up as in `SetOpeningDefault` when the input gives settings. The DevKit says `Place` opens its own undoable command scope and closes it afterwards, so do **not** call it inside `ACAPI_CallUndoableCommand`. title: Leave sub-element objects out of GetAllElements, as GetElementsByType does
body:
## Problem

`GetAllElements` also returns the objects that belong to another element: zone stamps and the parts of stairs and railings. `GetElementsByType` has left these out since the `IncludeSubElemObjects` filter was added (1ce6d1d3).

The built-in scripts that look at "all elements" therefore saw them as elements of their own. On a small office model, Project Health Check listed every stair part under *Elements without an Element ID* and *Unclassified elements*. On TestProject.pla, 141 of the 272 elements `GetAllElements` returns are such objects.

## Change

- **Add-on:** `GetAllElements` and `GetElementsInDrawOrder` follow the same rule as `GetElementsByType`. Sub-element objects are returned only when the `IncludeSubElemObjects` filter is given. One helper, `IsSubElemObject`, is used by both listing paths. The three command descriptions say so.
- **builtin-scripts:** `utilities.archicad.get_elements` drops sub-element objects itself, so the scripts behave the same with released Add-Ons (1.7.2 and older).
- **New check:** `archicad-addon/Test/checks/get_all_elements_skips_subelement_objects.json` creates a zone on story 1 and verifies that:
  - `GetAllElements` returns the zone without its stamp;
  - with `IncludeSubElemObjects` it returns both;
  - `GetElementsByType` Object behaves the same way.

  The check first deletes the template's elevation markers, because they are listed on every story.
- **Expected outputs re-recorded** for the four examples that list all elements: `filter_elements`, `get_and_set_details_of_elements`, `get_connected_elements` and `save_as_module_file`. Each was compared with a run that adds `IncludeSubElemObjects` to every `GetAllElements` call (the old behaviour). Their differences come from this change only, except that `get_and_set_details_of_elements` also picks up the wall detail fields added on `main` since it was last recorded.

## Behaviour change

Scripts and the Grasshopper *Get All Elements* component now get fewer elements: only the ones the user placed. To get the old list, pass `"filters": ["IncludeSubElemObjects"]`.

## Tested

On Archicad 29 with a local RelWithDebInfo build:
- the new check passes, 6/6 (`tapir_test_runner.py check ... --brief`);
- the 8 examples whose stored outputs use `GetAllElements` were run against TestProject.pla. After re-recording, the four above match. `get_classifications_of_mainelements_and_subelements`, `get_design_options` and `highlight_elements` pass unchanged. `test_ifc_commands` differs only in IFC property fields that are out of date on `main` and unrelated to this change.

title: CreateHatches: buildingMaterialId is lost and the tool default fill is used
body:
Archicad 29 AUT build 3200, Tapir 1.7.2, Windows. Reproduced in a disposable copy, using native API.ExecuteAddOnCommand (TapirCommand), without a geometry wrapper.

In an active worksheet, create a hatch with a valid building material and no fill/pens overrides:
```json
{"hatchesData":[{"coordinates":[{"x":0,"y":0},{"x":1,"y":0},{"x":1,"y":1},{"x":0,"y":1}],"buildingMaterialId":{"guid":"56403B22-CF68-924A-B1FF-F47DE89A6AEB"},"layerIndex":1}]}
```
CreateHatches succeeds and returns an elementId. GetDetailsOfElements on it returns:
```json
{"fillPenIndex":179,"fillBackgroundPenIndex":0,"fillId":{"guid":"E1913637-3D9D-D740-BF63-7791B52C344A"},"buildingMaterialId":{"guid":"00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"}}
```
Expected: the explicitly supplied building material is retained and used. Actual: it reads back as the null GUID, with the default fill/pens. The input GUID is the project building material Erdreich (cut fill 42, pens 35/55).

The current main schema accepts buildingMaterialId. CreateHatchesCommand::SetTypeSpecificParameters assigns hatch.buildingMaterial but does not switch the hatch into a building-material mode; please check whether a hatch flag/type also needs setting. This is a source observation, not a tested fix.

Workaround: read the material cut fill/pens and create an ordinary fill; this loses the material association. Test hatch deleted.

title: MoveElements: silent success for a worksheet element when another database is active
body:
Archicad 29 AUT build 3200, Tapir 1.7.2, Windows. Native TapirCommand requests, reproduced in a disposable project copy.

1. ChangeWindow to worksheet A. CreateTexts at (0,0,0), layerIndex 1 (Archicad layer), text "CODEX ROUND9 TEMP".
2. ChangeWindow to a different worksheet B.
3. Move the text from A:
```json
{"elementsWithMoveVectors":[{"elementId":{"guid":"E46A0988-B8B0-4B2B-9FD4-E6E49A6A841B"},"moveVector":{"x":1,"y":0,"z":0}}]}
```
Response:
```json
{"executionResults":[{"success":true}]}
```
GetDetailsOfElements still reports position {"x":0,"y":0}.
4. ChangeWindow back to A and send the identical MoveElements request. It again returns success, and the position now reads {"x":1,"y":0}.

Expected: either move the referenced element or return a clear active-database error. Actual: success without a change when its worksheet is inactive. The layer is visible and unlocked; the same element and vector work as soon as its owning worksheet is active.

Related control: DeleteElements while B was active returned success:false, error -2130313215 "Failed to delete the element." Deleting in A succeeded. This report concerns the misleading MoveElements success; it is distinct from the hidden-layer case #555 / #861. Main still calls MoveElement after the editability check without an owning-database check.

Workaround: activate the owning worksheet before edits. Test text deleted.

title: SetDetailsOfElements: drawingScale reports success but remains unchanged on a Drawing
body:
Archicad 29 AUT build 3200, Tapir 1.7.2, Windows. Native TapirCommand requests in a disposable project copy.

Create a temporary Drawing from a worksheet view, activate its master layout and read its details: drawingScale=1, ratio=1. Send SetDetailsOfElements:
```json
{"elementsWithDetails":[{"elementId":{"guid":"F7E2765E-1905-44F9-A617-AD3A8CA15C5E"},"details":{"typeSpecificDetails":{"drawingScale":0.01,"ratio":0.5,"customName":"CODEX ROUND9 RENAMED"}}}]}
```
Response:
```json
{"executionResults":[{"success":true}]}
```
GetDetailsOfElements afterwards: drawingScale=1, ratio=0.5, customName="CODEX ROUND9 RENAMED".

The ratio and name changes work. The nominal drawingScale write is silently ignored. Expected: apply a documented writable setting, or reject/explain an unsupported or derived field. Main DrawingSettings still calls this modifiable and the C++ sets its change mask. If Archicad derives it from the source instead, please document that and avoid a misleading success.

This concerns drawingScale, not ratio (which works), and is separate from #817/#828, the include-scale-in-autotext flag. Temporary Drawing deleted.

title: SetDetailsOfElements: Drawing clipPolygon uses layout coordinates despite the model-coordinate description
body:
Archicad 29 AUT build 3200, Tapir 1.7.2, Windows. Native TapirCommand requests in a disposable project copy.

CreateDrawings from a worksheet view, position {"x":1,"y":1}. Readback: pos={"x":0.572,"y":0.485}, modelOffset={"x":0,"y":0}, bounds={"xMin":1,"yMin":1,"xMax":1.06,"yMax":1.12}.

Set a smaller clip on the active master layout:
```json
{"elementsWithDetails":[{"elementId":{"guid":"F7E2765E-1905-44F9-A617-AD3A8CA15C5E"},"details":{"typeSpecificDetails":{"clipPolygon":[{"x":1,"y":1},{"x":1.03,"y":1},{"x":1.03,"y":1.06},{"x":1,"y":1.06}]}}}]}
```
Response: {"executionResults":[{"success":true}]}. Readback returns the same polygon (plus closing point), and bounds now equals {"xMin":1,"yMin":1,"xMax":1.03,"yMax":1.06}. These are coordinates on the layout, including placement, rather than local source-model coordinates.

Main DrawingSettings and DrawingDetails both describe clipPolygon as "in model coordinates"; ElementCommands.cpp copies these coordinates directly into the Drawing memo. Please clarify the coordinate convention in the schema/docs, including its relationship to pos, ratio and modelOffset, or convert the input if model coordinates are intended.

Separate old suspicion checked and dropped: UpdateDrawings with the two temporary drawings returned {"success":true}; the single aggregate result matches its schema. Both temporary drawings deleted.

title: RenameNavigatorItem: renaming a Layout Book Drawing leaves its customName unchanged
body:
Archicad 29 AUT build 3200, Tapir 1.7.2, Windows. Native TapirCommand requests in a disposable project copy.

Create a temporary Drawing on a normal layout with name "CODEX ROUND9 LAYOUT" (nameType CustomName). Find its DrawingItem in GetNavigatorItemTree(LayoutBook), activate that layout and call:
```json
{"navigatorItemId":{"guid":"721E287A-DABC-4F94-AFFD-ED3152B8956C"},"newName":"CODEX ROUND9 NAV RENAMED"}
```
RenameNavigatorItem returns {"success":true}. The LayoutBook tree then reports the new name. GetDetailsOfElements on the Drawing still returns:
```json
{"nameType":"CustomName","customName":"CODEX ROUND9 LAYOUT"}
```
UpdateDrawings returns success, but does not synchronize the names.

Expected: the navigator and Drawing name stay consistent, or the command clearly reports that it only renames the navigator entry. Actual: success leaves two different names for the same placed Drawing. This test confirms the underlying customName mismatch; it does not separately verify title-block autotext rendering.

Workaround: set the Drawing customName through SetDetailsOfElements. Test Drawing deleted.
author: thespatialist

title: GetDetailsOfElements: Drawing navigatorItemId does not resolve to the source view
body:

CreateDrawings from the known View Map source 4FCD0CED-00D4-4F2D-A639-0983086B6701. GetDetailsOfElements on the new master-layout Drawing returns navigatorItemId 0308A1E0-232F-4357-AA26-652126277B4A; a second Drawing of the same source returns 237235D4-4532-4075-9207-469341E7F93F. Neither equals the source view.

For the first returned id:
```json
{"navigatorItemIds":[{"navigatorItemId":{"guid":"0308A1E0-232F-4357-AA26-652126277B4A"}}]}
```
GetViewSettings returns:
```json
{"viewSettings":[{"error":{"code":-2130313112,"message":"Failed to get view settings from the navigator item, probably it's not a view"}}]}
```
Calling it on the original source View Map id succeeds. The LayoutBook tree has yet another id for the placed Drawing item, so the returned id is not simply that DrawingItem id either.

Main DrawingDetails documents navigatorItemId as the view/layout the Drawing was created from, while ElementCommands.cpp exposes elem.drawing.drawingGuid directly. Expected: a usable source-view navigator id (possibly in a separate clearly named field), or documentation identifying what this id actually represents.

Related #641/#454 introduced the field; this report is a live semantic/readback problem after creation, not a request to expose a missing field. #836/#837 cover Drawing Manager data; this specifically concerns the advertised source-view id. Temporary drawings deleted.

title: Get3DGeometryOfElements: a 3D Document active window returns Failed to get the 3D model
body:

Use one existing Wall, unchanged throughout, elementId 89BEC9B9-E51D-45B2-8EC4-579C9C97CB84. Call Get3DGeometryOfElements:

title: MEP: the 237 functions left out of #1456 (preference table rows by key, AC27 tables, tool defaults, routing parameters, ports), with the DevKit declarations
body:
This continues #1456, whose six parts are open as #1457–#1462 and which hit the six-part limit. Below are the 237 MEP functions none of those parts uses. Each comes with its declaration (from the AC27–AC30 DevKits the build checks use: 27.3001, 28.3001, 29.3000, 30.3000) and the design decisions, which I've made as the requester. Everything is in namespace `ACAPI::MEP`, in `Support/Modules/MEPAPI/ACAPI/MEP<Class>.hpp` (for example `MEPPipeBranchPreferenceTable.hpp`). `MEPCommands.cpp` on `main` shows the includes and the `#ifdef ServerMainVers_2800` gating to follow.

**Building now, without waiting for #1457–#1462 to merge.** These parts must not wait for #1456's pull requests and must not be built on their branches: a part can only build on earlier parts of its own issue. So:
- Each part puts its commands in a **new source file** (named per part below) instead of `MEPCommands.cpp`. All six of #1456's parts edit that file heavily, so this part then only overlaps them in the `AddOnMain.cpp` registration, which the steward merges.
- Where a part needs a helper that exists only on one of #1456's branches (the table-type lookup from #1459/#1460, the JSON of a tool default from #1461), copy that code into the new file. #1459 did the same with #1293's changes. Keep it `static` with a different name, so the copies don't collide once both are merged.
- Never change a command that #1457–#1462 add.
- Register the new commands in a new `CommandGroup` "MEP Commands (extended)" block right after the existing MEP block in `AddOnMain.cpp`, with the version `main` carries.
- Ids as `{guid}` (`UniqueID` from GUID as on `main`), enums by enumerator name, lengths in metres, one execution result per item, writes in one undo step per call.


## 1. Preference table rows by key: branch and elbow tables

New file `MEPPreferenceTableRowCommands.cpp/.hpp` (see "Building now" above), AC28+:
- `GetMEPPreferenceTableRows {tableId, keys: [key]}`: for each key, `{key, valid, values}`. `valid` comes from `IsRowValid…`. `values` holds the table type's fields by name (`mainAxisDiameter`, `branchAxisDiameter`, `length`, `branchOffset`, `connectionLength`, `description` for branches; the elbow fields for elbows), each from its `Get…By…` getter.
- `SetMEPPreferenceTableRows {tableId, rows: [{key, values}]}`: partial. Only the given fields are set, each with its `Set…By…` setter, inside the table's `Modify`. Each row gets its own result.
- `AddMEPPreferenceTableRows {tableId, rows: [{key, values?}]}`: `AddNewRow (key)`, then the given values. Returns the new row index.
- `DeleteMEPPreferenceTableRows {tableId, keys}`: `DeleteRowBy…`.
- **The key:** AC29+ uses the table's `Key` struct (below) with the `…ByKey` functions. AC28 takes the same JSON key and calls the `…ByReferenceIds` functions with its reference ids; it rejects an angle it can't use, with a clear error. Find the table type from `tableId` the same way `GetMEPPreferenceTables` does on #1459's branch: copy that lookup into the new file rather than depending on it.
- Branch tables (pipe and duct) and elbow tables (pipe and duct) in this part.

The `Key` structs (AC29/AC30, `ACAPI/MEP<Table>.hpp`):
```cpp
// DuctBranchPreferenceTable
struct Key { uint32_t mainAxisReferenceId; double branchAxisAngle; uint32_t branchAxisReferenceId; };
// DuctElbowPreferenceTable
struct Key { uint32_t referenceId; double angle; };
// DuctTransitionPreferenceTable
struct Key { uint32_t beginReferenceId; uint32_t endReferenceId; };
// PipeBranchPreferenceTable
struct Key { uint32_t mainAxisReferenceId; double branchAxisAngle; uint32_t branchAxisReferenceId; };
// PipeElbowPreferenceTable
struct Key { uint32_t referenceId; double angle; };
// PipeTransitionPreferenceTable
struct Key { uint32_t beginReferenceId; uint32_t endReferenceId; };
```
