title: Commands that miss a patch release keep the previous version (44 commands of 1.7.3 registered as 1.7.2)
body:
44 of the 112 commands that `AddOnMain.cpp` registers for the first time in release **1.7.3** carry the version **1.7.2** in their `RegisterCommand<…>(group, "1.7.2", …)` call — for example `Change3DStyles`, `Create3DStyles`, `CreateAttributeFolders`, `DeleteAttributeFolders`, `Get3DCutPlanes`, `Get3DStyleDetails`, `GetCategoryValuesOfElements`, `GetContainingDatabases`. Release 1.7.2 does not have them (compared by tag: the 1.7.2 source does not register them, the 1.7.3 source does). The command reference shows the same version, so it says these commands exist since 1.7.2.

**Why it happens:** a command gets the version `main` carries when its pull request is written (as the README says to do). Since the weekly releases, many pull requests stay open across a release: written while `main` carried 1.7.2, merged after 1.7.2 was tagged, released in 1.7.3. For minor and major releases the release workflow already rewrites the commands registered with the skipped version; for a patch release nothing rewrites the ones that missed the previous release.

**Effect:** a script or agent that checks the version before calling a command (for example "available since 1.7.2", and the add-on reports 1.7.2) calls a command that is not there and gets `4010`. Documentation generated from the registrations shows the wrong release.

**Possible fixes** (either would do):
- In the weekly release, before tagging version X: every command registered with a version lower than X that the previous release tag does not register gets X. That is the same rewrite the workflow already does for minor/major releases, extended to commands that missed the previous release.
- Or at merge time: the build check (or the steward when it merges `main` into a bot branch) flags or updates a newly registered command whose version is lower than `tools/package_info.json`.

Found while regenerating a command catalog from the release tags; it now takes the first tag that registers a command as its version instead of the registered string.

title: GetElementsInDrawOrder crashes Archicad (AC26 and AC28), even without parameters
body:
`GetElementsInDrawOrder` (new in 1.7.3, #1167) crashes Archicad on its simplest calls. Tapir 1.7.3 (release), Archicad 26 (GER, 7004) and Archicad 28 (GER, 7006), Windows 11, untitled projects from the stock templates, floor plan active.

| Parameters | AC26 | AC28 |
|---|---|---|
| `{}` | crash | crash |
| `{"elementType": "Wall"}` | crash | crash |

The project held two walls and a slab created through Tapir. The HTTP connection is reset and Archicad is gone (crash reporter opens, project recovery on the next start). Reproduced in two separate runs on each version, each in a freshly started Archicad.

The open #1161 (`GetElementsInCreationOrder`, `ACAPI_DrawOrder_CreationOrderGetNext`) probably shares the walking code and is worth checking for the same problem.

title: MoveGraphicOverrideRules crashes Archicad 28 when the rule id is an element guid
body:
`MoveGraphicOverrideRules` (new in 1.7.3, #1441) crashes Archicad 28 when `graphicOverrideRuleId` is the guid of an element instead of a rule. Tapir 1.7.3 (release), Archicad 26 (GER, 7004) and Archicad 28 (GER, 7006), Windows 11, untitled projects from the stock templates, floor plan active. (AC26 answers "requires Archicad 27 or newer", correctly.)

```json
{"graphicOverrideRules": [{"graphicOverrideRuleId": {"guid": "<guid of a wall in the project>"}, "ruleGroupName": "zz test"}]}
```

Archicad 28 crashes (connection reset, crash reporter, project recovery on the next start). Reproduced twice in freshly started Archicads.

A guid that does not exist at all is handled correctly: `{"guid": "00000000-0000-0000-0000-00000000BEEF"}` returns a per-rule error and Archicad keeps running. So the crash seems to come from a guid that exists but is not a graphic override rule.

Expected: the same per-rule error as for an unknown guid.
author: weltmaister

title: GetElementAtCoordinate: no hit is an error instead of found:false, and AC28 misses a slab at the default z
body:
`GetElementAtCoordinate` (new in 1.7.3) has two problems. Tapir 1.7.3 (release), Archicad 26 (GER, 7004) and Archicad 28 (GER, 7006), Windows 11, untitled projects from the stock templates, floor plan active.

**1. Nothing found is reported as an error.** Searching where there is no element returns `{"error": {"code": -2130313112, "message": "Failed to search for an element at the coordinate."}}` on both versions, although the output schema has `found`. A caller cannot tell "no element here" from a real failure. Expected: `{"found": false}`.

**2. Archicad 28 misses a slab at the default `z`.** A slab created with `{"level": 0, "thickness": 0.2, "polygonCoordinates": [(1000,1000), (1005,1000), (1005,1004), (1000,1004)]}`, searched with `{"elementType": "Slab", "coordinate": {"x": 1002, "y": 1002}}`:

| | AC26 | AC28 |
|---|---|---|
| `z` omitted (0) | `found: true` | error above |
| `"z": 0.1` | — | `found: true` |

The slab's top is at 0. Reproduced twice on AC28 in freshly started Archicads. Perhaps AC28 needs the point strictly inside the slab's height range, or a tolerance; either way the default `z` should find a slab whose top is at the story level, as on AC26.
author: weltmaister

title: MeasureTexts: fontIndex/fontName are optional in the schema but one of them is required
body:
`MeasureTexts` (new in 1.7.3, #1129): the schema marks both `fontIndex` and `fontName` as optional, but a text without either is refused. Tapir 1.7.3 (release), Archicad 26 (GER, 7004) and Archicad 28 (GER, 7006), Windows 11, untitled projects from the stock templates, floor plan active.

```json
{"texts": [{"text": "Hello", "height": 2.5}]}
```
→ `{"measurements": [{"error": {"code": -2130313112, "message": "Each text requires 'fontName' or 'fontIndex'."}}]}` on both versions (reproduced twice). With `"fontIndex": 1` it measures correctly (15.9 mm on paper, 1.59 m with `inModelUnits` at 1:100).

A caller that builds the call from the schema, as an MCP client or a generated wrapper does, gets an error for a schema-valid call. Either the schema should require one of them (`anyOf: [{required: [fontIndex]}, {required: [fontName]}]`), or the command should fall back to a default font (the text tool's default, for example).

Side note: `fontName` is matched against Archicad's font list, not Windows font names (`"Arial"` gives "No loaded font is named 'Arial'"). The description could point to `GetFontsByName`.
author: weltmaister

title: SolveStairBaseline crashes Archicad 29 with one straight stair, including an input accepted by CreateStairs
body:
Tested on 2026-10-26 with released Tapir 1.7.3, Archicad 29 AUT build 3200, Windows, in a disposable PLN. Related command introduction: #1210 / #1214. This is a runtime crash report, not a request for the command. I have not established whether it is a regression.

## Single input already accepted by CreateStairs
The project has story index 2 at elevation 6.4 m. This input successfully created a temporary straight Stair (with id T173-Treppe-01 added only for CreateStairs):
```json
{"stairsData":[{"baseLinePoints":[{"x":110,"y":0},{"x":114.2,"y":0}],"zCoordinate":6.4,"floorIndex":2,"totalHeight":2.8,"flightWidth":1.2,"stepNum":16,"riserHeight":0.175,"treadDepth":0.28}]}
```
The created stair had a 3D box approximately x=110..114.2, y=0..1.2, z=6.4..9.2. All temporary elements were removed, absence read back, and the PLN saved before the solver call.

Calling **SolveStairBaseline** with exactly the JSON above (one item, not a mixed batch) closed the HTTP connection without a JSON response. The test-project window disappeared and it was absent from subsequent live instance discovery; a separate MAIN instance stayed available.

## Separate too-short case
After reopening and saving the test PLN, this independent call also crashed it:
```json
{"stairsData":[{"baseLinePoints":[{"x":110,"y":5},{"x":111,"y":5}],"zCoordinate":6.4,"floorIndex":2,"totalHeight":2.8,"flightWidth":1.2,"stepNum":16,"riserHeight":0.175,"treadDepth":0.28}]}
```
Expected: a Correct/Solved/NotSolved result or a structured error; the Archicad process/window should survive either input.

No empty-object schema probes were used. Schemas were read offline, both risky calls followed separate saves, and no solver element was created. The single straight valid input shows that neither multiple stairs in one call nor only an impossible baseline is required. No crash stack/minidump is available. Exact logical inputs and post-disconnect instance observations were retained locally.

title: SetProjectNotes duplicates architect and draftsmen when only notes is provided
body:
Observed with released Tapir 1.7.3 on Archicad 29 AUT build 3200 / Windows, 2026-10-26, in a disposable project. Related feature: #1327. Regression status is unknown.

```json
{"notes":"T173-Test 2026-10-26"}
```

2. GetProjectNotes then returned:
```json
{"architect":"#Planer:in #Planer:in","draftsmen":"IS IS","notes":"T173-Test 2026-10-26"}
```

title: GetDetailsOfElements: Stair elevation is doubled, baseline is local, and treadDepth is inconsistent
body:
Live readback in released Tapir 1.7.3, Archicad 29 AUT 3200 / Windows (2026-10-26). Related reader feature #823/#826; this concerns the returned data, not a request for Stair support. Regression status unknown.

A fresh temporary stair was created successfully with:
```json
{"stairsData":[{"id":"T173-Treppe-01","baseLinePoints":[{"x":110,"y":0},{"x":114.2,"y":0}],"zCoordinate":6.4,"floorIndex":2,"totalHeight":2.8,"flightWidth":1.2,"stepNum":16,"riserHeight":0.175,"treadDepth":0.28}]}
```
Story 2 is at 6.4 m. GetDetailsOfElements for the returned GUID reported:
```json
{"type":"Stair","floorIndex":2,"id":"T173-Treppe-01","details":{"stepNum":16,"riserHeight":0.175,"treadDepth":0,"flightWidth":1.2,"totalHeight":2.8,"level":6.4,"zCoordinate":12.8,"finishVisible":true,"baseLinePoints":[{"x":0,"y":0},{"x":4.2,"y":0}]}}
```
But Get3DBoundingBoxes returned:
```json
{"xMin":110,"xMax":114.200004578,"yMin":0,"yMax":1.200000048,"zMin":6.399999619,"zMax":9.200000763}
```
Observations:
- zCoordinate is 12.8 although the actual stair base is 6.4; level also reads 6.4. Existing stairs on stories +6.4 and -3.05 similarly read zCoordinate=12.8 and -6.1 respectively.
- The returned baseline starts at (0,0), while the input/model is at (110,0). If local coordinates are intentional, a placement transform or explicit coordinate-space contract is needed for a round trip.
- Fresh readback treadDepth=0 for input 0.28. An existing straight stair read treadDepth=1 while two successive riser positions in its parent Get3DGeometryOfElements model are horizontally 0.2799999997 m apart. This reader discrepancy should be distinguished from the older CreateStairs input issue #425.

Expected: correct absolute elevation, unambiguous baseline coordinate space/placement, and a meaningful going value (or explicitly documented unsupported value). The temporary stair and all other test elements were removed and their absence verified after reopening the PLN.

title: GetOpeningDetails returns translated points instead of direction vectors for opening axes
body:
Observed in released Tapir 1.7.3, Archicad 29 AUT 3200 / Windows, 2026-10-26. Regression status unknown. Related API coverage #1463.

A simple disposable fixture makes the translation evident. Story index 2 is at 6.4 m.

1. Relevant wall item from the original two-wall CreateWalls call (unrelated second wall omitted):
```json
{"wallsData":[{"id":"T173-Wand-01","begCoordinate":{"x":100,"y":0},"endCoordinate":{"x":104,"y":0},"floorIndex":2,"zCoordinate":0,"height":2.8,"structureType":"Basic","thickness":0.2}]}
```
2. CreateOpenings in the returned wall (HOST_GUID is that returned GUID):
```json
{"openingsData":[{"ownerElementId":{"guid":"HOST_GUID"},"basePoint":{"x":102,"y":0.1,"z":7.4},"width":1,"height":1}]}
```
3. GetOpeningDetails with the created Opening GUID, in the normal elements array, returned this geometry:
```json
{"anchorPoint":{"x":102,"y":0,"z":8.4},"extrusionDirection":{"x":100,"y":1,"z":6.4},"xAxis":{"x":101,"y":0,"z":6.4},"yAxis":{"x":100,"y":0,"z":7.4},"polygon":[{"x":-0.5,"y":-0.5},{"x":0.5,"y":-0.5},{"x":0.5,"y":0.5},{"x":-0.5,"y":0.5}]}
```
The three vectors contain the host origin (100,0,6.4). Subtracting that origin gives extrusion=(0,1,0), xAxis=(1,0,0), yAxis=(0,0,1). As returned, they are not unit direction vectors. A translation appears to have been applied to vectors as though they were points; this is an inference from the output, not a source-code diagnosis.

Two additional existing Opening elements also showed translated axes, so this was not limited to this fresh fixture. The schema describes xAxis/yAxis as the opening plane axes and extrusionDirection as its direction.

Expected: transform directions with the linear part only (or document a different representation and provide enough data to use it). Anchor points should remain world-coordinate points. All temporary fixtures were removed and verified absent. HOST_GUID above is an explicit placeholder; no project file is attached.

body:

A temporary Basic Wall was created at (100,0)->(104,0), floorIndex=2 (story elevation 6.4), zCoordinate=6.4, bottomOffset=0, height=2.8, layerIndex=1, id=T173-Wand-01-R, referenceLineLocation=Outside, relativeTopStory=0, topOffset=0. Its original readback was recorded.

GetAllFavorites(elementType=Wall) found `IW 20cm Stahlbeton tragend`; GetFavoriteSettings confirmed elementType=Wall. ApplyFavoritesToElements was sent:
```json
{"favoritesToApply":[{"elementId":{"guid":"8CB5FE5F-6C2D-4517-B1A2-1F120F0CBB1F"},"favorite":"IW 20cm Stahlbeton tragend"}],"applySettings":true,"applyClassifications":false,"applyCategories":false,"applyProperties":false,"keepFields":["id","layerIndex","height","relativeTopStory","topOffset","referenceLineLocation"]}
```

title: Get3DBoundingBoxes returns inverted sentinel bounds (+/-1e35) for Stair treads
body:
Observed in released Tapir 1.7.3, Archicad 29 AUT 3200 / Windows, on 2026-10-26. Related parent-Stair bbox fix #563/#564, but this report concerns tread subelements rather than the parent Stair. Regression status unknown.

GetSubelementsOfHierarchicalElements on a real Stair returned these two entries in stairTreads:
```json
[{"elementId":{"guid":"06510AF3-F482-41D7-B612-04C5DF8DD949"}},{"elementId":{"guid":"0D4BE99C-EA44-431B-B73E-8576F07A6C05"}}]
```

Passing them to Get3DBoundingBoxes as normal elements returned, for EACH tread:

```json
{"boundingBox3D":{"xMin":1e35,"xMax":-1e35,"yMin":1e35,"yMax":-1e35,"zMin":6.4,"zMax":6.4}}
```

title: Built-in scripts using tkinter crash on macOS: Tcl version conflict (launcher leaks TCL_LIBRARY into script environment)
body:
## Built-in scripts using tkinter crash on macOS: Tcl version conflict (launcher leaks TCL_LIBRARY into script environment)

### Summary
Running the built-in script **AutomaticNumberingBasedOnPolyline** (and presumably any built-in script that opens a `ScriptWindow` via `utilities/ui.py`) fails immediately on macOS when `tk.Tk()` is created. The script's Python (uv-managed CPython 3.14.5, Tcl/Tk 9.0.3) picks up the Tcl library folder bundled inside `TapirInstaller.app` (Tcl 8.6.16), which causes a version conflict.

### Environment
- macOS: 26.5.2, Apple Silicon (aarch64)
- Archicad: 28 / 7006
- Tapir add-on: 1.7.3
- Script Python: uv-managed `cpython-3.14.5-macos-aarch64-none` (Tcl/Tk 9.0.3)
- Script environment: `~/.cache/uv/environments-v2/automaticnumberingbasedonpolyline-501d63ab864a25b3`

### Steps to reproduce
1. In Archicad, open the Tapir palette.
2. Run the built-in script **AutomaticNumberingBasedOnPolyline**.
3. The script fails before the window appears.

### Expected behavior
The script window opens.

### Actual behavior
`tk.Tk()` raises `_tkinter.TclError`:
File “.../builtin-scripts/utilities/ui.py”, line 72, in init
self.root = tk.Tk()
File “.../cpython-3.14.5-macos-aarch64-none/lib/python3.14/tkinter/init.py”, line 2484, in init
self.tk = _tkinter.create(screenName, baseName, className, interactive, wantobjects, useTk, sync, use)
_tkinter.TclError: Cannot find a usable init.tcl in the following directories:
/tools/deps/lib/tcl9.0 /Users/<user>/.cache/uv/environments-v2/automaticnumberingbasedonpolyline-501d63ab864a25b3/lib/tcl9.0 ...

/private/var/folders/.../T/TapirInstaller/1793026743_3155/TapirInstaller.app/Contents/Frameworks/_tcl_data/init.tcl: version conflict for package “Tcl”: have 9.0.3, need exactly 8.6.16
version conflict for package “Tcl”: have 9.0.3, need exactly 8.6.16
while executing
“package require -exact Tcl 8.6.16”


Full traceback attached below.

### Analysis
- The error message shows Tcl 9.0.3 loading `init.tcl` from `TapirInstaller.app/Contents/Frameworks/_tcl_data/`. That folder layout matches a PyInstaller-frozen app, which sets `TCL_LIBRARY` / `TK_LIBRARY` to its bundled Tcl/Tk 8.6 data at startup.
- These environment variables appear to be inherited by the child process that runs the script under the uv-managed Python. That Python's tkinter is built against Tcl 9.0.3, so it loads the wrong `init.tcl` and fails on `package require -exact Tcl 8.6.16`.
- A secondary issue: without `TCL_LIBRARY`, Tcl only searches paths relative to the uv *environment* (`~/.cache/uv/environments-v2/...`), not the base interpreter (`~/.local/share/uv/python/cpython-3.14.5-macos-aarch64-none/lib/tcl9.0`), so simply unsetting the variables may not be enough on its own.

### Suggested fix
1. When launching script subprocesses, remove `TCL_LIBRARY` and `TK_LIBRARY` (and any other PyInstaller-injected variables) from the child environment.
2. Optionally, make `utilities/ui.py` robust by pointing Tcl/Tk at the libraries matching the running interpreter before creating the root window.

### Proposed Workaround
Add this to `builtin-scripts/utilities/ui.py` after `import tkinter as tk`:

```python
import os
import sys

def _fix_tcl_tk_env():
    for var in ("TCL_LIBRARY", "TK_LIBRARY"):
        os.environ.pop(var, None)
    lib = os.path.join(sys.base_prefix, "lib")
    tcl_dir = os.path.join(lib, f"tcl{tk.TclVersion}")
    tk_dir = os.path.join(lib, f"tk{tk.TkVersion}")
    if os.path.isfile(os.path.join(tcl_dir, "init.tcl")):
        os.environ["TCL_LIBRARY"] = tcl_dir
    if os.path.isdir(tk_dir):
        os.environ["TK_LIBRARY"] = tk_dir

_fix_tcl_tk_env()
```

Note: the built-in scripts live in a temp folder (`/private/var/folders/.../T/Tapir/`), so local patches may be overwritten on update.

title: Proposal: let community Archicad test results gate the bot's auto-merge (commit status instead of comment)
body:
## Current state

The steward asks the issue's author to test each bot PR in Archicad, and the community test runner (`tools/community-test-runner/`) answers such requests with a comment whose first line is machine-readable (`tapir-test: AC28 GER PASS 17/17 build <sha> tapir <version>`). I run it on AC26 and AC28 for bot PRs.

These results are not used anywhere, though:

- `claude_auto_merge.yml` gates on the build checks, the `claude-review` status and open human threads. A failed Archicad test does not hold a bot PR back; only a person reading the comment can.
- Every result comment counts as a human comment, so `claude_pr_review.yml` starts a re-review. For a PASS it answers "Looks correct, nothing blocking" and changes nothing, but it costs a model run, which is scarce (#977). Today I tested ten bot PRs, and each PASS comment started a re-review. I have stopped posting PASS results for PRs that bring no checks of their own for that reason.

## Proposal

1. **Turn a result comment into a commit status.** A small workflow on `issue_comment` reads a comment whose first line matches `^tapir-test: AC(\d+)\S* \S+ (PASS|FAIL) \d+/\d+ build ([0-9a-f]{7,40})`. It acts only for authors listed in a repository variable (e.g. `ARCHICAD_TESTERS`), and only when the sha is the PR's current head. Then it sets the commit status `archicad-test/AC<v>` to success or failure on that head. Testers need no extra token, and the workflow runs no model and no PR code.
2. **Let auto-merge respect it.** A `failure` of any `archicad-test/*` status on the head blocks the bot's auto-merge, the same way `do-not-merge` does. A missing status does not block, so nothing changes for PRs nobody tested.
3. **Skip the re-review for result comments.** `claude_pr_review.yml` ignores comments whose first line starts with `tapir-test:`. The status from 1. carries the information, and the review already reruns on every new head.

A status is tied to a commit, so a new push (e.g. the steward merging `main`) leaves the old result behind by itself, and the test has to be repeated for the new head.

## What a result means

Without checks in the PR, the runner runs the general catalog (`archicad-addon/Test/checks/`). A PASS then means "the build loads and nothing known broke", not "the fix works". A FAIL that is not a known catalog gap is the useful signal, and that is what 2. makes count. For PASS results to say more, bot PRs could add a check file for their change. That could be a later step for the issue bot.

Happy to open a PR for 1.–3. if you agree with the approach. Since all three touch `.github/workflows/`, I'd rather ask first.

title: Jacamar HUD: SetToolMode, GoToView, common menu operations and GetFullActionIndex
body:
I want to build **Jacamar HUD** as a Tapir script. It's a keyboard-driven command palette for Archicad: you type a few letters, it fuzzy-matches against everything you can switch to (tools, views, layouts, layer combinations, common operations), and Enter runs the match. For that the script needs four things from the add-on, listed below. I checked each against the AC25–AC30 DevKits the build checks use, and against `main`. As the requester I've made the design decisions.

Two requests had to change to fit the DevKits:
- **There is no `APIEnv_SetToolModeID`.** The call is `APIEnv_SetToolBoxModeID` on AC25–26 and `ACAPI_Toolbox_SetToolBoxMode` on AC27+.
- **There is no `ACAPI_Menu_ExecuteMenuCommand`.** The API has no way to run an arbitrary Archicad menu command; `ACAPI_MenuItem_*` only handles an add-on's own menus. Section 3 instead exposes the common menu operations, each through the API call that does the same thing.

`ACAPI_View_GoToView` is already on `main`, inside `ChangeWindow {navigatorItemId}`. Section 2 adds a `GoToView` command that reuses that code.

**For every part:**
- Match the surrounding code and reuse the `CommandBase` helpers (`GetElementTypeNonLocalizedName` / `GetElementTypeFromNonLocalizedName` for type names, the navigator helpers `GetNavigatorItemTree` uses).
- Register each command in `AddOnMain.cpp` with the version `main` carries, add a Python example under `archicad-addon/Examples/`, and gate version-specific calls with `ServerMainVers_*`.
- These can be one PR, or one per section if that's easier to review.

## 1. `GetToolbox` and `SetToolMode`

- `GetToolbox {includeHidden?}`: from `ACAPI_Toolbox_GetToolBoxInfo (&info, includeHidden)`, returns `{tools: [{type, variationId?, name}], activeTool: {type, variationId?}}`.
  - `type` is the non-localized element type name (`Wall`, `Door`, …), as elsewhere in Tapir.
  - `variationId` is set only for library part tools (doors, windows, objects, lamps; `API_ElemVariationID`, a four-character code as text).
  - `name` is the localized tool name, from `ACAPI_Element_GetElemTypeName`.
  - Dispose `info.data` with `BMKillHandle` on every path.
- `SetToolMode {type, variationId?}`: `ACAPI_Toolbox_SetToolBoxMode`. `type: "Arrow"` (or an empty type) selects the Arrow tool, which the DevKit does for `API_ZombieElemID`. Return `APIERR_BADPARS` / `APIERR_BADID` as the error.
  - The DevKit remark matters for the HUD: the switch is posted as an event and happens only once Archicad processes its event queue, after the command returns. Say so in the description, so a script doesn't read the mode back right away and expect the new tool.
- **AC25–26:** `ACAPI_Environment (APIEnv_GetToolBoxInfoID, &info, &includeHidden)` and `ACAPI_Environment (APIEnv_SetToolBoxModeID, &item)`. On AC25 `API_ToolBoxItem` has `typeID` + `variationID`; on AC26+ it has `type` (`API_ElemType`). Map these in `MigrationHelper.hpp` as `main` maps other renames.
- The coverage checklist marks the whole `Toolbox` group not applicable ("user interface"). Once this merges, a maintainer should take `Toolbox` out of that list in `tools/api_coverage_rules.json` (the bot can't edit `tools/`).

```cpp
// AC27–AC30, ACAPI_Environment.h
GSErrCode ACAPI_Toolbox_GetToolBoxInfo (API_ToolBoxInfo* toolBoxInfo, bool enableHidden = false);
GSErrCode ACAPI_Toolbox_GetToolBoxMode (API_ToolBoxItem* toolBoxItem);
GSErrCode ACAPI_Toolbox_SetToolBoxMode (API_ToolBoxItem* toolBoxItem);
// AC25–AC26, APIdefs_Environment.h (through ACAPI_Environment)
APIEnv_GetToolBoxModeID = 'GTBX', // par1: API_ToolBoxItem* par2: ---
APIEnv_SetToolBoxModeID = 'STBX', // par1: API_ToolBoxItem* par2: ---
APIEnv_GetToolBoxInfoID = 'GTBI', // par1: API_ToolBoxInfo* par2: bool (enable hidden)

// AC25, APIdefs_Environment.h
typedef struct {
  API_ElemTypeID typeID; // element type
  API_ElemVariationID variationID; // type subcategory (0 for generic types)
  Int32 filler_1[2];
} API_ToolBoxItem;
// AC26–AC30, APIdefs_Environment.h
typedef struct {
  API_ElemType type; // element type
  Int32 filler_1[2];
} API_ToolBoxItem;
// AC25–AC30, APIdefs_Environment.h
typedef struct {
  Int32 nTools; // number of tools installed (internal, subtypes)
  API_ToolBoxItem** data;
  API_ToolBoxItem activeTool;
  Int32 filler_1[6];
} API_ToolBoxInfo;
```

From the DevKit comment of `ACAPI_Toolbox_SetToolBoxMode`:
> For those types which can have more toolbox modes (ID_Wind, ID_Door, ID_Symb, ID_Light), the variationID of the tool should also be supplied. For `API_ZombieElemID` or an invalid element type ID specification the arrow mode will be set. Note that the function does not switch the toolbox immediately, but posts an event into the application queue. The command will be executed only when the application events are processed.

## 2. `GoToView`

`GoToView {navigatorItemId}`: opens a View Map view with its saved settings (layer combination, scale, model view options, zoom), through `ACAPI_View_GoToView (viewGuidStr)`. Move the view branch of `ChangeWindow` (`ApplicationCommands.cpp`, the `navigatorItemId` case, including its check that the item is a view or viewpoint and not a folder) into one helper that both commands call, so they can't drift apart. `ChangeWindow` keeps its schema and behavior. AC25–26: `ACAPI_Automate (APIDo_GoToViewID, …)`, as `main` already does.

```cpp
// AC27–AC30, ACAPI_Automate.h
GSErrCode ACAPI_View_GoToView (const char* viewGuidStr);
// AC25–AC26, APIdefs_Automate.h
APIDo_GoToViewID = 'GOVW', // par1: const char* par2: ---
```

## 3. `RunMenuOperation`: the common menu operations

`RunMenuOperation {operation}` runs one operation from a fixed list. Each maps to the API call behind the menu command, reusing the code of the Tapir command that already does it:

| `operation` | Menu command | Call |
|---|---|---|
| `FitInWindow` | View > Zoom > Fit in Window | as `FitInWindow` |
| `ZoomIn` / `ZoomOut` | View > Zoom > Zoom In / Out | `ACAPI_View_Zoom` with the current box (`ACAPI_View_GetZoom`) scaled by 0.5 / 2 around its center |
| `PreviousZoom` | View > Zoom > Previous Zoom | as `ResetZoom` |
| `ZoomToSelection` | View > Zoom > Zoom to Selection | `ACAPI_View_ZoomToSelected` (AC25–26 `APIDo_ZoomToSelectedID`) |
| `Rebuild` | View > Refresh > Rebuild | as `RebuildView` (`ACAPI_View_Rebuild`) |
| `Redraw` | View > Refresh > Redraw | `ACAPI_View_Redraw` |
| `Save` | File > Save | as `SaveProject` |
| `DeselectAll` | deselect everything | `ACAPI_Selection_DeselectAll` (AC25–26 `ACAPI_Element_DeselectAll`) |
| `ArrowTool` | the Arrow tool | section 1's `SetToolMode` with `Arrow` |

- An unknown `operation` is an `APIERR_BADPARS` error that lists the valid names. The input schema has the names as an `enum`, so the HUD can read the list from the schema.
- Not included: Undo / Redo, because the API has no call for them, and other add-ons' menu items.

## 4. `GetFullActionIndex`: everything the HUD can switch to, in one flat array

`GetFullActionIndex {kinds?}` returns `{actions: [...]}`, one entry per action. `kinds` filters by kind, all by default. Each entry:

```json
{
  "id": "view:4F0E…",            // stable across calls: kind + guid, or kind + name for tools and operations
  "kind": "view",                // tool | view | layout | layerCombination | operation
  "name": "3D / All",            // what Archicad shows (localized)
  "path": "Views/Interior",      // the navigator folders above it, "" for tools, layer combinations and operations
  "command": "GoToView",         // the Tapir command that runs it
  "parameters": { "navigatorItemId": { "guid": "4F0E…" } }
}
```

`command` and `parameters` are exactly what to send to run the action, so the script can pass them on as they are.

| `kind` | Source | `command` / `parameters` |
|---|---|---|
| `tool` | section 1's toolbox list (hidden tools left out) | `SetToolMode {type, variationId?}` |
| `view` | every view in the View Map (`API_PublicViewMap`) as `GetNavigatorItemTree` walks it; folders only go into `path` | `GoToView {navigatorItemId}` |
| `layout` | every layout in the Layout Book (`API_LayoutMap`); master layouts left out | `ChangeWindow {navigatorItemId}` (on `main`) |
| `layerCombination` | the layer combination attributes, as `GetLayerCombinations` lists them | `ActivateLayerCombination {attributeId}` (#916) |
| `operation` | section 3's list | `RunMenuOperation {operation}` |

- **Order:** by kind in the order above, then as the navigator shows them (views and layouts) or alphabetically (the rest), so the result is stable between calls.
- **Speed:** it is read-only and called often, so read each source once per call and do no per-item `ACAPI_Navigator_GetNavigatorItem` round trips beyond what the tree walk needs. Tested on a project with a few hundred views it should return well under a second.
- **#916 dependency:** the layer combination entries point at `ActivateLayerCombination`, which #916 adds (`ACAPI_Navigator_ChangeCurrLayerComb`; AC25–26 `APIEnv_ChangeCurrLayerCombID`). Wait for #916 to merge before building this part; don't add a second activate command.

Not tested in Archicad: I'll test each part's build when the bot links it.

title: GetAttributesFromProject returns empty lists for Layer, BuildingMaterial and Surface
body:
Tested on 2026-10-27 with released Tapir 1.7.3, Archicad 29 AUT build 3200, Windows, from a disposable test project. Related: #1216 / #1221.

`GetAttributesFromProject` on a closed `.pln` returns an empty `attributes` array for **Layer**, **BuildingMaterial** and **Surface**. The other requested types from the same call are filled. Reproduced with two different source files (both earlier copies of the open project), so the source files do contain these attributes.

Input (source file not open in any Archicad):
```json
{"projectFilePath":"D:\\...\\WKL519_08.pln","attributeTypes":["Layer","LayerCombination","BuildingMaterial","Composite","Fill","Line","Surface","PenTable","ZoneCategory","Profile"]}
```
Result (5.5 s, no error items), compared with `GetAttributesByType` in the open project, which is a later copy of the same file:

| attributeType | GetAttributesFromProject (source .pln) | GetAttributesByType (open copy) |
|---|---|---|
| Layer | **0** | 192 |
| LayerCombination | 19 | 21 |
| BuildingMaterial | **0** | 90 |
| Composite | 49 | 49 |
| Fill | 214 | 216 |
| Line | 38 | 38 |
| Surface | **0** | 242 |
| PenTable | 12 | 13 |
| ZoneCategory | 18 | 18 |
| Profile | 29 | 30 |

The source's 49 Composites use building materials, and its 19 layer combinations refer to layers, so the empty lists can't be right. A second source file gives the same pattern: `["Layer","Fill","BuildingMaterial","Composite"]` → 0 / 214 / 0 / 49. A call with `["Layer"]` only also returns `[]`.

Expected: the layers, building materials and surfaces of the source file, or a per-type error if a type can't be read this way.

title: Label widthFactor / charSpaceFactor: ignored by CreateLabels, reset to 1 by a text-only ModifyLabels
body:
Tested on 2026-10-27 with released Tapir 1.7.3, Archicad 29 AUT build 3200, Windows, in a disposable project copy, on a visible and unlocked layer.

**1. CreateLabels ignores the factors.**
```json
{"labelsData":[{"labelClass":"Text","favoriteName":"Text/Autotext","text":"T173 Etikett","floorInd":0,"begCoordinate":{"x":400,"y":50},"midCoordinate":{"x":401,"y":51},"endCoordinate":{"x":403,"y":51},"style":{"widthFactor":1.2,"charSpaceFactor":1.1}}]}
```
The label is created, but GetDetailsOfElements reads `style.widthFactor` 1 and `style.charSpaceFactor` 1.

**2. A text-only ModifyLabels resets them.**

| step | call | widthFactor / charSpaceFactor read back |
|---|---|---|
| a | `ModifyLabels` with `style: {widthFactor: 1.2, charSpaceFactor: 1.1}` only → success | 1.2 / 1.1 |
| b | `ModifyLabels` with `text: "T173 Etikett neu"` only → success | **1 / 1** |

The schema says "Only provided fields are changed; omitted fields are left as-is". The text change rebuilds the content (as documented), but the factors aren't kept. In my run the leader-line coordinates stayed the same.

Expected: CreateLabels applies the given factors, and a text-only ModifyLabels keeps them. Workaround today: send `style` again in the same or a following ModifyLabels.

title: CreateLayout with position "last" at the Layout Book root creates the layout but returns only an error (no databaseId)
body:

Without `parentNavigatorItemId` (Layout Book root):

```json
{"layoutsData":[{"layoutName":"T173-C Root","masterNavigatorItemId":{"guid":"…"},"position":"last"}]}
```

title: Fix revision response schemas and element GUID extraction
body:
ChatGPT found the following while updating the MCP:

- `GetCurrentRevisionChangesOfLayouts`
- `GetRevisionChangesOfElements`

These findings come from schema and C++ source inspection; I have not reproduced them in a running Archicad instance.

### 1. Incorrect required-property name

`RevisionChangesArrayItem` declares `revisionChanges`, but requires `revisionChange`.

Because `additionalProperties` is false, the successful object cannot satisfy the schema: the required singular property is undeclared.

The required property should be `revisionChanges`.

[Schema definition](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/1.7.3/docs/archicad-addon/common_schema_definitions.js#L10002)

### 2. Response schemas declare an object where implementations return an array

Both command response schemas reference `RevisionChangesOfEntities`, which describes one success/error object. However, both implementations return a list containing one success/error object per requested layout or element.

For example, the element command builds:

{
  "revisionChangesOfElements": [
    {"revisionChanges": []}
  ]
}

The contract currently expects an object at `revisionChangesOfElements`, so generated typed clients reject this list-shaped response.

The response contract should describe an array whose items are either a revision-change wrapper or an error. Fixing the required-property spelling alone will not resolve this mismatch.

[Layout command](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/1.7.3/archicad-addon/Sources/RevisionCommands.cpp#L340) · [Element command](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/1.7.3/archicad-addon/Sources/RevisionCommands.cpp#L414)

### 3. Element revision lookup uses the database-ID extractor

`GetRevisionChangesOfElementsCommand::Execute` transforms its `elements` input using `GetGuidFromDatabaseArrayItem`.

Valid element items contain `elementId`, while that helper reads `databaseId`. The shared extractor returns `APINULLGuid` when the requested field is absent, so the command passes null GUIDs instead of the supplied element GUIDs.

This should use `GetGuidFromElementsArrayItem`. The layout command's use of the database extractor is appropriate.

[Element lookup](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/1.7.3/archicad-addon/Sources/RevisionCommands.cpp#L430) · [Extractor definitions](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/1.7.3/archicad-addon/Sources/CommandBase.hpp#L67) · [Missing-field handling](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/1.7.3/archicad-addon/Sources/CommandBase.cpp#L115)

Suggested verification: query multiple layouts/elements, check success and error entries, validate the returned arrays against the corrected schemas, and confirm that element lookups receive the supplied element GUIDs.

title: Zones: let us read and set the contour pen and line type
body:
Hi Tapir team 👋

We use Tapir to create zones in bulk (`CreateZones`), and one thing we keep running into: there's no way to control the zone's contour line, meaning the pen and line type of the boundary on the floor plan.

Right now `GetDetailsOfElements` gives us the name, number, category, stamp position, outline and holes for a zone (tested on Tapir 1.7.2 / Archicad 28), but nothing about how the contour is drawn. The only workaround we've found is `ApplyFavoritesToElements`, but that's a pretty big hammer. It also swaps the category and resets the stamp, when all we wanted was a different line.

What would really help:

- **Read it:** return the contour pen and line type in ZoneDetails.
- **Change it:** accept those fields in `SetDetailsOfElements` (or in the new `ModifyZones` from #896 / #899, which seems like a natural fit), leaving everything else untouched.
- **Set it on creation:** optional fields in `CreateZones`, so new zones come out right the first time.

If it's not much extra work, the zone's cover fill (fill type, foreground and background pen) would be a nice bonus in the same spot.

Thanks a lot for all the work on Tapir. It's become the backbone of our in-house Archicad tools!

title: CreateWalls/ModifyWalls: no way to set flipped, so a read wall cannot be rebuilt as it was
body:
## Summary

`GetDetailsOfElements` reports a wall's `flipped`, but no command writes it: `CreateWalls`, `ModifyWalls` and `SetDetailsOfElements` have no `flipped` input. A new wall takes `flipped` from the Wall tool default. For a complex-profile wall that mirrors the whole cross section across the reference line, so the caller cannot rebuild a profile wall it has just read.

## Repro (Archicad 30 build 3001 ITA, Tapir 1.7.3, Windows 11)

1. Take any straight complex-profile wall with `flipped: false` (here one created by the IFC import, profile 827 × 2690 mm).
2. Read it with `GetDetailsOfElements`, and its profile with `GetProfiles`.
3. Rebuild the profile with `CreateProfiles` (`newSkins` from the read `outlineCoords`), then create the wall with `CreateWalls`: the same `begCoordinate`, `endCoordinate`, `height`, `referenceLineLocation`, `offset`, plus `structureType: "Profile"` and the new `profileId`.
4. Compare the two with `Get3DBoundingBoxes`.

**Expected:** the same wall, `flipped: false`.
**Actual:** `flipped: true` (from the tool default). The bounding box is mirrored and off by the full profile width (827 mm).

Workaround: swap `begCoordinate` and `endCoordinate`. The geometry then matches (0.0 mm off), but `flipped` still reads `true`, so a read → write round trip does not reproduce the element.

## Request

Accept an optional `flipped` (boolean) in `CreateWalls` and `ModifyWalls`, and in the wall case of `SetDetailsOfElements` if that fits better. This is `API_WallType::flipped` with its mask bit; it applies to every wall type, not only complex-profile walls. Same spirit as #531: an explicit parameter should not be overridden by the tool default.

title: SetDetailsOfElements: "Failed to change element" for every element in a Worksheet (same call works on the Floor Plan)
body:
**Environment:** Archicad 29 (Windows), Tapir 1.7.3.

**Steps**
1. `CreateWorksheets` creates a new independent worksheet.
2. `ChangeWindow` with its `navigatorItemId`; `GetCurrentWindowType` returns `Worksheet`.
3. `CreateHatches` / `CreatePolylines` create elements in the worksheet (confirmed with `GetElementsByType` + `databases`).
4. `SetDetailsOfElements` on those elements, with any change:
   - hatch: `{"layerIndex": <index>}`
   - hatch: `typeSpecificDetails: {"fillPenIndex": 3}`
   - hatch: new `coordinates` + `holes`
   - polyline: `typeSpecificDetails: {"linePenIndex": 3}`

**Result:** every call returns `-2130312912 "Failed to change element"`. `DeleteElements` on the same elements, with the worksheet active, works.

**Expected:** the same behavior as on the Floor Plan, where the identical hatch call (`coordinates` + `holes`) succeeds and `GetDetailsOfElements` returns the hole.

**Impact:** `SetDetailsOfElements` is currently the only way to give a hatch holes, so hatches with holes cannot be created in worksheets or other 2D databases.

title: CreateHatches: accept "holes" (same format SetDetailsOfElements already accepts for hatches)
body:
`SetDetailsOfElements` already sets hatch holes (`holes: [{polygonOutline, polygonArcs}]`, PR #484), and `GetDetailsOfElements` returns them. `CreateHatches` still always creates a single contour (`nSubPolys = 1` in `CreateHatchesCommand::SetTypeSpecificParameters`).

Accepting the same optional `holes` array in each `hatchesData` item would make create and modify symmetric, and would avoid a second call per hatch when creating many hatches.
author: cmartif

title: 2D creation commands: optional databaseId to create elements in a given Worksheet/Detail without changing the active window
body:
**Problem**
2D creation commands always create elements in the current database, so creating content in a worksheet or detail requires activating its window first.

**Observed** (Archicad 29, Tapir 1.7.3)
- `CreateWorksheets` returns only a `databaseId`.
- `ChangeWindow` with `{"windowType": "Worksheet", "databaseId": <that id>}` fails with -2130313110 "Failed to change current database". This looks like the never-opened-window case fixed for elevations in #995.
- `ChangeWindow` with the `navigatorItemId` works, but obtaining that id requires reading the whole Project Map with `GetNavigatorItemTree`, which is very large on big projects.
- `GetElementsByType` with `"databases": [<same id>]` works, so the id itself is valid.

**Proposal**
1. An optional top-level `databaseId` on the 2D creation commands (CreatePolylines, CreateHatches, CreateTexts, CreateLineElements, CreateArcs, CreateCircles, CreateSplines, CreateLabels, CreateHotspots). The command would switch to that database, create, and switch back, as `ExecuteActionForEachDatabase` already does for commands that take `databases`.
2. `CreateWorksheets` and `CreateDetails` also returning each new `navigatorItemId` (as #1039 expected), so the new item can be opened or placed with CreateDrawings directly.

Related: #819 (copy 2D elements between databases).

title: CreateHotlinkNodes: allow XRef nodes from DWG/DXF files (if the API supports APIHotlink_XRef)
body:
**Problem**
DWG/DXF files cannot be attached as XRefs through Tapir. This would allow scripts to place external CAD drawings in a given position and rotation, for example georeferenced DWGs aligned with the Survey Point via `GetSurveyPointTransformation`.

**Current behavior**
`CreateHotlinkNodes` (#622) always sets `hotlinkNode.type = APIHotlink_Module`. `CreateHotlinkInstances` already uses the node's own type, and `GetHotlinks` already lists XRef nodes.

**Question / proposal**
Does `ACAPI_Hotlink_CreateHotlinkNode` accept `APIHotlink_XRef` with a DWG/DXF source? If yes, add an optional `"type": "Module" | "XRef"` to `CreateHotlinkNodes`. If the API does not allow it, please close this issue; knowing that is useful too.
author: cmartif

title: Feature request: dimensioning new section/elevation views programmatically (SectElem GUIDs, level dimensions)
body:
Dear Developer Team,
Environment: Archicad 29 (HUN, build 5101), Tapir 1.5.9, Windows Server (multi-user RDP). Commands sent through the Archicad JSON API (`API.ExecuteAddOnCommand`).
Use case
We use Archicad for formwork drawings (zsaluterv). Every load-bearing wall gets its own wall-elevation section (hundreds per project). We create the sections with `CreateSections` successfully, but we cannot dimension them automatically. Four gaps block the workflow:
1. Real SectElem GUIDs are not obtainable for a section view
`CreateAssociativeDimensionsOnSection` requires `sectionElementId`(s) — the GUID of the section element (SectElem) in the section database. In a newly created section:
`GetElementsByType` with `elementType: "SectElem"` (current section window, or with `databases` set to the section's database) returns the GUIDs of the parent model elements (walls, slabs, openings…), not the SectElem GUIDs.
`GetSelectedElements` after Ctrl+A in the section window also returns the parent model GUIDs.
Passing those GUIDs to `CreateAssociativeDimensionsOnSection` fails: "The referenced 'sectionElementId' is not a valid section element." (code −2130313112).
`CreateAssociativeDimensions` with the parent GUID and `nodeType` 130/430 (as seen in existing section dimensions) fails: "Failed to create associative dimension."
The real SectElem GUIDs only become visible indirectly: after a user places a dimension manually, `GetDimensionData` shows them as `witnessPoints\[].baseElementId`. With those GUIDs, `CreateAssociativeDimensionsOnSection` works perfectly (tested: `SlabCompositeFaces` preset on two slabs). `GetDetailsOfElements` also works on them (`type: "SectElem"`, with section-plane polygons).
The SectElem GUIDs are not derivable from the parent GUID (we compared two parent/SectElem pairs; no constant relation).
Request: one of the following:
make `GetElementsByType("SectElem")` return the real SectElem GUIDs (optionally with the parent element GUID), or
a command that maps parent element GUID + section database → SectElem GUID(s), or
let `CreateAssociativeDimensionsOnSection` accept a parent element GUID together with the section database.
2. Elevation-type (level) linear dimensions cannot be created
Our level dimensions in sections are linear dimensions in elevation mode (`Dimension` element; `GetDimensionData` returns the absolute elevation as `dimensionValue`, e.g. −0.80 / −0.50 / 3.66 / 3.88 …). We can create the linear dimension chains, but not in elevation mode:
`CreateAssociativeDimensions` always creates a normal linear dimension (values are segment lengths).
`CreateFavoritesFromElements` / `UpdateFavoritesFromElements` from an elevation-mode dimension succeeds, but `ApplyFavoritesToElements` on a linear dimension does not switch it to elevation mode.
`ApplyFavoritesToElementDefaults` with that favorite before `CreateAssociativeDimensions` does not help either: the new dimension is still linear (`dimensionValue` = segment length).
Request: a parameter on `CreateAssociativeDimensions` (and `CreateAssociativeDimensionsOnSection`) to create the dimension in elevation mode (or to respect the dimension tool defaults / a favorite name), and/or a `SetDetailsOfElements` field for the dimension type. A separate `CreateLevelDimensions` (the Level Dimension tool) would also be welcome.
3. "Explode into Current View" is not available
Our workaround for #1 is: explode the section into 2D (Edit → Reshape → Explode into Current View), move the 2D copy beside the view, and dimension the 2D hatches/polylines (this works well: `CreateAssociativeDimensions` binds to hatch/polyline vertices via `inIndex`/`nodeId`). The explode step itself still needs a manual menu click per section.
Request: a command to explode selected/all elements of the current (section) view into 2D drawing elements, optionally keeping the originals, returning the GUIDs of the new elements.
4. Geometry of existing sections / openings is not readable
`GetDetailsOfElements` on `CutPlane` (section markers on the plan): "Not yet supported element type"; `API.Get2DBoundingBoxes` on them: "Element not supported". We cannot read the start/end point, depth or direction of existing sections.
`GetDetailsOfElements` on `Opening` elements: "Not yet supported element type"; `API.Get3DBoundingBoxes` on them: Internal error (6000).
Request: details (geometry) for `CutPlane` (start/end, depth, direction/marker side, vertical range) and for `Opening` (position, size, host element).
Notes
`CreateSections`: the view direction is to the left of the start→end direction. It would help to document this, and to allow passing a favorite (section settings) at creation time.
Thank you for Tapir — it already covers most of our workflow (section creation, associative dimensions, favorites, layers, navigator).
thank you very mutch in advance, best regards,
Istvan
author: kipisti

title: GetAllProperties: optional filter to read the expressions of specific properties
body:
Since #321, `GetAllProperties` returns `isExpressionBased` and `expressions`, and `UpdatePropertyDefinitions` rewrites them in place (GUID kept, order preserved). Thanks — the read/modify/write cycle works (tested with 1.7.3 on Archicad 29).

The remaining problem is size. `GetAllProperties` takes no parameters, so reading the expressions of one property means downloading every built-in and custom property with its full availability list. In a large template a single 100-property page of the response can exceed 2 MB (#1292 measured ~600k tokens for a full dump), which is impractical for scripts and MCP clients.

Any of these would solve it:
1. Optional `propertyIds` parameter in `GetAllProperties`, returning only those definitions.
2. Optional `propertyType` (`UserDefined` / `BuiltIn`) and `includeAvailability: false`.
3. Or `isExpressionBased` + `expressions` in a details command that takes property GUIDs.

Related: #1145 / #1146 (`CheckPropertyExpressions`, `GetPropertyExpressionReferences`) would complete the workflow:
- validate each expression before `UpdatePropertyDefinitions`, which today returns a generic "inconsistent definition" error for the whole list without saying which expression failed;
- build `###Property:<GUID>###` references from a property id. Name-based references (`{Property:Group/Name}`, `###Property:Group/Name###`) are rejected on write.
author: cmartif

title: CreateFills: percent of Solid fills is ignored
body:
**Environment:** Archicad 29 (build 3200, German), macOS, Tapir 1.7.3

**What happens**

`CreateFills` with `subType: "Solid"` and a `percent` below 1 creates the fill with `percent` 1.0 (a full solid fill).
The same happens with `overwriteExisting: true` on an existing percentage fill: the percent is reset to 1.0.

`GetFills` reads the percent of existing percentage fills correctly (e.g. 0.05, 0.25, 0.95 for Archicad's
5 % … 95 % fills), so reading and writing are not symmetric: a fill copied with GetFills → CreateFills
loses its percentage.

**Expected**

The fill is created (or overwritten) with the given `percent`, as the schema describes
("Translucency percentage [0..1] (gradient and some Solid fills)").

**How to reproduce**

```python
fill = {"name": "Test 25 %", "subType": "Solid", "percent": 0.25}
CreateFills {"fillDataArray": [fill]}
GetFills {"attributeIds": [<new id>], "fields": ["subType", "percent"]}
# -> subType "Solid", percent 1.0   (expected 0.25)
```

Same result for 0.05 … 0.95, on create and on overwrite.

**Note**

`CreateFillsCommand` does read the value (`data.Get ("percent", fill.filltype.percent)`), so Archicad
probably overwrites or ignores `filltype.percent` on create/modify for this subtype. Maybe the percentage has
to be set in another field or in `API_AttributeDefExt` for Solid fills.
author: Kappa-lo

title: GetFills / CreateFills: symbol fills lose their offsets and solid parts (copies draw wrong)
body:
**Environment:** Archicad 29 (build 3200, German), macOS, Tapir 1.7.3

**What happens**

Symbol fills copied with `GetFills` → `CreateFills` (all fields, same file or another file) are created but draw wrong: the pattern is all black or broken. In our test all 17 symbol fills we copied came out wrong, although `GetFills` on the new fill returns the same data as on the original.

Also, two *different* symbol fills can return identical `GetFills` data, so the read data is not the full definition.

**Likely cause (from the source)**

`GetFills` / `CreateFills` leave out two parts of a symbol fill's definition:

1. **The symbol offsets `c1` / `c2`** (X1/Y1 and X2/Y2 in the Fill Types dialog, which say how the motif repeats). `GetFills` only returns `filltype.c1/c2` as `gradientStart` / `gradientEnd` for gradient fills, so for symbol fills they are never read. On create they stay (0,0) unless `gradientStart/End` are passed, so all copies of the motif sit on top of each other.
2. **The solid fill items of the motif** (`sfill_SolidFills`, `sfill_FillCoords`, `sfill_SubPolys`, `sfill_PolyArcs`, count in `filNumb`). The comment in `CreateFillsCommand` says they are not supported. Symbol fills with filled shapes lose them.

**Expected**

`GetFills` returns, and `CreateFills` accepts, the complete symbol fill definition: e.g. `symbolOffset1` / `symbolOffset2` (c1/c2) and `symbolSolidFills` (polygons with holes and arcs), so a symbol fill can be copied 1:1.

**How to reproduce**

1. In a project with a symbol fill (e.g. one of Archicad's insulation fills), read it with `GetFills` with all fields.
2. `CreateFills` with that data and a new name.
3. Draw a hatch with each fill: the copy looks different (black or broken pattern).
author: Kappa-lo

title: Import attributes from another project file (append / overwrite like the Attribute Manager) and export them to a file
body:
**Environment:** Archicad 29 (build 3200, German), macOS, Tapir 1.7.3

**Use case**

We maintain an office template and several project files that must share the same attributes (surfaces, fills, building materials, composites, line types, layers). Today the only scripted way to bring an attribute from one file into another is: read it (`GetAttributesFromProject` or `GetFills`/`GetSurfaces`/... in the source file) and recreate it with `Create*` in the target. That is slow and loses information:

- the attribute gets a new GUID, so files no longer match by GUID;
- some data cannot be recreated at all: symbol fills (#1614), percentage fills (#1613);
- references between attributes (a composite's building materials, a building material's fill and surface) have to be remapped by hand.

Archicad's own Attribute Manager does this in one step ("Append" / "Overwrite", matched by name or by index), and can save attributes to a file and load them from one.

**Request**

Follow-up to #1216 / #1221, where `load: true` was left for a maintainer decision:

1. **Import:** `ImportAttributesFromProject` (or `GetAttributesFromProject` with `load: true`) from a .pln / .tpl (and .aat if the API allows it):
   - `attributes`: by type + name, index or GUID (or "all of type")
   - `mode`: `append` (new only), `overwriteByName`, `overwriteByIndex`, like the Attribute Manager
   - dependent attributes brought along or mapped to existing ones by name, with a report of what was created, overwritten, mapped or skipped
   - a `dryRun` that returns that report without changing anything
2. **Export:** write selected attributes of the open project to a file (.aat, or a .pln/.tpl), so a curated set can be kept as one source file.
3. If `ACAPI_Attribute_GetAttributesFromProject` + `CreateExt` is the only route: keep the full `API_AttributeDefExt` from the source file, so symbol fills, percentages and the like come over complete, even if the GUID can't be kept.

Related: #1582 (`GetAttributesFromProject` returns empty lists for Layer, BuildingMaterial and Surface).

Happy to test on AC29 (macOS) with a template and a project file.
author: Kappa-lo

title: IFC import translators: list them and choose one for IFCFileOperation merge/open
body:
**Environment:** Archicad 29 (build 3200, German), macOS, Tapir 1.7.3

**Use case**

We merge consultants' IFC files into reference files every day by script (`IFCFileOperation` with `method: merge`). The result depends heavily on the import translator (geometry conversion: Morphs, Objects or MEP elements; layer and property mapping). Export translators can already be listed and chosen (`GetIFCExportTranslators`, `translatorName` on save — thanks!). For import there is nothing yet.

**What happens today**

- `IFCFileOperation merge` / `open` take no translator. The merge does not use the project's default import translator: it uses **the translator of the last manual merge in the current Archicad session**.
- `OpenProject` resets that. Even a project-default import translator set in the IFC Translators dialog did not help: after `OpenProject` the next scripted merge came in with different geometry (native MEP elements instead of Morphs).
- So a reliable scripted build must start with one manual merge of a tiny IFC and then never reopen the project.
- Also worth a note in the docs: without the dialog, the IFC's first storey is placed on the **active** storey of the floor plan. We call `ChangeWindow` to storey 0 before every merge.

**Request**

1. `GetIFCImportTranslators`: list the import translators of the project (name, which one is the default).
2. `translatorName` for `IFCFileOperation` with `method: merge` and `open` (like `save` already has).
3. If the API allows it: read (and ideally set) the main settings of a translator: geometry conversion per element type, layer mapping, property mapping file. Even read-only would let us check a file before merging.
4. Optional: a `targetStoryIndex` (or "keep IFC levels") for merge, so the result does not depend on the active storey.

Happy to test on AC29 (macOS).
author: Kappa-lo

title: Steward: push-merge fails at "Create the App token" (Invalid keyData), so conflict fixes are never pushed
body:
Since 05:39 UTC today, every steward run that merges `main` into a bot PR fails in the `push-merge` job at **Create the App token**:

```
Failed to create token for "tapir-archicad-automation" (attempt 1): Invalid keyData
DOMException [DataError]: Invalid keyData
    at importDerKey (node:internal/crypto/webcrypto_util:136:11)
```

Example: https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/actions/runs/40723856465 (Fix bot PR #1494, job `push-merge`).

`actions/create-github-app-token` cannot read the private key in `TAPIR_BOT_APP_PRIVATE_KEY`. The `app-id` input is there, so the secrets exist, but the key is not a usable PEM. Common causes are a truncated paste, lost line breaks, or a value that is not the `.pem` file GitHub generated for the App.

**Effect**
- Today 318 "Fix bot PR" runs ended in failure. Of the 171 fix runs between the merge of #1447 and today, `push-merge` ran 10 times and failed every time; I found none where it succeeded, so the key may never have worked.
- In each one the `fix` job runs the model and resolves the conflict, but nothing is pushed. The PR stays in conflict, and the bot still writes its "fixed" comment. #1293 and #1547 have had the same conflict "fixed" several times today with no new commit.
- The steward starts the next round an hour later, so each of these runs uses a model run from the usage limit (#977) and achieves nothing.

**Suggested fix** (needs a maintainer, the bot can't change secrets):
1. Generate a new private key in the App's settings and store the whole `.pem` file content, including the `-----BEGIN … KEY-----` and `-----END … KEY-----` lines, as `TAPIR_BOT_APP_PRIVATE_KEY`.
2. Until the key works, setting `BOT_PR_STEWARD=false` pauses the steward and stops the runs that have no effect.

A follow-up could be to write the "fixed" comment only after `push-merge` succeeded, so that a failed push shows up on the PR.
author: weltmaister

title: CreateStairs: allow landings on multi-segment baselines (per-edge segment type, per-vertex turn type, landing edge offset)
body:
Environment: Archicad 29 JPN, Tapir 1.7.3, Windows 11.

Since #445, multi-segment (L/U) baselines work in CreateStairs. But we found no way to say that a turn should be a **landing**. When we create a U-shaped stair from a 4-point baseline, the solver turns the middle turn into winders. The textbook we follow (and most real two-flight stairs) needs a landing there, so today we create these stairs by hand.

Request: let CreateStairs (and later ModifyStairs, #824) take:
- per baseline edge: `segmentType` (flight / landing, i.e. `APIST_LandingSegment`)
- per baseline vertex: `turnType` (e.g. `APIST_LandingTurn`)
- the landing edge offsets (`currLandingStartEdgeOffset` and related fields in `API_StairPolylineEdgeData`), so the landing depth can be set

Our case: width 1150, riser 153.8, tread 240, baseline on the left. Baseline (mm): (2520,24250) → (5400,24250) → (5400,24490) → (2520,24490). The middle turn should be a landing with its edge offset by 50, giving a landing depth of 1350.

The tread depth side of the same case (we asked for 240 and got 292) is already tracked in #425 / #750, so this issue is only about landings. As noted in #425, the landing position is what decides whether a two-flight stair fits its stairwell.

Related: #425, #444/#445 (multi-segment baselines), #824 (ModifyStairs), #1210 (SolveStair), #1558 (SolveStairBaseline crash), #1561 (stair read-back). The DevKit sample Element_Test creates stairs and could serve as a reference. Happy to test a build on Archicad 29 JPN.
